items.title: Trigger Designer
items.text:
Trigger Designer is a desktop workbench for building data pipelines as a graph of nodes. You read a file, clean and shape it, test it, and write the result, all on a canvas. You configure each step in a panel beside the canvas, and the app shows you the data as you go.

You do not write code to use it. You drag nodes, connect their sockets, and fill in the settings. Workflows are saved as portable .tds files you can share with a colleague or run unattended from the command line.

items.title: Who it is for
items.text:
• Auditors and analysts who need repeatable checks over ledgers, journals and transaction lists.
  • Anyone who receives a messy spreadsheet or export and needs a clean, documented result without writing a script.
  • Reviewers who must show what was run, on which file, with which settings.

Everything runs on your own computer. Every Run leaves a record you can verify.

items.title: The shape of every pipeline
items.text:
Most workflows follow the same four steps:

Input  ->  Prepare  ->  Test  ->  Output
read       clean,       audit     write the
the file   shape        checks    result
  1. Input. File Input reads CSV, text, Excel, Parquet, JSON, SQLite or DuckDB.
  2. Prepare. Preparation nodes fix types, trim text, filter rows, calculate columns, sort, aggregate and reshape.
  3. Test. Audit nodes find duplicates, gaps, Benford outliers and risky entries, and draw repeatable samples.
  4. Output. File Output writes CSV, Parquet, Excel, JSON or NDJSON. Workpaper Output builds a formatted Excel workpaper.

Join and Transform nodes sit between these steps when you need to combine tables or change their shape.

items.title: Start here
items.text:
• Build your first workflow

    Read a CSV, tidy it and find duplicate orders in about ten minutes.

  • The canvas and nodes

    The screen, the sockets, undo, and how a workflow is wired together.

  • Node reference

    Every node in the palette, with its settings, an example and its messages.

  • Running workflows

    What the 100-row preview shows, and what a Run does, step by step.

  • Errors and problems

    Read a message, look up a TD- code, fix the workflow.

  • Run history and the audit trail

    Show what ran, verify the record, compare two runs.

  • Workpapers

    Produce the formatted Excel workpaper and tie it to the run record.

  • Command line

    Run a saved workflow unattended and read the exit code.

items.title: Two habits that save trouble
items.text:
Preview is a sample. While you edit, every node works on the first 100 rows. Counts, totals and audit results in the preview describe that sample. Press Run before you quote a number or hand over a file.

Click away after typing. A setting is saved as you type, but the node recalculates when you select another node or click the canvas. The yellow mark on a node means a change is waiting to run.

items.title: Signal — Trigger Designer Design System
items.text: Source of truth for the application UI. Visual reference: docs/assets/design_system_preview.html in the source tree (not part of the published site). Config Dock contract: §§1–7 (the sections AGENTS.md points at). Reference implementations: the Data Preview strip (qt/widgets/data_preview_panel.py) and the Select tool (qt/widgets/nodes/Preparation/select.py:134-259). Status: Signal 1.0 is the target contract. The Preview strip is the reference implementation; tokens and states marked target below are not in base.qss yet. The migration order is in §19.

items.title: 0.1 Principles
items.text:
1. Dense over spacious. One row does the work of three. A panel earns its air; a control does not.
  2. Live over Apply. Evaluate on change. Debounce heavy text work (§6); never add an Apply button to avoid wiring a signal.
  3. Icons over text. Every repeated action is an icon-only IconButton. Text survives only in dialogs and the paired All / None toggles.
  4. One chrome strip. Identity left, search flexible, counts before actions. No second toolbar, no footer repeating the strip.
  5. Semantic tokens over hex. A widget asks for surface.raised or text.tertiary; it never owns a colour.
  6. Borders over shadows. Depth comes from four surfaces and one hairline. Shadows are reserved for floating things: menus, dialogs, canvas nodes.
  7. Accent is state. Selection, focus, checked, active tab, active path. Accent is never decoration.
  8. Status by exception. limited, failed, running, pinned — a badge or a dot appears only when the normal state does not apply.

items.title: 0.2 Color
items.text: The palette is intentionally narrow. Surfaces carry hierarchy; type carries emphasis; status carries meaning.

items.title: Surfaces
items.text:
Token Dark Light Use bg.canvas #0E1115 #F3F5F7 Node canvas behind the grid bg.base #14171B #FFFFFF Window, dock body, editor body, table background bg.raised #191E22 #F7F8FA Chrome strips, toolbars, tab bars, palette, status bar bg.overlay #1E242A #FFFFFF Menus, popups, dialogs bg.inset #101418 #F1F3F5 Fields, chips, code panes, log panes, checkboxes bg.hover #22282E #EDF0F3 Hover fill for buttons and rows bg.pressed #2C333A #E1E6EB Pressed fill

Rule: bg.hover must be a visible step from the surface it sits on. The old button_hover (#1A1F23) was within 1–2 RGB points of button_bg (#191E21), so hover was invisible. Do not reintroduce that pair.

items.title: Text
items.text: Token Dark Light Use text.primary #F5F7F9 #10151A Titles, active values, selected rows text.secondary #C6CDD5 #39434D Body, labels, chips text.tertiary #919BA6 #68737F Meta, counts, placeholders, table headers text.disabled #5C6672 #9AA5B1 Disabled controls only

items.text: Token Dark Light Use accent #5680C2 #2F6FB5 Selection, focus border, checked pin, active tab accent.hover #6A96D7 #3D82CE Hover on accent-filled controls accent.pressed #3A76BA #245A96 Pressed / active path border.subtle #242A30 #E8EBEE Chip edges, row separators, internal hairlines border.default #2F363D #D6DBE0 Field, panel and toolbar edges border.strong #3E4750 #BCC5CD Menus, dialogs, table outer edge

items.title: Status
items.text: Token Dark Light Use success #48A878 #2E8B5F Executed node, paid state, success badge warning #D9A441 #A9751A Limited preview, refund, non-fatal warning danger #E0686C #C1484D Failed node, validation error, destructive action info #5BA8D6 #2A7DAE Neutral informational badge activity #9B7BD4 #7452B4 Running / executing state node.selection #FFA637 #B26700 Canvas selection ring only

items.title: Node categories
items.text:
Token Dark Light node.input #C4574F #B84E47 node.prepare #3F9E63 #34875A node.join #4F7FD1 #3F6FBF node.transform #7C5CBF #7452B4 node.report #C99A3C #A87C22

Node colour identifies the category, never the state. State lives in the ring and the status dot (§13).

items.title: Current theme keys → Signal tokens
items.text:
base.qss is a str.format template. Every {token} must exist in every built-in theme, or startup raises. During migration, keep the existing keys as aliases.

Signal token Theme JSON key today Action bg.base background_primary keep bg.raised background_secondary keep bg.overlay menu_background keep bg.inset editor_background keep bg.hover background_hover keep, retune to #22282E bg.pressed background_pressed keep, retune to #2C333A text.primary text_primary keep text.secondary text_secondary keep text.tertiary text_inactive alias text.disabled text_disabled keep accent accent_primary keep accent.hover accent_secondary keep accent.pressed accent_tertiary keep border.subtle border_primary alias border.default card_border keep border.strong border_light alias danger error_text alias warning background_warning add a foreground token too success, info, activity, node.* — add to every theme JSON

items.title: 0.3 Typography
items.text:
Role Size / weight Line Use Display 20 / 600 24 Splash, about, empty application state Title 16 / 600 20 Dialog and window titles Heading 13 / 600 18 Dock titles, section titles Body 12 / 400 18 Default UI text, values, descriptions Label 11 / 500 16 Chips, buttons, tabs, table headers, meta Micro 10 / 600 14 Overlines, config info, dtypes, letter-spacing .06em, uppercase Mono 11 / 400 16 Logs, SQL, formulas, counts where alignment matters
  • UI face: Segoe UI Variable Text, falling back to Segoe UI. Data face: Cascadia Mono, falling back to Consolas.
  • No webfonts. No per-widget font sizes. Table headers use Micro; numeric cells use Mono with tabular figures.
  • Body text is 12px, not 13px. Header text in the old QHeaderView was 13px; the table header is now 11px Micro.

items.title: 0.4 Spacing, size and radius
items.text:
Token Value Use Space hairline 2 Inside a chip, icon/label gap Space chrome 4 Strip gaps, button groups Space strip 6 Strip horizontal padding, QHBoxLayout spacing Space panel 8 Dock/panel padding, card padding Space group 12 Gap between sections Space dialog 16 Dialog body padding Space section 24 Page/section separation Chrome strip 36 PreviewStrip and all shared chrome rows Toolbar 40 Config Dock Pattern A toolbar Control 30 QLineEdit, QPushButton, QComboBox Chip 24 Node, socket, scope and counts chips Dense row 24 Read-only preview tables Default row 28 Editable/data tables Icon 12 Dock actions; 16 maximum for a primary action Radius badge 3 Status badges Radius control 4 Buttons, fields, chips, tables Radius panel 6 Cards, menus, dialogs Radius node 10 Canvas node tiles Node scene body 120 Graphics item units; unchanged by this system Node tile 120 The visible tile at 100% zoom; palette tiles scale down from it

Density rule: 2 / 4 / 6 inside a panel; 8 / 12 only between groups. If a panel feels tight, remove a control or split the panel — do not grow the controls.

items.title: 0.5 Depth and motion
items.text:
• Four surfaces (canvas, base, raised, overlay) plus inset for controls. One 1px border marks each edge.
  • No shadows on docks, strips, panels or chips. Shadows are allowed only on floating nodes, menus and dialogs.
  • Hover is an instant fill change. Do not animate QSS colours or add fades; Qt stylesheets do not transition reliably.
  • The only timed behaviour in the UI is the 300ms debounce on text input (§6) and the 300ms preview coalescing.

items.title: 0.6 App shell
items.text:
QMainWindow
├─ Window chrome (32) — app icon, menus, window controls, drag row
├─ NodesDock (top, max height 105)
├─ ConfigDock (left, min width 300)
├─ QMdiArea / node canvas
├─ LoggingDock + DataPreviewDock (bottom, tabbed)
└─ Status bar (20)
  • The window is frameless (install_window_chrome, qt/widgets/common/window_chrome.py): the real QMenuBar, the centred document title and the caption buttons share the row that used to hold the menu bar alone. The title is centred on the window, not on the gap the menus leave: _balance_title sizes a spacer before the buttons to cancel the surplus the left group needs. Alt, mnemonics and every shortcut stay native; drag and edge resize go through startSystemMove / startSystemResize.
  • The Config Dock spans the main work area; the bottom docks span the full width.
  • The preview and logs share one bottom dock area as tabs. The Preview panel owns its own 36px strip; the dock adds no second header.
  • A tabbed dock wears the tab bar as its only chrome: its own title bar (name, float and close buttons) is hidden while it is a tab, and returns when the panel floats. Dragging a tab out of the bar pops that panel out, into a window with a normal frame (QMainWindow.DockOption.GroupedDragging, qt/helpers/dock_chrome.py). A dock with no tab bar beside it keeps its title bar, the only handle that moves it.
  • The canvas is the only surface that fills remaining space. Everything else is fixed-height chrome.
  • Window and dock titles label the surface: Node Configuration (Select), Logs, Data Preview. The document name stays in the MDI window (no .tds suffix) and in the chrome row.

items.title: 1. Layout tokens
items.text:
Token Value Notes Dock min width 300 qt/docks/node_config.py Main QVBoxLayout spacing 2, margins 5,5,5,5 transpose.py:77, cleansing.py:173 Toolbar QWidget + QHBoxLayout fixedHeight 40, margins 0,0,0,0 select.py:158-161 Control height 30 min (QLineEdit, QPushButton, QComboBox) select.py:168,175,205 Icon button 30x30, icon 12x12 (16x16 max for primary) select.py:172-180 Chrome strip 36 high; chip 24; search 26; action 30 data_preview_panel.py Window chrome 32 high; caption button 44x32, icon 12x12; app icon slot 32; edge resize zone 5 window_chrome.py Checkbox column width 50 (header.resizeSection(0, 50)) select.py:249 Scroll threshold ColumnChecklist max_height 150-220 config_widgets.py:71, cleansing.py:173 Default table row 28 (24 for dense read-only previews) polars_table_viewer.py End layout addStretch() last, never an empty HBox after stretch filter.py:104 violates this

Docks must dock_layout.addWidget(toolbar) then dock_layout.addWidget(view, 1) — stretch factor 1 on the main view. No dock.setContentsMargins(0,0,0,0) (see file_output.py:71 violation).

items.title: A. Toolbar + Table (Select, preferred for column/row lists)
items.text:
QVBoxLayout (dock_layout)
├─ QWidget toolbar [fixedH 40, QHBox margins 0]
│   ├─ QLineEdit search ("Search columns...", clear button, minH 30)
│   ├─ TextButton All / None
│   ├─ IconButton up / down
│   └─ IconButton options (menu)
└─ SelectTableView [stretch 1] via SelectFilterProxy
    ├─ CaseInsensitive over name, rename and dtype
    ├─ ExtendedSelection + SelectRows, 28px rows, no row numbers
    ├─ Interactive data columns (checkbox fixed at 50), widths kept on the content
    ├─ DtypeDelegate (single-click dropdown)
    └─ RenameDelegate (Enter/focus-out commits, Escape cancels)

Use for: Select, GroupBy, Join mappings, Unique lists. Do not use ConfigSection here — the toolbar is the section.

items.title: B. Form stack (for settings)
items.text:
QVBoxLayout [spacing 2, margins 5]
├─ ConfigSection("Title", info="one-line hint") [spacing 2, no overrides]
│   ├─ NoWheelComboBox / QLineEdit / QSpinBox
│   └─ ColumnChecklist(columns, checked)
└─ addStretch()

Use for: Filter, Sort, Split, Transpose, Formula sections, File In/Out. Reference: transpose.py:77, running_total.py:99. Never raw QComboBox (wheel-steal bug) — use NoWheelComboBox.

Pattern C — the chrome strip — is for shared docks, not a third Config Dock layout. See §8.

items.title: 3. Shared widgets (must reuse)
items.text:
Import from qt/widgets/common/__init__.py:

  • EmptyStateLabel — only empty state. Centered gray, default text "No incoming data available". Gate at top of create_layout: if incom_data is None: dock.addWidget(EmptyStateLabel()); return.
  • ConfigSection(title, info) — QGroupBox#ConfigSection + QLabel#ConfigSectionInfo (wordWrap). Never layout().setSpacing(10) / setMargins(15) — see unique.py:87 violation. Target: flatten the group-box border; the heading + hairline is the section.
  • ColumnChecklist(columns, checked, max_height) — scrollable checkboxes, changed(list) signal. Never hand-rolled QListWidget checkboxes (unique.py, join.py violations).
  • ColumnPicker(columns, checked) — 30px token field with a searchable popover checklist and All / None. Use it when a node has several column roles (Pivot, Unpivot, group selectors) instead of stacking full checklists. The popover reuses ColumnChecklist; the picker is one undo composite.
  • RuleStack — ordered cards with an optional summary header, collapse and duplicate. A collapsed card keeps the list readable; the summary states the rule in the user's terms. Use duplicate_requested only when the list item is copyable.
  • NoWheelComboBox — drops wheel events unless popup open. Use everywhere a combo sits in a scrollable dock.
  • IconButton / TextButton — see §4.

Table helpers: SelectTableModel, RowData, SelectFilterProxy, DtypeDelegate, RenameDelegate and SelectTableView in qt/widgets/select_table_widget.py — reuse the model/delegate split for any editable column list. SelectTableWidget and ComboBoxDelegate remain aliases for older imports.

Target shared primitives: Chip, StatusBadge and ToolbarStrip belong in config_widgets.py, not in a node. Do not fork them per dock.

items.title: 4. Icon-first buttons (mandatory)
items.text: Rule: icon-only QPushButton() + setIcon + setToolTip + setAccessibleName. No setText except dialogs (§4.3).

items.title: 4.1 Sizes
items.text:
btn = QPushButton()
btn.setIcon(QIcon(rsm.get("icon_add")))  # never QIcon.fromTheme on Windows
btn.setIconSize(QSize(12, 12))
btn.setFixedSize(QSize(30, 30))
btn.setToolTip("Add mapping")  # mandatory
btn.setAccessibleName("Add mapping")  # mandatory, screen reader
btn.setObjectName("IconButton")

Use IconButton.themed(...) when the icon comes from ResourceManager, with a :/qss_icons fallback. QIcon.fromTheme is last resort and is blank on Windows.

items.title: 4.2 Action → icon map
items.text:
Action resources.json id Fallback :/qss_icons/dark/rc/ Move up / down icon_move_up / icon_move_down — ADD arrow_up.png / arrow_down.png Add / Remove icon_add / icon_remove — EXISTS — Options menu icon_options — EXISTS (sliders) arrow_down.png Check all / Uncheck all icon_check_all / icon_uncheck_all — ADD — Apply / Evaluate / Run icon_apply — EXISTS media-playback-start theme equivalent Load / Save file icon_folder_open / icon_save — EXISTS — Refresh icon_refresh — EXISTS — Clear filter icon_clear — ADD — Export CSV / Excel icon_export — ADD (one icon, menu picks format) — Open in window icon_external — EXISTS — Pin / Unpin icon_pin / icon_unpin — EXISTS — Search icon_search — EXISTS —

Until ids are added, use QIcon(":/qss_icons/dark/rc/<name>.png") directly — never fromTheme.

items.title: 4.3 Exceptions (text allowed)
items.text:
• QDialogButtonBox / QMessageBox: Save / Cancel / Close text stays (settings_panel.py:79, about.py:164).
  • Destructive confirmations keep text.
  • Paired bulk toggles use TextButton with the labels All / None. Two near-identical checkbox glyphs cannot be told apart at a glance, so these keep their words. Used in Preparation/cleansing.py and Preparation/unique.py. TextButton is H30, objectName="TextButton", and inherits the same hover/pressed treatment as IconButton (§4.5).
  • Nothing else. These stay icons: join.py bulk L/R actions (folded into the Options menu), Evaluate, groupby.py Add/Remove/Apply, formula.py add/remove, file_input.py/file_output.py browse, graph.py open-in-window.

items.title: 4.4 Bulk toggles
items.text: No All / None icon rows. Either fold them into the toolbar Options QMenu (Join's four L/R actions) or use the All / None TextButton pair when the action pair is genuinely ambiguous.

items.title: 4.5 Hover / pressed states are mandatory
items.text:
Qt gives an objectName selector (QPushButton#IconButton) higher specificity than a pseudo-state (QPushButton:hover). Any widget that sets its own background-color/border via objectName must restate :hover, :pressed and :disabled, or hover silently does nothing.

  • Base QPushButton / QToolButton use a constant 1px solid {button_bg} border so recolouring the border on hover does not shift the button by a pixel.
  • Hover fill is {background_hover} (a real contrast step). Do not use {button_hover} for hover: in the shipped themes it is within 1–2 RGB points of {button_bg}, so the state is invisible.
  • Restated for #IconButton, #OptionsButton, #TextButton, #PreviewPinButton.
  • A button that carries its own glyph and has a QMenu must suppress the menu indicator, otherwise Qt stacks a second down arrow next to the icon:
QPushButton#OptionsButton::menu-indicator {{
  width: 0px; height: 0px; border: none; image: none;
  subcontrol-origin: padding; subcontrol-position: center; }}

Do not achieve this with inline setStyleSheet, and do not use setLayoutDirection(Qt.RightToLeft) as a substitute — it moves the glyph instead of removing the arrow.

items.title: 5. Empty / loading / error
items.text:
• No data: EmptyStateLabel() only. Delete custom variants (count_records.py:61 italic label, file_input.py _hide_all_options). The label is one quiet line; if a hint is needed, a second 10px line is allowed, nothing else.
  • Join/Append need both inputs: if left is None or right is None: EmptyState (fix join.py and-logic, Append.py:74 inverted gate).
  • Never connect signals outside the if data is not None branch (fix filter.py:104 crash).
  • Node errors surface via grNode.setToolTip(...), not red inline labels (fix sort.py:94).
  • Loading: use EmptyStateLabel("Loading...") as the placeholder. Do not invent spinners or skeleton cards until they are specified.
  • Error: a failed preview or workflow uses one sentence plus the underlying message, in text.secondary; the failure colour appears in the badge or node ring, not across the panel.

items.title: 6. Interaction: live-by-default
items.text:
Every setData / move / check / sort → data_processed → handleDataChanged → process_data_changes + apply_changes + evaluate.emit, as in select.py:255, groupby equivalent.

  • Debounce: 300ms for text search / rename edits; immediate for check/move/combo.
  • Heavy nodes (Join, GroupBy) still live — debounce, don't add Apply buttons. groupby.py:278 Apply and join.py:197 Evaluate are migration targets, not patterns.
  • Formula sections and the Filter expression editor are the SQL-text exception. Text updates the model and diagnostics live, but node evaluation waits until focus leaves the node's SQL editors, the user Runs, or selection/save/close needs the current text. Do not add Apply buttons for that path.
  • History: store diff only (old != new), verb format "Noun Verbed" e.g. "Column Selection/Rename/Type Changed".
  • Dock preservation: ConfigDock.updateConfig (node_config.py:30) skips wipe when id(content) == _current_key, suspends _suspend_input_tracking/_suspend_node_evaluation during create_layout. Do not rebuild widgets on every keystroke.

items.title: 7. QSS / theming
items.text:
• Zero inline setStyleSheet in node files and shared dock chrome. Use objectName + resources/qt/themes/base.qss / qss/_style.scss.
  • Required Config Dock objectNames: ConfigSection, ConfigSectionInfo, EmptyStateLabel, ColumnChecklist, ColumnPicker, ColumnPickerPopup, ColumnToken, ConfigSummary, RuleSummary, RuleNumber, DayToggle, SuffixEdit, IconButton, OptionsButton, TextButton, DataTypeCombo, JoinSourceLeft/JoinSourceRight, JoinSourceHeaderLeft/Right, JoinDtypeLabel.
  • Dock chrome objectNames: PreviewStrip, PreviewNodeChip, PreviewNodeLabel, PreviewPinDot, PreviewSocketChip, PreviewSocketCombo, PreviewSearchEdit, PreviewScopeCombo, PreviewCountsChip, PreviewStatusLabel, PreviewLimitedBadge, PreviewSourceBadge, PreviewPinButton, DockTabOnlyTitleBar.
  • The dock-chrome boundary is explicit: §§1–7 govern node config docks; shared dock chrome follows §7 and the new §§8–14. Both use objectName + base.qss/_style.scss, restate hover/pressed per objectName, and use no inline QSS.
  • base.qss is a str.format template: only keys present in the theme JSONs may be used. The full key set is grouped in qt/theme_manager.py (TOKEN_GROUPS): Surfaces, Text, Accent, Status, Borders, Controls, Canvas, Code, Nodes. tests/unit/test_theme_tokens.py asserts every {token} exists in every built-in theme (they all define the same key set) and that every colour token is exposed in the editor — run it after editing any theme file.
  • Same rule in _style.scss, using the $COLOR_* names from _variable.scss: $COLOR_BACKGROUND_1..6, $COLOR_TEXT_1..4, $COLOR_DISABLED, $COLOR_ACCENT_1..4, $SIZE_BORDER_RADIUS, $BORDER_1..3.
  • Never hand-edit generated QSS in one place only; keep base.qss and _style.scss in agreement. The generated runtime_theme.qss is gone: ThemeManager renders base.qss from the active theme at runtime, so there is nothing to regenerate by hand.
  • Target hooks to add: ChromeStrip, Chip, ChipDot, StatusBadge, CountsChip, PrimaryButton, DangerButton, DialogSurface, MenuSurface, TableHeader, TableRow. Add them to both QSS sources and to the objectName registry in §17.

items.title: Custom view delegates
items.text: Never hand a bare QStyleOptionComboBox to drawComplexControl — with no palette set, Qt falls back to the application default (light grey in Fusion) and the cell clashes with the themed surface. ComboBoxDelegate.paint in select_table_widget.py therefore paints from option.palette/option.font directly. If you add a delegate, copy the palette and font, and keep setAutoFillBackground(True) off editors that have a themed objectName.

items.title: Themes, user themes and preferences
items.text:
• qt/theme_manager.py is the only owner of QApplication.setStyleSheet(); every other surface listens to ThemeManager.themeChanged (TriggerWindow.apply_appearance, LoggingDock.apply_theme, SQLFormulaEditor.apply_theme, NodeBase.apply_theme). Never call setStyleSheet on the application or a window directly.
  • Theme files are schema 2 — a flat token dictionary is still read, but new files use:
{"schema": 2, "id": "dark", "name": "Dark", "appearance": "dark", "extends": null,
 "tokens": {"background_primary": "#14171b"}}

extends inherits a parent's tokens; a token missing from a user theme falls back to built-in dark with a warning. appearance (dark/light) drives System mode and the title-bar contrast, not the tokens. - Built-ins live in src/trigger_designer/resources/qt/themes/ (twelve ship: Dark, Light, and the Nord, Dracula, Monokai, Gruvbox Dark, Gruvbox Light, Tokyo Night, Catppuccin Mocha, Catppuccin Latte, Solarized Light and Rose Pine Dawn palettes; every one carries the full token set, and a new built-in is just another JSON file there — discovery is a glob). User themes live in %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\themes (env override TRIGGER_DESIGNER_DATA_DIR) and shadow a built-in with the same id. duplicate_theme is the supported way to fork a built-in; a shadowing theme must not extends the id it shadows (that resolves to itself and is reported as circular). - Everything the editor exposes is a colour token. Geometry, spacing, control heights and radius are design-system-owned (§§1, 4.1) and intentionally not themeable. - Preferences are one INI at %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\preferences.ini (qt/preferences.py); the first run migrates the legacy QSettings scopes (Blue Octa/Trigger Designer, Trigger/Trigger Designer, Trigger/NodeEditor). Do not add new QSettings scopes. - The canvas rendering settings live in the same INI under editor/render_detail_* and are applied by qt/render_settings.py: one threshold (render_detail_threshold, a percentage of full size) plus a mode per element (render_detail_card, _sockets, _label, _indicator), each always, auto or never. The scene owns the policy (QDMGraphicsScene.set_detail_policy) and resolves it into one on/off map per element; the status indicator is painted by this application, so it is registered as the badge element. - Layout is one auto-saved record (qt/layout_state.py): saveGeometry() plus saveState(1) over stable dock objectNames (NodesDock, ConfigDock, LoggingDock, DataPreviewDock), with Window ▸ Save Current Layout / Reset Layout. There are no layout presets and no named workspaces. - The last session's file list is captured on close but only reopened when layout/session is on; it defaults off ("layout on, files off"). - QMdiArea paints its own background brush, which no stylesheet rule reaches: TriggerWindow._theme_mdi_background() sets it from canvas_background.

items.title: 8. Chrome strip (signature component)
items.text:
The Preview strip is the only app chrome pattern. Generalise it; do not clone it with per-dock styling.

QFrame#ChromeStrip [fixedH 36, bg raised, bottom hairline]
└─ QHBoxLayout [spacing 4, margins 6,3,6,3]
    ├─ node chip       [24]  identity, optional pin dot
    ├─ socket chip     [24]  only when the host has several outputs
    ├─ search field    [26]  the only flexible element
    ├─ scope combo     [24]  search scope
    ├─ stretch
    ├─ counts chip     [24]  "1,284 rows · 12 cols", optional "limited" badge
    ├─ pin action      [30]  checkable
    ├─ refresh action  [30]
    └─ options action  [30]  QMenu, indicator suppressed

Rules:

  • The strip is 36px. Chips are 24px, fields 26px, actions 30×30 / 12px.
  • Order is fixed: identity → search → scope → counts → actions. Counts sit immediately before actions; they are not a footer.
  • Only the search field flexes. It has min-width 110, max-width 200, a leading search glyph and a clear button.
  • The strip owns no title. The dock/window title identifies the host; the strip identifies the node and data.
  • No pager footer. The whole collected frame is one page; the table scrolls.
  • Standalone hosts (Data Preview window) hide node, socket and pin. They are not disabled or replaced with placeholders; they are absent.
  • Collapse order on a narrow host: socket → scope → counts → node label. Keep identity, search and actions longest.
  • A limited badge appears only when collection stopped at the size limit. It is not a permanent status.

Target objectNames: ChromeStrip, ChromeChip, ChromeChipDot, ChromeSearch, ChromeScope, ChromeCounts, ChromeBadge, ChromeAction. Preview* names remain as aliases until migration.

items.title: Chips — identity and counts
items.text:
• 24px high, bg.base on bg.raised, 1px border.subtle, radius 4, 11px Label text, 6px dot.
  • Use for node identity, socket, search scope and counts.
  • Truncate a long node title with Qt.ElideMiddle and keep the full title in the tooltip.
  • Counts format: 1,284 rows · 12 cols. When filtered: 48 / 1,284 rows · 12 cols. When counting: 1,284 rows · counting….

items.title: Badges — status by exception
items.text:
• 18px high, radius 3, 10px Micro/600, horizontal padding 5.
  • limited → warning background (background_warning / warn_text), text primary.
  • Executed → success soft; Failed → danger soft; Pending → info soft.
  • A badge is not a chip. Do not use it for counts or identity.

items.title: 10. Fields, combos and focus
items.text:
• Field height 30px (26px inside a chrome strip), bg.inset, border.default, radius 4, 12px Body.
  • Hover: border.accent. Focus: border.accent + a 2px accent-soft ring. Never remove the ring; never use a native 3px dotted outline.
  • Placeholder is text.tertiary; disabled text is text.disabled; selection is accent with white text.
  • Always NoWheelComboBox in a scrollable dock. A raw combo steals wheel events from the panel.
  • Search fields: leading search glyph, clear button, debounce 300ms. Enter does not submit; the field is the truth.
  • Checkboxes stay native in size and painting; theme via QCheckBox::indicator, not a custom widget.

items.title: 11. Tables
items.text:
Property Default Dense preview Row height 28 24 Header 11px Micro, uppercase, text.tertiary, bg.base same Grid horizontal hairline only horizontal hairline only Selection accent at 18% + text.primary same Hover row bg.hover same Numeric cells Mono, right-aligned, tabular figures same Dtype 10px Micro after the column name same Sort indicator small chevron, accent same
  • Do not draw vertical grid lines. The row separator is enough.
  • QHeaderView::section must use the theme tokens; no default Fusion header.
  • Editable tables keep the checkbox column fixed and every data column Interactive; keep the widths on the content so a dock rebuild does not reset them, and let spare width grow the name column.
  • Delegates must paint from option.palette/option.font; never hand a bare QStyleOptionComboBox to drawComplexControl.
  • The Preview table is dense (24px); editable tables are 28px. Do not mix densities in one view.
  • Copy/export menus stay in the strip's Options menu; no table footer.

items.title: Menus
items.text:
• bg.overlay, 1px border.default, radius 6, shadow allowed.
  • Items 27–28px high, 8px horizontal padding, 4px radius, 12px Body.
  • Hover/selected: accent-soft fill + text.primary. No accent bar.
  • Separators: 1px border.subtle, 4px vertical margin.
  • Shortcut text: 10px Mono, text.tertiary; only for real shortcuts.
  • Dialog-opening items end in …; immediate commands do not.

items.title: Dialogs
items.text:
• bg.base, 1px border.strong, radius 8, shadow allowed.
  • Header 34px, Title 16/600, close icon 22×22.
  • Body padding 16px, one column, 8px gap.
  • Footer 42–48px, right-aligned buttons, 6px gap. QDialogButtonBox text stays.
  • Exactly one primary action per dialog. Destructive confirmations use DangerButton + explicit noun.
  • No custom title bar, no illustration headers, no multi-column forms unless the dialog is a dedicated manager.

items.title: Node body
items.text:
• 120×120 scene units, radius 10, category fill, white glyph.
  • Node title: 11px Label, text.secondary, centred under the tile; elide middle, full text in tooltip.
  • Palette tiles scale the same artwork to 22–32px; they are not a second icon set.

items.title: State matrix
items.text:
State Ring Status dot Notes Idle none none Category fill is the only signal Hover 1px rgba(255,255,255,.30) none Must not shift layout Selected 2px node.selection (#FFA637) optional success Selection outranks hover Running 2px activity spinner/dot optional No pulsing fill on the whole tile Executed 2px success success check, bottom edge (centred) Clears when the node is dirtied Error 2px danger danger glyph, bottom edge (centred) Tooltip carries the message; replaces the status glyph
  • State is never colour alone: the ring plus dot/glyph plus tooltip.
  • One status glyph per node. An error or warning replaces the executed/dirty glyph in the same place; never draw a second indicator in a corner.
  • The ring is drawn outside the tile and must not change the node's hit area.

items.title: Edges and grid
items.text:
• Grid: 22px minor, 110px major, rgba(255,255,255,.035) / .06 in dark; dark ink at equivalent alpha in light.
  • Edge default: #454D57 (light: #AAB4BE), 1.4px screen width, vector-effect: non-scaling-stroke.
  • Edge active/selected: accent, 1.8px. No magenta/tan defaults; those are legacy and belong to the old editor skin.
  • Edge hover: lighten one step, do not change width.
  • No animated dashes or particles by default; execution state belongs to the node ring.
  • Canvas and grid colours are tokens — canvas_background, canvas_grid_light, canvas_grid_dark — applied by apply_theme_to_scene(); state rings read node_selection / activity / success / danger through NodeBase._pen_role. Keep paint methods token-driven; a literal QColor("#...") in a paint() is a bug.
  • The workspace frame behind the sub-windows is canvas_background too (TriggerWindow._theme_mdi_background), so the graph and the frame read as one surface. Edge and socket colours are user settings, not theme tokens (qt/node_editor_colors.py).

items.title: Snapping and arrangement
items.text:
• Snapping is a preference (editor/snap_to_grid) copied onto the graphics scene by apply_theme_to_scene(), because the drag handler reads it once per mouse move. The same value is the check item under Edit › Arrange and the node context menu; hold Alt while dragging to bypass it. New nodes dropped from the palette land on the grid.
  • Arrange commands live in one table, qt/helpers/node_arrange.py: align horizontal / vertical centres, distribute horizontally / vertically, arrange in row / column / grid, snap selection. Both menus and the shortcut page read that table, so labels, minimum selections and defaults cannot drift apart.
  • Geometry rules: align shares the selection's bounding-box centre; arrange starts at its top-left with a 40-unit gap; a grid uses ceil(sqrt(n)) columns; distribute keeps the outer nodes fixed and evens the edge gaps (never negative). A command that changes nothing records no undo step.
  • Each command is one MoveNodesCommand per press - positions only, not a scene snapshot. A group whose child moved is refitted explicitly, since the vendored Group only refits from a mouse-driven positionChanged.
  • Shortcuts are per-command, edited under Preferences › Shortcuts, and stored as a JSON object under editor/shortcuts (INI holds scalars only). Missing key = default, empty string = cleared. A sequence needs Ctrl/Alt/Shift or a function key, so it cannot shadow typing in the node editors; clashes are checked against the window's live actions.
  • Known limitation: dragging a group by its header moves every child through the vendored Group.mouseMoveEvent, which does not pass through the node's snap correction.

items.title: Canvas chrome
items.text:
• Floating toolbar top-left, 30px actions, no background plate beyond their own buttons.
  • No minimap, no floating legend, no permanent help text. The status bar carries hints.

items.title: Logs
items.text:
• 11px Mono, row 22, timestamp text.tertiary, level badge 10px Micro, message text.secondary.
  • Level is the only colour: INFO info, WARN warning, ERROR danger, CRITICAL danger + bold, DEBUG tertiary.
  • No card per line. The log pane is one bg.inset surface with hairline separators.
  • Auto-scroll is a checkbox in the dock controls, not a footer button.
  • Colours come from the theme (text_*, info, warning, danger) via LoggingDock.apply_theme(); the SQL editor's syntax colours are the Code token group (syntax_*, editor_line_number_*, editor_current_line). No hardcoded log or syntax colours.

items.title: Diagnostic feed
items.text:
The Logs dock is one list of records, not a tab per kind. A record is a log line or a node problem; a problem carries the whole NodeError, so code, Fix, Caused-by and technical text stay structured.

  • Row. 22px: a 12px severity glyph, HH:MM:SS in text.tertiary, then the node name as a link (accent.secondary) with its numeric id in text.tertiary for a problem, or the message directly for a log line. The message is text.secondary, elided right, never wrapped.
  • Glyph. Shape carries the kind so colour is never the only signal (§15): circle-with-bang error, triangle warning, ring info, square debug, dot below that.
  • Expansion. A problem row expands in place (double-click, Space, or the chevron) to code Fix: …, then Caused by: …, then the first technical line when the toggle is on. Detail text is 11px Mono in text.tertiary, 16px per line.
  • Strip. 40px, background.secondary. Counted chips are the filter and the count: All, N Errors, N Conv, N Warnings, N Messages, then the icon actions and the Last Run / Configuration segmented control. A zero count uses text.inactive through [zero="true"]; the selected chip is accent.primary. Chips are 30px tall, so the hit area meets §15.
  • Colour owner. The delegate resolves every colour from the active theme and re-reads it in apply_theme(). No setForeground, no inline style=.
  • Empty state. One EmptyStateLabel, wording per filter: "No messages yet", "No problems", "The last run reported nothing", "Nothing matches this filter".

items.title: Status bar
items.text:
• 20px high, bg.raised, top hairline, 10px Label, text.tertiary.
  • Left: file path or current action. Right: Ready, encoding, column count. Truncate the path, never the state.

items.title: 15. Accessibility
items.text:
• Minimum interactive target: 30×30. A 24px chip is not a button; do not make it clickable without a 30px hit area.
  • Every icon-only control has a tooltip and setAccessibleName. The two strings match.
  • Focus is always visible: 1px accent + 2px soft ring. No outline: none without a replacement.
  • Status is not colour-only: pair the colour with a word, glyph or dot.
  • Contrast: text.secondary on bg.base ≥ 4.5:1; text.tertiary is for meta only, never body copy; disabled text is exempt.
  • Keyboard: Ctrl+F focuses preview search, Ctrl+R refreshes, Esc closes overlays, Tab reaches every control in visual order.
  • No motion that cannot be disabled. QSS transitions are not used; debounce is not a visual animation.

items.title: 16. Content and copy
items.text:
• Sentence case for labels, menu items and tooltips. Title Case for window and dialog titles.
  • Menu items that open a dialog end in …; immediate commands do not.
  • Counts: 1,284 rows · 12 cols; use a thin middot and thousands separators.
  • History: "Noun Verbed" — Column Selection Changed, Node Label Changed, Dtype Changed.
  • Empty: one sentence plus, at most, one hint line. No exclamation marks, no jokes.
  • Tooltips: sentence case, no trailing period, describe the action not the icon (Refresh preview, not Refresh).
  • Errors: what failed, on what, and the next action. Keep the raw exception out of the badge; put it in the tooltip or log.
  • Numbers in tables: right-aligned, tabular, consistent decimals.

items.title: Tokens
items.text:
1. Add the token to every built-in theme JSON in resources/qt/themes/ — dark.json, light.json and each palette theme (schema 2, under tokens) — and to the matching TOKEN_GROUPS group in qt/theme_manager.py so the editor exposes it.
  2. Add the matching $COLOR_* values to qss/_variable.scss and the selectors to qss/_style.scss.
  3. Add the same selectors to resources/qt/themes/base.qss; write {{ / }} for QSS blocks, {token} for values.
  4. Run tests/unit/test_theme_tokens.py — it collects every {token} in base.qss and fails if any built-in theme (or the editor's group list) is missing one.

items.title: Python-painted surfaces
items.text:
qt/theme_manager.py is the single accessor: ThemeManager.color(token) returns a QColor, token() the raw value, both cached per theme. ResourceManager.get_theme_color delegates to it, so older call sites keep working.

Route these through it:

  • node category fills and state rings (node_base.py)
  • table row parity (polars_table_viewer.py)
  • canvas grid and background (apply_theme_to_scene)
  • log levels and the SQL editor's syntax colours (apply_theme)
  • the workspace frame (TriggerWindow._theme_mdi_background)
  • the caption glyphs and app icon in the window chrome (window_chrome.py)

Missing tokens fall back to the built-in dark value, and a user theme that omits one gets it filled with a warning. No widget should call QColor("#...") in a paint() method. Edge and socket colours are a user setting, not a token (qt/node_editor_colors.py).

items.title: Shared widget constants
items.text:
qt/widgets/common/config_widgets.py owns:

STRIP_H = 36
TOOLBAR_H = 40
CONTROL_H = 30
CHIP_H = 24
ROW_H = 28
DENSE_ROW_H = 24
ICON_SIZE = 16

IconButton, TextButton, Chip and StatusBadge use these constants. Do not repeat the numbers in node files.

qt/widgets/common/window_chrome.py owns the window row: CHROME_H = 32, CAPTION_BUTTON_W = 44, RESIZE_MARGIN = 5. Pure Qt on purpose: the 5px zone replaces the native border (no 1px hover assist), the frameless window gets no DWM shadow or rounded corners, and Win11's Snap Layouts flyout does not open from the maximize button. Those need Win32 calls and stay out until asked for.

items.title: ObjectName registry
items.text: objectName Owner States to restate IconButton shared hover, pressed, disabled, checked OptionsButton shared hover, pressed, disabled, menu-indicator TextButton shared hover, pressed, disabled ConfigSection shared — ConfigSectionInfo shared — ColumnChecklist shared — EmptyStateLabel shared — WindowChrome main window — WindowChromeIcon, WindowChromeTitle main window — WindowChromeButton main window hover, pressed, [danger="true"] tone PreviewStrip → ChromeStrip Preview / shared chrome — PreviewNodeChip → ChromeChip Preview / shared chrome — PreviewSearchEdit → ChromeSearch Preview / shared chrome hover, focus, disabled PreviewScopeCombo → ChromeScope Preview / shared chrome hover, focus, disabled PreviewCountsChip → ChromeCounts Preview / shared chrome — PreviewLimitedBadge → ChromeBadge Preview / shared chrome — PreviewSourceBadge → ChromeBadge Preview / shared chrome [source="run"] tone PreviewPinButton Preview hover, pressed, disabled, checked PrimaryButton dialogs hover, pressed, disabled DangerButton dialogs hover, pressed, disabled MenuSurface menus — DialogSurface dialogs — PreferencesDialog, ThemeEditorDialog preferences / theme editor — PreferencesSidebar, PreferencesPages, PreferencesPage preferences item hover, selected ThemeList, ThemePreview preferences item hover, selected ThemeEditorScroll, ThemeEditorContent theme editor — RenderDetailLabelCombo, RenderDetailIndicatorCombo preferences hover, focus, disabled ColorHexEdit, ColorSwatch, ThemeTokenRow, ContrastLabel theme editor hover, focus FieldLabel, FieldHint, hover, selected FormulaCompleterPopup SQL editor hover, selected

items.title: Guards
items.text:
Tests that fail fast, all under tests/ (the shared fixtures live in tests/conftest.py and keep the preference store in a temp dir):

  • Theme parity: parse base.qss, collect every {token}, assert it exists in both theme JSONs, and assert every colour token is exposed by TOKEN_GROUPS (test_theme_tokens.py).
  • Theme manager: schema 2, extends, missing-token fallback, invalid colours, accent variants, preview/commit/cancel, save/import/export/delete (test_theme_manager.py).
  • Preferences: defaults, typed coercion, legacy migration, reset (test_preferences.py).
  • Layout: geometry and dock-state round trip, session gating and filtering, off-screen guard (test_layout_state.py).

Target guards still to add:

  • No inline QSS: no setStyleSheet in qt/widgets/nodes/** or the shared dock chrome.
  • Accessible actions: every QPushButton with an empty text() has a non-empty toolTip() and accessibleName().
  • No fromTheme in nodes: a grep test for QIcon.fromTheme outside the documented fallback helper.

items.title: References
items.text:
• Preview strip: qt/widgets/data_preview_panel.py
  • Window chrome: qt/widgets/common/window_chrome.py
  • Preview dock host: qt/docks/data_preview.py
  • Config dock host: qt/docks/node_config.py
  • Shared widgets: qt/widgets/common/config_widgets.py
  • Table: qt/models/polars_table_viewer.py, qt/widgets/select_table_widget.py
  • Canvas: qt/node_base.py, qt/node_editor_colors.py
  • Theme: resources/qt/themes/ (base.qss plus one JSON per built-in theme), qss/_variable.scss, qss/_style.scss
  • Theme engine: qt/theme_manager.py, theme editor qt/dialogs/theme_editor_dialog.py, swatches qt/widgets/common/theme_widgets.py
  • Preferences: qt/preferences.py, dialog qt/dialogs/preferences_dialog.py, host window qt/main_window.py
  • Layout and session: qt/layout_state.py, qt/helpers/preview_dock_state.py (legacy migration only)
  • Visual preview: docs/assets/design_system_preview.html in the source tree

items.title: 18. Anti-patterns (do not copy)
items.text:
1. Inline QSS per button (groupby.py:219, select.py:191).
  2. QIcon.fromTheme on Windows — invisible icons.
  3. Text All/None rows (join.py:162, cleansing.py:198) unless they are the paired TextButton exception.
  4. Custom spacing 10/15 on sections (unique.py:87, split.py:92).
  5. Raw QComboBox in docks, raw QListWidget checkboxes.
  6. Signals connected when data is None (filter.py).
  7. dock.setContentsMargins(0,0,0,0) wiping dock padding (file_output.py:71).
  8. Stub nodes with no create_layout (union.py, find_replace.py) — add EmptyStateLabel gate at minimum.
  9. A second toolbar or a footer that repeats the strip.
  10. Accent used as decoration or category colour.
  11. Status communicated by colour alone, or a whole dock repainted for one error.
  12. Shadows on panels, strips, chips or table cells.
  13. 44px controls or 16px gaps inside a dock.
  14. Per-node forks of Chip, StatusBadge, IconButton or ConfigSection.

items.title: Phase 1 — tokens and guards
items.text:
• Add Signal keys to every built-in theme JSON (schema 2; TOKEN_GROUPS in qt/theme_manager.py is the authoritative list).
  • Route Python-painted colours through ThemeManager.color() — qt/style_tokens.py turned out to be unnecessary, the manager is the accessor.
  • Add theme-parity, inline-QSS, accessible-action and fromTheme tests.

items.title: Phase 2 — QSS foundation
items.text:
• Add surface, text, accent, status and node tokens to base.qss and _style.scss.
  • Add ChromeStrip, Chip, StatusBadge, PrimaryButton, DangerButton hooks.
  • Restate hover/pressed/disabled per objectName; keep a constant 1px base border.
  • Verify the light theme, not just dark.

items.title: Phase 3 — shared chrome
items.text:
• Move the Preview strip to the shared ChromeStrip composition; keep Preview* aliases.
  • Apply the strip rhythm to the Logs dock and Config Dock header.
  • Align the status bar and tab bars to 20 / 24px.
  • Update the standalone Preview window to hide node, socket and pin.

items.title: Phase 4 — Config Dock
items.text:
• Flatten ConfigSection: heading + hairline, 4px gaps, no group-box border.
  • Normalise toolbars to 40px, controls to 30px, icons to 12px.
  • Replace hand-rolled checklists with ColumnChecklist; use TextButton only for All/None.
  • Gate every dock on EmptyStateLabel; remove custom empty variants.
  • Align tables to 28px rows and the 11px header.

items.title: Phase 5 — canvas
items.text:
• Move node category colours to node.* tokens.
  • Add 2px state rings and status dots; selected ring uses node.selection.
  • Replace tan/magenta edge defaults with neutral + accent.
  • Set the 22 / 110px grid and canvas surface.
  • Keep the 120-unit node body; do not shrink the scene without a separate decision.

items.title: Phase 6 — polish and proof
items.text:
• Menus and dialogs: 6/8px radius, 27px items, one primary action.
  • Add a light-theme screenshot for each surface.
  • Delete ad-hoc colours and spacing that now have tokens.
  • Re-run the Select, Join, GroupBy, Filter, Preview and Logs smoke tests.

items.title: Config Dock backlog (from the original contract)
items.text:
• IconButton exists in widgets/common/config_widgets.py and is exported.
  • Add the missing icon ids (move up/down, check all/uncheck all, clear, export) to qt/resources.json.
  • select.py: drop "Options" text → icon_options, swap fromTheme go-up/go-down → bundled arrows.
  • join.py: icon-ify All/None→Options menu, Evaluate→apply icon, QListWidget→ColumnChecklist, fix empty gate to or.
  • groupby.py: kill blue-pill QSS, Add/Remove/Apply→icons, bold labels→ConfigSectionInfo.
  • formula.py: + Add formula→icon, remove→icon_remove, adopt NoWheelComboBox.
  • filter/sort/split/unique/cleansing: adopt Pattern B tokens, NoWheelComboBox, fix filter.py signal crash, unique.py spacing.
  • file_input/output: Load/Save→icons, remove setContentsMargins(0), add EmptyStateLabel path.
  • graph.py, count_records.py, union.py, find_replace.py: add empty gates + sections.
  • Move all inline QSS to base.qss + _style.scss.

items.title: 20. References
items.text:
• Select dock: src/trigger_designer/qt/widgets/nodes/Preparation/select.py:134-280
  • Table model/delegate: src/trigger_designer/qt/widgets/select_table_widget.py:36-771
  • Dock host: src/trigger_designer/qt/docks/node_config.py:10-129
  • Shared widgets: src/trigger_designer/qt/widgets/common/config_widgets.py:1-139
  • Preview panel: src/trigger_designer/qt/widgets/data_preview_panel.py
