items.title: The Config Dock, Data Preview, Logs and Problems
items.text:
Around the canvas there are three panels. The Node Configuration dock (the Config Dock) is where you set up a node. The bottom panels (Data Preview, Logs and Run History) share one tab bar and show what the workflow is doing and what it produced.

Back to the guide index
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: On this page
items.text:
• Show, hide and arrange the panels
  • Config Dock
  • Data Preview
  • Logs
  • Problems
  • If something goes wrong

Run History has its own page: Run history and audit trail.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: Show, hide and arrange the panels
items.text:
All panels are in the Window menu.

Menu entry Panel Where it opens Node Configuration Config Dock Left of the canvas Show Logger Logs Bottom Data Preview (Ctrl+Shift+D) Data Preview Bottom, in the same tab bar as Logs Problems Problems Bottom, in the same tab bar Run History Run History Bottom, in the same tab bar Nodes Toolbar The node palette Top

You can drag a panel's tab out of the tab bar to float it, or drag a panel to another edge. The app remembers the layout when you close it (switch this off in Edit > Settings > Layout). Window > Save Current Layout stores the arrangement now; Window > Reset Layout puts everything back where it started.

Every panel follows the workflow window that is in front. If you have two workflows open, switching tabs switches what the panels show. Each workflow has its own logs, problems and preview.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: Config Dock
items.text:
The Config Dock shows the settings of the one selected node. Its title names the node: "Node Configuration (Duplicates)". With nothing selected, or with several nodes selected, it is empty.

From top to bottom:

  1. Label - an optional note shown above the node on the canvas (see Labels and groups).
  2. The node's own sections, for example Match on, Match type and Result for Duplicates. Each node is described on its page in the node reference.

Hover the title area of the dock for a one-line summary of how the node is set up.

How edits behave:

  • Live. A change is stored in the workflow immediately. You do not press OK or Apply.
  • Typing is debounced. Text boxes wait a short moment (about 300 ms) after you stop typing before the edit is recorded.
  • One undo step per change. The Edit menu says what Undo will reverse. See Undo and redo.
  • The node recomputes when you leave it. Until then the node shows the amber "!" (changes not run yet). Select another node or click the empty canvas to let it recompute on the live sample.
  • Buttons are icons. Hover one to read its tooltip. Text buttons appear only in dialogs and for the paired All / None column toggles.
  • Lists of columns show a check box per column, with All and None at the top.

The dock does not run the whole workflow. It recomputes the node on the live sample (the first 100 rows of each input). See Running workflows.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: Data Preview
items.text: Open it with Window > Data Preview (Ctrl+Shift+D). It shows the output of the node you have selected, in a table.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: The strip at the top
items.text:
Control What it does Node chip The name of the node on display. Socket chip Appears only when the node has several outputs (for example Duplicates D, U, S). Choose which output to show. Search box ("Search this preview...") Filters the rows you can see as you type (Ctrl+F jumps to it). The scope list next to it limits the search to one column; the default is all columns. Source badge from Run means the table is the output of the last Run. evaluated - not run means it was computed by live evaluation on the first 100 rows of each input. Hover the badge to read this. Counts chip For example 1,000 / 48,213 rows - 17 cols: rows shown, rows collected, total rows in the source. "counting..." means the total is still being worked out. A limited tag means the preview stopped at its size cap. Pin Freezes the panel on the current node so that selecting other nodes no longer moves it. Pin a node, then click around while you compare. Refresh (Ctrl+R) Collects the table again. Options (three dots) Copy as TSV, Export CSV..., Export Excel..., Open in standalone window, Unpin.

If the pinned node is deleted, the panel says "Pinned node is no longer in the scene" and unpins itself.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: What you see
items.text:
Situation What the preview shows The workflow has been Run, and you have not edited the node since The result of the Run (badge: from Run). You edited the node, or have not yet Run The live sample: at most 100 rows per input (badge: evaluated - not run). The node has no table output, or has a problem "No previewable data on this socket", or the table of a different socket. The node has no rows "No rows". Nothing selected "Select a node to preview its output".

An edit after a Run makes the preview go back to the live sample for that node, because the Run's table no longer matches the settings.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: How much is shown
items.text: The preview collects at most 1,000 rows or about 2 MB, whichever is smaller. That is a window onto the result, not the whole result. The counts chip tells you if more rows exist in the source.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: Exporting from the preview
items.text:
Export CSV... and Export Excel... write the rows currently collected in the preview (and, if you have typed in the search box, only the rows that match). They do not re-run the node or write the complete output. To save a full result, use a File Output node and Run.

  • Export CSV... asks for a file name (default dataframe_export.csv).
  • Export Excel... asks for a file name (default dataframe_export.xlsx).
  • Copy as TSV copies the table to the clipboard so you can paste it into Excel.

The menu items' tooltips say this too. When the export is partial (the preview was cut at the size limit, the source has more rows than the preview, or the search hides some rows), a dialog titled Export complete tells you how many rows were written, for example "Exported 1,000 of 2,500 rows", and reminds you that the full output is written by a File Output node when you Run. When the export covers every row of the source, no dialog is shown.

If a file cannot be written, a dialog titled Export failed appears ("The CSV file could not be written" or "The Excel file could not be written"), followed by the reason, for example that the file is open in Excel. Close the file and try again.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: Standalone window
items.text: Choose Options > Open in standalone window, or alt-click an output socket on the canvas (after a Run), to open the table in a separate resizable window. It has the same search and export controls and does not follow your selection.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: Logs
items.text:
The tab named Logs is the app's running commentary and its problem list for the active workflow: loading the file, evaluating, each Run, and every node that currently has an error or warning.

One row is one record. A log line shows its time, a level glyph and its message. A problem row shows the node, the message and a chevron, and clicking it selects that node on the canvas and centres it.

The strip above the list is both the filter and the count:

Chip Shows All Everything, in the order it happened. N Errors Errors, excluding type-conversion failures. N Conv Type-conversion failures (TD-TYP-...). N Warnings Warnings, including the knock-on ones a failed input raises. N Messages Plain log lines.

Ctrl+F opens the search field. It matches a message, a code, a node name or a problem's detail, and settles 300 ms after you stop typing.

Control Meaning Last Run / Configuration Show the problems the last Run reported, or the ones the current workflow state reports. Log lines appear in both modes. Copy details (icon) Copies the selected problems, or every problem the filter shows when nothing is selected, with the Fix lines. Show technical details (icon, toggle) Adds the raw engine message and stack trace to the expanded rows and to the copied text. Your choice is remembered. Clear (icon) Empties log lines only. A live problem is not yours to delete: it leaves when its node goes clean. Follow new entries (icon, toggle) Keeps the newest record in view.

Expand a problem row with a double-click or Space to see its code, the Fix: line, Other fix: alternatives, Caused by: when the real problem is in an earlier node, and the technical text when that toggle is on.

The dock keeps the last 1,000 log lines per workflow. Problems are never trimmed away by that cap, and a fixed problem disappears the moment its node recomputes cleanly.

After a Run, the Logs hold a summary: whether it completed, failed or was cancelled, how long it took, and the line "Run log saved: ..." with the path of the run record (see Run history). If a Run fails you also get "Run finished with N problem(s).", and the list switches to Last Run with the Errors chip selected.

A technical log file for the whole session is also written to disk. It is meant for support: when the app is installed from the packaged build it is in %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\logs, otherwise in a logs folder next to the source.

More on reading and fixing errors is in Errors and problems.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Symptom What to do The Data Preview is empty Select a node. If it still says "No previewable data", the node has an error (check Problems) or only a summary output; choose another socket in the socket chip. The preview shows 100 rows only That is the live sample. Run the workflow to see the Run's result (up to 1,000 rows). The preview and my output file differ in row count The preview is capped at 1,000 rows or 2 MB. Open the output file, or look at the counts chip for the true total. Export Excel fails Close the target file in Excel, or pick another name. If the message mentions that Excel export is not available, use Export CSV instead and tell your administrator. Logs are too noisy Raise Level to INFO or WARNING. A panel has vanished Window > ... and tick it again, or Window > Reset Layout. The Config Dock layout looks stale after loading a very old file Click another node and then the first one again.
path: Config Dock, preview, logs and problems

items.title: Errors and problems
items.text:
When something is wrong, the app tells you which node, what is wrong, and what to try. Every message carries a stable code such as TD-SCH-001 so that you, a colleague and a support person all mean the same thing. This page explains where messages appear, how to read them, and lists every code.

Back to the guide index

items.title: On this page
items.text:
• Where you see an error
  • How to read a message
  • Row numbers, values and "did you mean"
  • Errors caused by an earlier node
  • Technical details and copying details
  • Privacy: hiding data values in messages
  • A fixing routine that works
  • Error code reference

items.title: Where you see an error
items.text:
Where What you see The node A red ring and a red round "!" badge on its bottom edge (amber for a warning). Hover the node to read a short message. The Logs dock One row per node with a problem, mixed into the log stream: node, one-sentence description, and an expandable code plus Fix: line. Click a row to jump to the node. See Logs. The log file The error is written once, when it first appears, with its full technical text. The run record A failed node's error is stored in the run record (see Run history). A dialog Only for things outside a node: a file that cannot be opened, an Excel export that failed, a workflow with unknown nodes.

Errors come in two kinds. A live error appears while you edit (it is about the sample of 100 rows). A run error appears when you press Run (it is about all the data). A node can have both. A live error disappears as soon as you fix the setting and the node recomputes. A run error disappears when you start the next Run, or when you change the node or its connections.

items.title: How to read a message
items.text:
Example: a real error from the Logs dock (copied with Copy details)

[TD-TYP-001] Select 'Amounts': Column 'Amount' has values that cannot be read as whole numbers.
Fix: Clean or correct the value in the source data.
Other fixes: Add a Select node before this one and set 'Amount' to a whole number; values that cannot be converted become empty instead of stopping the run.
Columns: Amount
Rows/values: 'abc'
Phase: run   Severity: error   Time: 2026-10-30T16:59:07+00:00
Line Meaning [TD-TYP-001] The code. The letters say the family (TYP = data types, SCH = columns, IN = input files, OUT = output files, SHAPE = node settings, RUN = running, AUDIT = audit nodes). Look it up in the reference below. Select 'Amounts': ... The node (its title, then its label in quotes if it has one) and what is wrong, in one sentence. Fix: The first thing to try. Other fixes: Alternatives. Columns: The columns involved. Rows/values: An example of the offending data, when the app can find it. Phase: run (you pressed Run) or live (editing). Severity: error stops the node; warning does not.

Warnings (amber badge) are not errors

A warning means the node produced a result but something deserves attention, for example "Only 12 rows were tested; at least 50 are needed for a reliable result" from an Audit node. The node still passes data downstream.

items.title: Row numbers, values and "did you mean"
items.text:
The app does a little detective work for you.

Row and value location. When a column cannot be converted (to a number, a date and so on, codes TD-TYP-001, TD-TYP-003 and TD-TYP-005), the app runs a second, bounded search to find the first offending row and a few bad values, and rewrites the message:

Column 'Amount' contains 'abc' in row 3, which cannot be read as whole numbers.

Things to know about row numbers:

  • Row 1 is the first data row of the table going into the failing node, after any earlier nodes have filtered or sorted it. It is not the line number in the CSV file or the row number you see in Excel (which would also count the header).
  • The search looks at no more than a set number of rows (default 5,000,000). In a bigger table, the first bad value might be beyond the limit and the message stays general.
  • Both the search and its limit are in Edit > Settings > General > Error messages (see Preferences).

Did you mean. If a column, a sheet or a function name is not found, the app compares the name with the real ones and suggests the closest, ignoring case, spaces, hyphens and underscores:

[TD-SCH-001] Duplicates: Column 'Order_Id' was not found. Fix: Use the column 'Order_ID' instead.

items.title: Errors caused by an earlier node
items.text:
Often the node that fails is only where the problem shows. A Select node may complain about a column, when the real cause is a File Input that read the column as text. The app tries to find the real cause:

  • The real culprit is shown with its own error, and the nodes after it show "Stopped because 'X' has a problem" or "Skipped because 'X' failed" (codes TD-RUN-003, TD-RUN-008). These are knock-on errors: fix the first node and they clear by themselves.
  • In the Logs dock a line Caused by: names the culprit node.

When you see several errors, start with the one that is furthest upstream (closest to the File Input).

items.title: Technical details and copying details
items.text:
Messages are written for people, but the engine's own words are kept for support.

  • In the Logs dock, click the Show technical details icon button in the toolbar (hover to see its tooltip). An expanded problem row then also shows the engine's exception text and, for run errors, the stack trace. The toggle is remembered between sessions (preference errors/show_technical, off by default).
  • Click Copy details to put the selected problems (or all of them, when none is selected) on the clipboard. If technical details are on, they are included. Paste this into an email or ticket.

items.title: Privacy: hiding data values in messages
items.text:
By default a message can include a few of the offending values ("contains 'abc'"). That is useful, but values from a ledger can be sensitive. Tick Edit > Settings > General > Error messages > "Hide data values in error messages" (preference errors/redact_values, off by default) and:

  • messages keep the code, the column and the row number but leave the values out (the row line says "values hidden by privacy setting"),
  • the engine text and stack trace have the offending values scrubbed,
  • the error stored in the run record is redacted the same way.

The setting is read when an error is created, so it affects errors raised after you switch it on; recompute the node or Run again to refresh one that is already on screen. It removes values from messages; it does not change what is in your data or your output files. See Security and privacy.

items.title: A fixing routine that works
items.text:
Follow these steps in order

  1. Open Logs and pick the Errors chip. Start with the topmost, most upstream node.
  2. Read the Fix: line and apply it.
  3. Click away from the node (to let it recompute) and check that the red mark is gone.
  4. If the same column keeps failing, look at the data type: text columns that hold numbers are the usual cause. See Troubleshooting.
  5. Still stuck? Show technical details, Copy details, and send the text with the workflow file to support.

items.title: Error code reference
items.text:
Codes are stable: a code is never reused for something else. Placeholders in braces, such as {column}, are filled in with the real name when the message is shown. A few codes are marked flagged reserved in the catalogue; they are defined but the catalogue marks them as not yet raised in that form.

The table is generated from the code. To regenerate it after the catalogue changes, run from the repository root:

.venv\Scripts\python.exe scripts/gen_error_reference.py

Add --check to see whether the page is out of date without changing it.

117 codes. Generated from core/errors/catalogue.py and core/shaping/common.py; do not edit by hand.

items.title: Reading input files (TD-IN)
items.text:
File Input, folders, databases.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-IN-001 The file '{path_name}' was not found. 1. Check that the file exists and that the drive or network share is reachable.2. Choose the file again with Browse in the File Input node. TD-IN-002 '{path_name}' cannot be read: it is open in another program or access is denied. 1. Close the file in Excel or any other program, then run again.2. Ask for read permission on the folder. TD-IN-003 Sheet '{sheet}' does not exist in '{path_name}'. 1. Pick one of the available sheets in the node settings.2. Use the sheet '{suggestion}' instead. TD-IN-004 '{path_name}' is not UTF-8 text. Open the file in Excel or Notepad and save it again as 'CSV UTF-8'. TD-IN-005 '{path_name}' is empty. Check that the export that produced the file finished, then reload it. TD-IN-006 '{path_name}' is not a readable Excel workbook. 1. Open it in Excel and save it again as .xlsx.2. If it is really a text file, rename it to .csv and choose File type CSV. TD-IN-007 Some rows have more fields than the header. 1. Check the delimiter in the node settings.2. Make sure values containing the delimiter are wrapped in quotes. TD-IN-010 I could not read the data in this file Check the file type and delimiter; the details name the column. TD-IN-011 The input file could not be opened Check the path and your access rights. TD-IN-012 The folder matches too many files Narrow the include pattern or raise "Max files". TD-IN-013 The database could not be read as requested Check the table name and use a single SELECT statement; databases are read-only. TD-IN-014 The File Input settings need attention Open File Input and fix the highlighted setting.

items.title: Columns and schemas (TD-SCH)
items.text:
A column is missing, renamed or differs between files.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-SCH-001 Column '{column}' was not found. 1. Use the column '{suggestion}' instead.2. Select the column again in this node; it may have been renamed, dropped or typed differently upstream. TD-SCH-002 The column name '{column}' appears more than once. Rename one of the columns with a Select node before this step. TD-SCH-003 The columns in '{path_name}' changed since the workflow was saved. (warning, flagged reserved in the catalogue) Review the nodes that use the changed columns. TD-SCH-004 The two tables have different columns or types. Make both inputs have the same columns and types (use Select nodes), or use a mode that fills missing columns. TD-SCH-005 Columns have different numbers of rows. Check the upstream step that builds these columns from separate lists. TD-SCH-010 An added column name already exists in the data Rename the filename/sheet column in File Input. TD-SCH-011 Files in the folder have different columns Use "Union by name" or fix the odd file named in the details.

items.title: Data types and conversion (TD-TYP)
items.text:
A value could not be read as a number, date or other type.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-TYP-001 Column '{column}' has values that cannot be read as {target_human}. 1. Clean or correct the value{row_hint} in the source data.2. Add a Select node before this one and set '{column}' to {target_one}; values that cannot be converted become empty instead of stopping the run.3. In the formula, use TRY_CAST([{column}] AS {target_sql}) so bad values become empty. TD-TYP-002 Join keys have different types: '{left_key}' is {left_type} but '{right_key}' is {right_type}. 1. Add a Select node on one side and set the key column to the same type (usually Text).2. Check that both columns really contain the same kind of value. TD-TYP-003 Column '{column}' is text, so it cannot be {op_past}. 1. Clean or correct the value{row_hint}.2. Add a Select node before this one and set '{column}' to Decimal. TD-TYP-004 Text and numbers cannot be compared. Set the column to a number type with a Select node, or put the value in quotes if the column is text. TD-TYP-005 A value in '{column}' does not fit in the target type ({target}). Use a wider type (for example Int64 or Decimal) in a Select node. TD-TYP-006 This step needs a {expected} column but '{column}' is {got}. Check which column this node uses and its type in the Select node. TD-TYP-007 The filter condition must give true or false, not {got}. Write a comparison such as [Amount] > 0.

items.title: Joins (TD-JOI)
items.text:
Join and union problems.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-JOI-001 No columns are mapped. (flagged reserved in the catalogue) Map at least one column in the node settings. TD-JOI-002 Both inputs must be connected. (flagged reserved in the catalogue) Connect a node to each input.

items.title: Node settings and data shaping (TD-SHAPE)
items.text:
Select, Formula, Filter, SQL Query, Pivot, Reconcile, Fuzzy Match and the other shaping nodes.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-SHAPE-001 A required setting is missing Fill in the missing setting. TD-SHAPE-002 An output column name is empty, duplicated or already exists Choose a unique name. TD-SHAPE-003 A selected column is not in the input any more Select the column again. TD-SHAPE-004 A setting value is out of range or unknown Pick a value from the list or inside the range. TD-SHAPE-005 A required input has no data Connect and fix the upstream node. TD-SHAPE-040 The pattern is not a valid regular expression Escape special characters with a backslash. TD-SHAPE-041 The pattern is too long Shorten the pattern. TD-SHAPE-042 Find text is empty Type the text to find. TD-SHAPE-043 Too many rules Remove rules or split them over two nodes. TD-SHAPE-044 The column must be text Convert the column to text with a Select node. TD-SHAPE-050 The column is not a date and not text Choose a date or text column. TD-SHAPE-052 A holiday is not a YYYY-MM-DD date Type holidays as year-month-day. TD-SHAPE-053 Working days must name at least one weekday Tick at least one weekday. TD-SHAPE-060 Index, header and value columns must be different Pick three different columns. TD-SHAPE-061 Too many new columns Filter the header column to fewer distinct values. TD-SHAPE-070 Amount or date column is set on one side only Pick it on both sides, or on neither. TD-SHAPE-071 Add a key column pair or a date column Add a key pair or a date window. TD-SHAPE-072 Too many possible matches Add key column pairs or narrow the date window. TD-SHAPE-081 Too many possible fuzzy pairs Use a longer prefix or add a 'Must also match' column. TD-SHAPE-082 Too many rows to compare without blocking Turn on prefix or first-word blocking. TD-SHAPE-091 The column must be a number Pick a numeric column, or a text column that holds numbers. TD-SHAPE-101 The split pattern can match nothing Use a pattern that needs at least one character, such as \s+ not \s*. TD-SHAPE-110 Only one statement is allowed Remove everything after the first statement. TD-SHAPE-111 Only SELECT queries are allowed Write a SELECT query; changing data or settings is not allowed. TD-SHAPE-112 The SQL uses a function or file access that is not allowed Remove file-reading, system or random functions. TD-SHAPE-113 The SQL could not be parsed or run Check the SQL syntax. TD-SHAPE-114 The SQL is too long Shorten the SQL. TD-SHAPE-115 The query took too long Simplify the query or filter the data first. TD-SHAPE-120 The formula must use the column placeholder Write {col} where the column goes, for example UPPER({col}). TD-SHAPE-130 The generated rows do not match the input rows Set Start, Increment and End so the number of generated values equals the number of input rows, or remove the input.

items.title: Writing output files (TD-OUT)
items.text:
File Output and workpaper export.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-OUT-001 The output folder does not exist. Create the folder, or choose an existing one in the File Output node. TD-OUT-002 '{path_name}' cannot be written: it is open in another program or read-only. 1. Close the file in Excel or any other program, then run again.2. Choose a different file name or clear the read-only flag. TD-OUT-003 Excel export is not available in this installation. 1. Export as CSV or Parquet instead.2. Reinstall the application. TD-OUT-004 '{path_name}' is not a valid output file name. 1. Remove characters such as < > : " | ? * and keep the path short.2. Choose a file, not a folder. TD-OUT-005 The disk is full. Free some space or write to another drive. TD-OUT-006 Nothing is connected to this output. Connect the node whose result you want to save to the File Output node. TD-OUT-010 A workpaper with this name already exists Choose another file name, or set "If the file exists" to New version. TD-OUT-011 The table has too many columns for Excel Excel allows at most 16,384 columns; select fewer columns before writing. TD-OUT-012 The workpaper settings are not valid Check the output file (it must end in .xlsx) and the Prepared on date (YYYY-MM-DD). TD-OUT-013 The table is too large for an Excel sheet An Excel sheet holds at most 1,048,575 data rows; save it as CSV or Parquet instead. TD-OUT-014 Excel could not create the workbook A sheet name or cell content is not valid for Excel; rename the sheet or shorten the text. TD-OUT-015 Excel output must use the .xlsx extension Change the output file name to end in .xlsx (the writer cannot create the old .xls format).

items.title: Running a workflow (TD-RUN)
items.text:
Problems found while a run executes.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-RUN-001 This step took longer than {seconds} seconds and was stopped. 1. Filter or sample the data earlier in the workflow.2. Write large results to Parquet instead of CSV or Excel. TD-RUN-002 This step ran out of memory. 1. Filter rows or drop unused columns earlier in the workflow.2. Close other programs and run again. TD-RUN-003 Stopped because '{culprit_label}' has a problem. Fix '{culprit_label}' first, then run again. TD-RUN-004 The run was cancelled before this step. (warning, flagged reserved in the catalogue) Run the workflow again. TD-RUN-005 Input {input_number} is not connected. (warning) Connect a node to this input. TD-RUN-006 This step needs the result of an earlier step that is not available. 1. Fix the earlier step ('{culprit_label}') and run again.2. Open the earlier step so it is calculated, then run again. TD-RUN-008 Skipped because '{culprit_label}' failed. (warning) Fix '{culprit_label}' and run again.

items.title: Expressions and formulas (TD-EXP)
items.text:
Problems in formula or expression text.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-EXP-001 The expression has a syntax error. Check brackets, quotes and operators near the marked spot. TD-EXP-002 Unknown function '{function}'. 1. Use '{suggestion}' instead.2. Check the function name in the formula help list. TD-EXP-003 The expression cannot be evaluated. Check the column names and types used in the expression. TD-EXP-004 The pattern (regular expression) is not valid. Escape special characters such as ( ) [ ] with a backslash. TD-EXP-005 A function received a value it cannot use. Check the arguments of the function, or use TRY_CAST for conversions.

items.title: System and resources (TD-SYS)
items.text:
Memory, time and environment.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-SYS-001 {message} Check this node's settings. TD-SYS-100 The data engine could not run this step. Check the node settings and the upstream data; copy the details if you need help. TD-SYS-998 The data engine stopped unexpectedly. Run again; if it repeats, copy the details and report it. TD-SYS-999 Something unexpected went wrong. Copy the details and report it if it repeats.

items.title: Audit nodes (TD-AUDIT)
items.text:
Benford, Duplicates, Gaps, Sample and the risk filters.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-AUDIT-001 Choose the {label} column. Pick the column in the node settings. TD-AUDIT-002 Column '{col}' is not in the input data. Pick the column again; it may have been renamed upstream. TD-AUDIT-003 Column '{col}' holds nested values and cannot be used for this test. Choose a plain text, number or date column. TD-AUDIT-004 {label} must be {rule}. Enter a value inside the allowed range. TD-AUDIT-005 The input already has a column named '{name}', which this node adds. Rename the existing column first. TD-AUDIT-006 '{text}' is not a date. Use YYYY-MM-DD. Type the date as year-month-day. TD-AUDIT-007 Date format '{fmt}' is not supported. Choose one of the formats in the list. TD-AUDIT-008 Switch on at least one risk test. Tick at least one test in the node settings. TD-AUDIT-009 {label}: {detail}. Fix the list of numbers (count and order). TD-AUDIT-010 No row has a readable amount in '{col}', so a value-based sample cannot be drawn. Choose a numeric amount column or clean the values. TD-AUDIT-101 Only {n} rows were tested; at least {min} are needed for a reliable result. (warning) Treat the result as indicative only. TD-AUDIT-102 {n} values could not be read as {kind} and were skipped. (warning) Clean those values or convert the column with a Select node. TD-AUDIT-103 Requested {k} but only {n} rows exist; the whole population was selected. (warning) Lower the sample size.

items.title: Command line (TD-CLI)
items.text:
Raised by the command-line runner; see cli.md.

Code What it says How to fix it TD-CLI-001 The workflow file could not be read. Check the path and that it is a .tds file. TD-CLI-002 The workflow was saved by a newer Trigger Designer. Update this program. TD-CLI-003 The workflow uses an unknown node type. Open and re-save it in a compatible version. TD-CLI-004 The workflow has a cycle. Remove the connection that loops back. TD-CLI-005 Unknown or missing parameter. Use one of the listed parameter names. TD-CLI-006 A parameter value is not valid. Use the example format shown. TD-CLI-007 This parameter target is not supported. Choose a supported setting. TD-CLI-008 The workflow has not been approved to run unattended. Approve it first (approve). TD-CLI-009 The approved workflow changed since approval. Approve it again. TD-CLI-010 The generated code was refused by the safety policy. Remove the flagged node or setting. TD-CLI-011 A custom-code node was refused. Remove the custom-code node. TD-CLI-012 Another run of this workflow is in progress. Wait and try again. TD-CLI-013 The outputs could not be saved. Close the output files in other programs and run again. TD-CLI-014 The output folder is missing or not writable. Create it or use --create-output-dirs. TD-CLI-015 There is not enough free disk space. Free space or lower --min-free-mb. TD-CLI-016 The scheduler could not be configured. Check Windows Task Scheduler permissions. TD-CLI-017 The run log failed verification. Treat the log as modified. TD-CLI-018 This workflow writes no files. (warning) Add a File Output node.

items.title: Files and formats
items.text:
This page covers the workflow file (.tds), the data files the app can read and write, and how the app remembers recent files and your last session.

Back to the guide index

items.title: On this page
items.text:
• The workflow file (.tds)
  • What is inside a .tds

  • Saving
  • Opening files from other versions

items.title: The workflow file (.tds)
items.text:
A workflow is saved as a .tds file ("Trigger Designer Scene"). It holds the nodes, their settings, the connections, the labels and groups, and where the nodes sit on the canvas. It does not hold your data.

A .tds is plain text in the JSON format, written in UTF-8. You can open it in any text editor to see what it contains, but you should edit workflows in the app. Because it is text, it works well with version control, and you can send it by email.

To open one: File > Open (Ctrl+O, the file filter says "Design (*.tds)"; you can select several files), File > Open Recent, the welcome dialog, or start the program with the file as its argument (trigger-designer "C:\Work\Orders\orders_check.tds").

Opening a workflow that is already open just brings its tab forward.

items.title: What is inside a .tds
items.text:
Top level:

Key Meaning id An internal number for the canvas. scene_width, scene_height Size of the canvas area. nodes A list of nodes (below). edges The connections: start and end are socket ids, plus the edge style and input_index. groups The coloured group boxes: title, position, size, whether collapsed, the ids of the nodes inside, and colours. comments Canvas comments. workflow_metadata Facts about the file itself (below).

Each node has:

Key Meaning id, title Its id and displayed title. op The stable operation name, such as input.file_input or audit.duplicates. This is how the app knows which node it is, and it does not change when nodes are added to the app. node_code, node_type The older numeric identification, kept for compatibility. op wins when both are present. pos_x, pos_y Position on the canvas. inputs, outputs The sockets (index, whether several edges are allowed, a type). content The node's settings. What it contains depends on the node; for File Input it is the file path, type, delimiter and so on. label_text, label_visible, label_offset The floating label.

workflow_metadata:

Key Meaning schema_version The version of the file layout. This guide describes version 2. app_version The program version that saved the file (currently 0.1.0). saved_at When it was saved, in UTC. workflow_uuid An identity for this workflow. It is created the first time you save, stays the same across saves and when you rename the file, and changes if you use File > New. The run record stores it, so records can be tied back to a workflow even after a rename.

Keys that a newer version of the app added to workflow_metadata are carried through a load and save, not dropped.

items.title: How file paths are stored
items.text:
Paths are stored, not embedded

A workflow records where your data lives, not the data itself. Keep the .tds and its data folder together and a copied project still opens; move the .tds on its own and the app falls back to the absolute path recorded at save time.

File Input stores each source path twice:

Key Content filePath The absolute path, such as C:\Work\Orders\data\orders.csv. filePathRel The path relative to the workflow file, using forward slashes, such as ../data/orders.csv. It is stored only when the data is not more than six folders up from the workflow, and not on a different drive.

When a workflow opens, the app uses the relative path first, if the file exists there, and falls back to the absolute path. So a project folder (workflow plus its data) can be zipped, copied to another drive, or sent to a colleague, and still opens correctly as long as the relative layout is kept. If you move only the .tds, the relative path no longer points at the data, and the absolute path is used instead, which is why the original data still loads when you move a workflow on the same computer.

Relative paths are written when you save. A workflow that has never been saved has no folder to be relative to.

The File Output node stores a path in its settings as you type it. Use a full path (or a path you checked) to be sure where the file goes.

items.title: Saving
items.text:
• File > Save (Ctrl+S) saves to the current file. File > Save As... (Ctrl+Shift+S) asks for a new name. A new, never-saved workflow asks for a name the first time.
  • The title shows an asterisk while the workflow has unsaved changes. Closing it asks whether to Save, Discard or Cancel.
  • Saving first picks up any text you were typing and any pending edit.
  • Saves are atomic. The app writes the new content to a temporary file in the same folder (named like .tds-xxxx.tmp), forces it to disk, and only then replaces your file. If something goes wrong halfway (a full disk, a crash, a power cut), your previous workflow is still there untouched. Stray .tds-*.tmp files can be deleted.
  • Files are written as UTF-8.

Saving a workflow is independent of running it. A Run does not save the workflow; the run record states whether the workflow had unsaved changes (workflow_modified_since_save).

items.title: Opening files from other versions
items.text:
Situation What happens Same version Opens normally. A progress dialog ("Please wait") shows "Reading...", "Validating workflow..." and "Evaluating workflow..." for larger files. Saved by an older version (file layout version 1, or a file without workflow_metadata) Opens. Old numeric node codes are converted to the stable op names, older File Input settings are brought up to date, and edges that point at sockets that no longer exist are removed with a line in the Logs ("Removed invalid edge during workflow load"). The next save writes the current layout. Saved by a newer version (schema_version higher than this program's) Opens, and a Workflow Validation Warnings dialog says: "This workflow was saved by a newer version of the app (file format N, this app understands 2). Some settings may be ignored; saving will overwrite them." Do not save it from this version unless you accept losing what this version does not understand. Use Save As to keep the original. Contains a node this version does not have The node loads as a placeholder titled Unknown, its settings are kept in the file, and the dialog lists "Unknown node type 'x' ... Its settings were kept; install the providing node or replace it." The rest of the workflow works. A node's saved settings look wrong Each node can check its own loaded state; problems are listed in the same warnings dialog (and in the Logs), by node. Contains a loop Opens, the loop is reported, and the workflow cannot Run until you break the loop. Not valid JSON A dialog titled "Error loading " says the file is not a valid JSON file. Text in the legacy local code page is also accepted: the app tries UTF-8 first, then your computer's code page, and logs that it did so. File not found A dialog "Error loading ".

If a file is partially damaged, the app loads what it can and logs the problem rather than refusing the whole file. Always glance at the Logs after opening a workflow that came from outside.

To see which version wrote a file, open it in a text editor and look at workflow_metadata near the end.

Opening a workflow you did not write: see Security and privacy.

items.title: Input file types
items.text:
Set the type in the File Input node (the Type list). The app guesses it from the file's extension when you choose a file.

Type Extensions Notes CSV .csv, .tsv Delimiter and header row are settings. Everything is first read as text; you set number and date types with a Select node (see Troubleshooting). Text .txt Read like CSV with the delimiter you choose. Excel .xlsx, .xlsm, .xls One sheet, several sheets or all sheets; start row. Excel files are read in full. Parquet .parquet, .pq Keeps column types. Fast and compact. JSON .json An array of records. Nested values can be kept as text. JSON Lines .ndjson, .jsonl One record per line. SQLite .sqlite, .sqlite3, .db Read-only: a table, or one SELECT query. DuckDB .duckdb, .ddb, .db Read-only, same as above. A .db file is recognised as SQLite or DuckDB by its first bytes.

The Source can also be a folder or a pattern such as D:\data\*.csv: all matching files are read and combined, with controls for include and exclude patterns, subfolders, order, what to do when files have different columns, and what to do when one file cannot be read. By default at most 10,000 files are read from one source.

Encoding: UTF-8, or UTF-8 (replace bad bytes) for files that are not valid UTF-8, such as many Latin-1 exports.

Databases are always opened read-only.

Each File Input node has its own page in the node reference.

items.title: Output file types
items.text:
Set the format in the File Output node (the Format list). The app suggests the format from the file name's extension.

Format Typical extension Notes CSV .csv Optional byte-order mark for Excel; delimiter. Excel .xlsx The whole table is written; limits of Excel apply (1,048,575 data rows and 16,384 columns per sheet). Parquet .parquet Written without loading everything into memory. JSON .json An array of records; loaded fully before writing. NDJSON .ndjson One record per line. Arrow IPC .ipc, .arrow A fast binary format for other tools. Custom delimited any Your own delimiter.

Workpaper export (a formatted Excel workpaper with an index and a header block) is described in workpaper.md.

An output file is written when you Run, never while you edit. Writing replaces an existing file of the same name without asking, so give each output its own name. If the file is open in Excel, the write fails with a message that says so (TD-OUT-002).

items.title: Recent files and session restore
items.text:
• File > Open Recent lists the files you opened or saved most recently, newest first, numbered &1 to &9 for keyboard selection. It holds 10 by default (Edit > Settings > General > Recent files, from 1 to 50) and ends with Clear Recent Files.
  • If you pick a file that is gone, a dialog "Recent file not found" says so and removes it from the list.
  • The welcome dialog at startup lists the recent files with New Project, Browse... and Open. Untick Show this dialog on startup to stop it (also in Edit > Settings > General).
  • Layout. The app remembers window size, position and the arrangement of the panels, and restores them at startup (Edit > Settings > Layout > Restore window and dock layout on startup, on by default).
  • Session restore. The list of workflows that were open when you closed the app is always saved, but it is reopened at startup only if you tick Reopen files from the last session (Layout page, off by default). It does not happen when you start the program with a file name on the command line.

items.title: Other files the app creates
items.text:
What Where Preferences (preferences.ini) and your own themes %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\ The run script of the last Run %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\last_run\check_output.py Run records <workflow name>.runs\ next to each workflow (see Run history) Session log files %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\logs\ for the installed app; a logs folder beside the source when run from source

The environment variable TRIGGER_DESIGNER_DATA_DIR moves the %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer folder, for portable installations. Edit > Settings > General > Open Preferences Folder opens it.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Symptom What to do "Error loading ..." dialog The file is missing or is not a .tds. Open it in a text editor: a workflow starts with { and contains "nodes". A node says the file was not found after moving a workflow See Troubleshooting. The Logs say "File ... is not UTF-8; decoded as ..." The workflow was saved by an old tool in your local code page. Save it again from this version and it becomes UTF-8. "Workflow Validation Warnings" lists unknown node types Use a program version that has those nodes, or replace the placeholders. Stray .tds-xxxx.tmp file next to the workflow A save was interrupted. Your workflow is intact; delete the temp file. Save appears to do nothing The title still shows the asterisk. Check that the folder is writable and the disk is not full, then use Save As to another location. Details are in the Logs.

items.title: Limits and performance
items.text:
How big can your data be, how long can a step take, and what can you do to keep a big workflow quick? This page gives the numbers the app really enforces, explains the difference between nodes that stream data and nodes that hold it in memory, and ends with advice for big files.

Back to the guide index

items.title: On this page
items.text:
• The short answer
  • Limits the app enforces
  • Lazy and eager nodes
  • Live editing versus Run
  • What the run record adds
  • Advice for big files
  • If something goes wrong

items.title: The short answer
items.text: There is no fixed limit on rows or file size. The practical limit is your computer's memory (RAM), and it applies at the steps that must hold a whole table at once. A few explicit caps stop a step with a clear message, and every step has a 30-second timer. The preview and the live editing view only ever show a small part of the data, whatever the file size.

items.title: Limits the app enforces
items.text:
What Limit What happens Where it is explained Rows read while you edit (live evaluation) 100 rows per input; at most 100 rows shown per output Only a sample is processed while editing; Run processes everything. Running workflows Data Preview after a Run 1,000 rows or 2 MB, whichever is smaller A window onto the result. Exports from the preview write only these rows. Data Preview Time per step in a Run 30 seconds (Workpaper Output: 10 minutes) The step stops with TD-RUN-001; the Run stops. Time and memory limits SQL Query run time 25 seconds Interrupted with TD-SHAPE-115. Security and privacy SQL text length 20,000 characters TD-SHAPE-114. same SQL Query memory 2 GB TD-SHAPE-113 with the engine's message. same Memory in general None enforced If the computer runs out, the step fails with TD-RUN-002. Files from one folder or pattern 10,000 by default (setting Max files in File Input) TD-IN-012 "The folder matches too many files". Files and formats Reconcile 5,000,000 candidate pairs TD-SHAPE-072 (checked at Run). node page Fuzzy Match 5,000,000 candidate pairs; and without blocking, 1,000,000 row pairs TD-SHAPE-081, TD-SHAPE-082, checked before any scoring. node page Pivot 500 distinct header values TD-SHAPE-061. node page Charts 2,000 distinct groups or points The chart says it was truncated. node page Excel output 1,048,575 data rows and 16,384 columns per sheet TD-OUT-013, TD-OUT-011; use CSV or Parquet for more. Files and formats Logs dock The latest 1,000 messages per workflow Older ones scroll off. Undo history 200 steps per workflow The oldest steps are dropped. Undo and redo Error row search 5,000,000 rows (a preference) The message stays general when the bad row is further down. Preferences Fingerprinting an input or output file Skipped above 2,048 MB (a preference) sha256_status is skipped_size_limit. Run history

Counts you see while editing describe the sample. For example, the Count node says "First 100 rows only: full count at Run".

items.title: Lazy and eager nodes
items.text:
The app builds most work as a plan, not as a calculation. A step on a CSV does not read the file; it adds a line to a plan. Data is only read, in pieces, when something at the end of the plan (such as a File Output) asks for the result. Such nodes are lazy, and they can handle files much bigger than your memory.

Some nodes need the whole table in memory to do their job. Those are eager. They still work on big data, but their size is bounded by RAM.

Group Nodes and inputs Behaviour Streams (no memory ceiling for the data itself) Reading CSV, Parquet and JSON Lines. Writing CSV, Parquet, JSON Lines and Arrow IPC. Column-based nodes such as Select. Data flows through in pieces. Holds the result in memory Filter and Formula (SQL result), Cleansing, Reconcile, Fuzzy Match, Pivot, SQL Query, Transpose (the sort step may need the whole table) The step's output has to fit in RAM. Reads the whole file Excel, JSON (an array of records), SQLite and DuckDB inputs Read in full, even while editing. Collects before writing Excel and JSON (array) outputs The whole table is gathered first.

Row order: after joins, groups and unpivots the order of rows is not guaranteed unless the node sorts. Add a Sort node when the order matters.

items.title: Live editing versus Run
items.text:
Editing is quick because it works on 100 rows. Run is the real work, on all of them. A workflow that feels instant while you build it may take minutes to Run on millions of rows, and a step that is fine on the sample may hit a limit on the full data. Two rules of thumb:

  • After you finish building, Run it once and look at the Logs and the run's duration before you rely on it.
  • Open Logs after a Run, not only while editing: some errors (a value that cannot be converted, 500+ pivot columns, too many fuzzy pairs) appear only on the full data.

items.title: What the run record adds
items.text:
The run record costs a little time:

  • Fingerprinting reads each input and output file once to compute its SHA-256 (a repeat Run on an unchanged file reuses the earlier hash). Turn it off, or lower the size limit, in the Audit trail preferences if you work with very large files.
  • Row counting in "All nodes" mode computes each node's result once and keeps it in memory so every node can have an exact row count. That is why Auto switches to Sinks only when the combined input is over 256 MB: there, only the input files and the written output files are counted and nothing is held. If you have a big input and plenty of memory, you may set All nodes; if a Run runs out of memory on a big input, set Sinks only or Off.

items.title: Advice for big files
items.text:
1. Prefer Parquet or CSV for large outputs. They are written as a stream. Excel and JSON arrays are collected first and Excel cannot hold more than about a million rows per sheet.
  2. Convert Excel inputs once. An Excel file is read in full every time the workflow opens. For a very large workbook, save the sheet as CSV or Parquet and read that.
  3. Filter and select early. Put a Select (drop the columns you do not need) and a Filter or Select Records as close to the input as you can. Fewer rows and columns make every later step quicker and smaller.
  4. Keep an eye on text columns. CSV columns are read as text. Converting only the columns you need, once, is cheaper than converting everything.
  5. Split a heavy step. If one step is near its time limit (30 seconds) on your data, put a Filter before it, or split the work in two workflows, writing the first stage to Parquet.
  6. Sample for audit tests. For a first look, a Sample node (with a seed) over the population lets you try tests quickly. Run the tests over the whole population when you are happy.
  7. Close what you do not need. Each open workflow keeps its own previews and logs. Close finished ones.
  8. Avoid joining on text keys with different cases or spaces. Clean them first (Cleansing or Normalize), or a join can multiply or lose rows.
  9. Check the Logs for timing. Every Run logs how long it took and the average of this session.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Symptom What to do "This step took longer than 30 seconds and was stopped" Apply advice 3 and 5. A very large write to CSV may also hit it: write Parquet, or filter first. "This step ran out of memory" Filter rows and drop columns earlier; use Sinks only or Off for Row counts; close other programs; avoid Excel/JSON for the big step. The workflow is slow to open Excel, JSON and database inputs are read in full on open. Convert them, or reduce Row limit in File Input while you build. Counts on screen are small You are looking at the 100-row sample. Run, then read the counts in the preview or the run record. The app is busy after a stopped step The step's background work cannot be forcibly ended; it finishes in the background. Wait a moment before the next Run.

items.title: Preferences
items.text:
Preferences are the settings that belong to you and your computer, not to a workflow: theme, font size, canvas behaviour, how errors are shown, and how run records are kept. They are stored in one file and apply to every workflow you open.

Back to the guide index

items.title: On this page
items.text:
• Open the Preferences window
  • How changes take effect
  • Appearance
  • Layout
  • Editor
  • Node Editor
  • Shortcuts
  • General
  • Complete list of stored preferences
  • Where preferences are stored and how to reset them

items.title: Open the Preferences window
items.text: Choose Edit > Settings. The window is titled Preferences and has six pages in a list on the left: Appearance, Layout, Editor, Node Editor, Shortcuts and General. The buttons at the bottom are Cancel, Apply and OK.

items.title: How changes take effect
items.text:
Kind of setting Behaviour Theme Previewed as you click. Apply keeps it and leaves the window open, OK keeps it and closes, Cancel goes back to the theme you had. Accent colour and font size Applied as you change them. Cancel restores the values you had when you opened the window. Everything else (check boxes, numbers, paths, colours of nodes) Saved the moment you change them. Cancel does not undo these. Shortcuts Validated when you press OK; if one is invalid the window stays open and says why.

The values are read each time they are needed: error settings take effect on the next error, audit settings on the next Run.

items.title: Appearance
items.text:
Setting Default Meaning Theme Dark The colour scheme. System - follow Windows appearance switches between a light and a dark theme with Windows. Built in: Dark, Light, Catppuccin Latte, Catppuccin Mocha, Dracula, Gruvbox Dark, Gruvbox Light, Monokai, Nord, Rose Pine Dawn, Solarized Light, Tokyo Night. Built-in themes are read-only. Customize... Makes an editable copy of the selected theme and opens the theme editor. Import... / Export... / Delete Share a theme as a .json file; delete one of your own themes. Accent Theme default The highlight colour. Choose one of seven swatches or a custom colour; Theme Default clears it. Application text (font size) System default 8 to 20 pt. Default goes back to the system size.

Stored as appearance/theme, appearance/accent (empty means the theme's own) and appearance/font_size (0 means the system size).

items.title: Layout
items.text:
Setting Default Meaning Restore window and dock layout on startup On Reopen the app with the window size, position and panel arrangement you left. (layout/restore) Reopen files from the last session Off At startup, open the workflows that were open when you closed the app. Not used if you start the app with a file name. (layout/session) Save Current Layout Store the arrangement now. Same as Window > Save Current Layout. Reset Layout Forget the saved arrangement and restore the default. Same as Window > Reset Layout.

The list of open workflows is always remembered; it is reopened only when the second check box is on.

items.title: Editor
items.text:
Setting Default Range Meaning Grid size 20 px 10 to 100 Spacing of the canvas grid and of snapping. (editor/grid_size) Show grid On Draw the grid lines. (editor/show_grid) Snap nodes to the grid while dragging On Hold Alt while dragging to move freely. Also the Snap to Grid item of Edit > Arrange. (editor/snap_to_grid) Simplify below 50 % 0 to 100 Below this zoom level the canvas may draw simpler nodes to stay fast. 0 % keeps every node fully drawn. (editor/render_detail_threshold) Node card Auto Always / Auto / Never Draw the full node card. (editor/render_detail_card) Sockets Auto Draw the sockets. (editor/render_detail_sockets) Label Always Draw the floating label. (editor/render_detail_label) Status indicator Auto Draw the badge on the node's bottom edge. (editor/render_detail_indicator)

For each of the four elements: Always draws it at every zoom, Never hides it at every zoom, Auto draws it only above the threshold. These settings change drawing only.

items.title: Node Editor
items.text:
Colours of the lines and sockets on the canvas. Click a swatch to choose a colour.

Group Item Default Edges Default #B08848 Edges Selected #ff00d0 Edges Hovered #FF37A6FF Edges Dragging #333334 Sockets Outline #FF000000 Sockets Highlight #FF37A6FF

Reset Node Colours restores these. They are stored under node_editor_colors/.

items.title: Shortcuts
items.text:
One row per Arrange command, plus Snap to Grid. Click the box and press the keys. A shortcut needs Ctrl, Alt or Shift, or must be a function key. Backspace clears one, and the circular arrow next to a row restores its default. Restore Defaults resets all of them. A shortcut that is already used elsewhere in the window is refused with a message.

Defaults: Align Horizontal Centers Ctrl+Shift+H, Align Vertical Centers Ctrl+Shift+V; the others have none. Stored as a single value editor/shortcuts holding only the ones you changed.

items.title: General section
items.text: Setting Default Meaning Show the welcome dialog on startup On The startup dialog with your recent files. (show_welcome_dialog) Recent files 10 How many files File > Open Recent keeps (1 to 50). (general/recent_limit) Clear Recent Files Forget every recent path. Open Preferences Folder Opens %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer in Explorer.

items.title: Error messages
items.text:
Setting Default Meaning Keep running independent branches after a failure On When on, a Run continues with the branches that do not depend on the failed node; nodes that do depend on it are skipped with TD-RUN-008. When off, a Run stops at the first failed node. See Running workflows. (errors/continue_past_failure) Hide data values in error messages Off Messages, copied details and stored errors show the code, column and row but not the offending values. See Errors and problems. (errors/redact_values) Find the offending row for conversion errors On Run a bounded second search to name the first bad row and a few bad values. (errors/locate_rows) Row search limit 5,000,000 How many rows that search may look at (100,000 to 100,000,000). (errors/locate_row_cap)

The Logs dock's Show technical details toggle is stored as errors/show_technical (default off) and is changed from the dock, not from this window.

items.title: Audit trail
items.text:
These control the run records.

Setting Default Meaning Record every run (run history) On Write a tamper-evident record after each Run. (audit/record_runs) Record the user and machine name On Off leaves the user and machine fields empty. (audit/record_identity) Fingerprint input files (SHA-256) On Hash each input file before it is read. (audit/hash_inputs) Fingerprint output files (SHA-256) On Hash each output file after it is written. (audit/hash_outputs) Store the generated code in each record On The code's hash is always kept; this also keeps the text. (audit/embed_code) Warn when an input changed since the previous run On One Logs line per changed input; never blocks a Run. (audit/warn_on_input_change) Run log folder empty Keep every run log in this folder instead of next to each workflow. Browse chooses it. (audit/run_log_dir) Row counts Auto Auto, All nodes, Sinks only or Off. (audit/row_counts) Count every node up to (MB) 256 The input size at which Auto changes from "All nodes" to "Sinks only". (audit/exact_counts_max_mb) Skip hashing files above (MB) 2048 Bigger files are not fingerprinted. (audit/hash_max_mb)

items.title: Engagement
items.text: Defaults used when you export a workpaper: Client, Engagement, Period, Prepared by (blank means your Windows user name) and a Logo image (PNG or JPG). They are stored as engagement/client_name, engagement/engagement_name, engagement/period, engagement/preparer and engagement/logo_path; the workpaper folder is export/workpaper_dir. See workpaper.md.

items.title: Reset
items.text: Reset All Preferences (after a confirmation) puts everything back to the defaults above, resets the layout and node colours, and refreshes the open workflows. Your own themes are kept.

items.title: Complete list of stored preferences
items.text:
Every key in the program's table of defaults:

Key Default general/schema_version 2 (internal) appearance/theme dark appearance/accent empty appearance/font_size 0 layout/restore true layout/session false editor/grid_size 20 editor/show_grid true editor/snap_to_grid true editor/shortcuts {} editor/render_detail_threshold 50 editor/render_detail_card auto editor/render_detail_sockets auto editor/render_detail_label always editor/render_detail_indicator auto errors/continue_past_failure true errors/redact_values false errors/locate_rows true errors/locate_row_cap 5000000 errors/show_technical false audit/record_runs true audit/run_log_dir empty audit/record_identity true audit/hash_inputs true audit/hash_outputs true audit/hash_max_mb 2048 audit/row_counts auto audit/exact_counts_max_mb 256 audit/embed_code true audit/warn_on_input_change true engagement/client_name, engagement/engagement_name, engagement/period, engagement/preparer, engagement/logo_path empty export/workpaper_dir empty

A few more values are written by the app itself and are not in that table: show_welcome_dialog (default on), general/recent_limit (default 10), recentFiles, the window geometry and dock state under layout/, the open-file list layout/session_files and layout/session_active, and the node colours under node_editor_colors/.

items.title: Where preferences are stored and how to reset them
items.text:
All preferences are in one text file, preferences.ini, in %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\ (set the environment variable TRIGGER_DESIGNER_DATA_DIR to use another folder, for a portable installation). Edit > Settings > General > Open Preferences Folder opens it. Your own themes are in the themes folder beside it.

The first time the app starts with no preferences.ini, it copies the theme, grid size, recent files and node colours from the settings older versions kept in the Windows registry.

To reset everything: Reset All Preferences, or close the app and delete preferences.ini.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Symptom What to do My change to a setting did not seem to apply Theme, accent and font apply at once. Audit settings apply to the next Run. Error settings apply to the next error. I pressed Cancel but a setting stayed changed Only theme, accent and font size are undone by Cancel. Other settings are saved as you change them. A shortcut is refused It is already in use, or it has no Ctrl, Alt or Shift and is not a function key. The window looks wrong after choosing a theme Theme Default under Accent, then pick the theme again; or Reset All Preferences. Preferences are lost between sessions The data folder may not be writable. Check %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer or the folder named by TRIGGER_DESIGNER_DATA_DIR.

items.title: Run history and the audit trail
items.text:
Every time you press Run, the app writes a run record: a small file that says what ran, on which files, with which settings, and what came out. Records are numbered, linked to each other in a chain, and can be checked later. They contain no data rows.

This is the evidence trail for the work: "this workflow, in this state, ran on this file (this fingerprint) at this time, by this person, and produced these results".

Back to the guide index
path: Run history and the audit trail
