items.title: What a run record is
items.text:
One record is one JSON file, written when a Run ends, whether it completed, failed or was cancelled. A record holds:

  • who and when: start and end time, user name and computer name (you can turn the names off),
  • what ran: the workflow file's fingerprint, every node with its settings, the generated code (or at least its fingerprint),
  • on what: every input file and output file with its size, modified time and SHA-256 fingerprint,
  • what happened: each node's status, row counts in and out, column names and types, warnings, and the error of a failed node,
  • the result of any audit test (Duplicates, Benford and so on),
  • its place in the chain: its number, the previous record's hash, and its own hash.

A record is written once and never rewritten. The file is also marked read-only on disk.

A record is not a copy of your data: no rows, no cell values. It does contain what you typed into node settings (for example the text of a Filter condition or a Find and Replace rule), file paths, column names, and, for a failed node, the error with up to a few offending values unless you have turned on hiding of data values. See Security and privacy.

You can switch recording off in Preferences (Record every run), but the default is on.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Where records are stored
items.text:
Each workflow has its own store, a folder of records.

Situation Store folder Default, workflow saved on disk Next to the workflow, in a folder named after it: for C:\Work\Orders\orders_check.tds, the folder C:\Work\Orders\orders_check.runs\ You set a Run log folder in Preferences <that folder>\<workflow name>-<8 characters>\ (the 8 characters come from the workflow's full path, so two workflows with the same name in different folders do not collide) The workflow has never been saved %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\runs\_unsaved\ (or <Run log folder>\_unsaved\ if you set one) The workflow's folder is read-only, or the store is locked A fallback folder %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\runs\<workflow name>-<8 characters>\, and the record carries a warning saying so

Inside a store folder you will find:

File What it is <run id>.json One run record. The run id is 32 hex characters. index.jsonl One line per sealed record: its number, run id, start time, status and hashes. This is what the Run History list reads, so it opens fast. hash_cache.json A speed-up cache of file fingerprints. It is not part of the evidence; you may delete it. <run id>.started A marker that exists only while a Run is in progress. A marker that is left behind means the app or computer stopped during a Run. .lock Exists for moments while a record is being written.

Records follow the path of the workflow. If you move or rename a workflow, its history stays behind in the old .runs folder and the next Run starts a new store. Move the .runs folder with it to keep one continuous history.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: The Run History dock
items.text: Open Window > Run History. It lists the runs of the workflow in front, from the primary store folder and from the fallback folder (used when the primary one was read-only), newest first. The status line says how many runs came from the fallback folder. The two folders keep separate chains, so run numbers can repeat; Verify run log checks both.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: The list
items.text:
Column Meaning # Run number in this store (1, 2, 3...). The newest run is at the top. Started Local start time. Status ok, failed or cancelled. Duration Wall-clock time of the whole Run. Nodes Number of nodes in the run. Rows out Rows written to output files, when counted. Chain Empty until you press Verify run log; then ok, or the first kind of problem found for that run.

The numbers in the last columns are loaded in the background for the 500 most recent runs.

When nothing is recorded yet, the dock says "No runs recorded yet".
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: The toolbar
items.text:
All buttons are icons; hover to read their tooltips.

Button (tooltip) What it does Refresh run list Reads the index again. Verify run log Checks the whole chain (see below). The status line then says "chain verified at HH:MM - head xxxxxxxx", or "chain verification FAILED (n)" and a dialog lists the problems. Open run log folder Opens the store folder in Explorer. Check inputs against selected run Re-fingerprints the input files recorded in the selected run and compares them with what the record says (see below). Compare two selected runs Select exactly two runs (click one, then Ctrl+click another), then press this toggle. The bottom-right table switches to differences. Export selected run as JSON Saves a copy of the record (file name run-0001-xxxxxxxx.json). Export selected run as HTML report Saves a self-contained web page with the summary, integrity details, inputs, outputs, steps, a Tests section (the result of each Audit node), errors, settings and generated code, and opens it. If you have verified the chain in this session, the report says whether it passed. The page embeds the record's JSON.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: The panes under the list
items.text:
• Summary for the selected run: run id, number, status, start and end, duration, workflow name and its fingerprint (or "unsaved"), a note when the workflow had unsaved changes at the time, how many inputs and outputs and whether they were all hashed, number of nodes (with failed and skipped counts), the row-count mode used, who ran it, program versions, how many inputs changed since the previous run, number of warnings and the start of the record hash.
  • Nodes table, one row per node: Node, Operation, Status, In, Out, Cols, Time, Test, Problem. Test is filled for Audit nodes, for example fail: 12 of 1,000 (1.2%) (the node's test_summary); it is empty for other nodes.
  • Differences table instead of Nodes when comparing: Kind, Node, Field, Old, New.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Check inputs
items.text:
The result dialog has one row per recorded input file:

State Meaning unchanged The file on disk has the same fingerprint as the one in the record. MODIFIED The file exists but differs from the record. Hover the row to see the recorded and the current fingerprint. MISSING The file is no longer where the record says. not checked The record has no fingerprint for it (hashing was off, or the file was above the size limit). unreadable The file could not be read.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Compare two runs
items.text:
The differences that matter to a reviewer, in a fixed order:

Kind Examples environment The app, Polars, Python or DuckDB version changed. input An input file's fingerprint changed, or an input appeared or disappeared. parameter A node setting changed (the field is shown as settings.<name>). row_count A node produced a different number of rows. status A node's status changed. output An output file's fingerprint or row count changed. node_set A node was added or removed.

Times, durations and run ids are never compared, so two runs of the same workflow on the same data show no differences.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: What each field means
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Run level
items.text: Field Meaning run_id Unique id of this run (32 hex characters). Also the file name. seq Number in the store's chain, starting at 1. status ok, failed or cancelled. started_at, finished_at, duration_s UTC times (ISO 8601, ending in Z) and the total in seconds. app_name, app_version, workflow_schema_version, python_version, polars_version, duckdb_version, os_name The environment. user, machine Who ran it and on what computer. Empty if you turned off Record the user and machine name. workflow_path Where the workflow was, or null if unsaved. workflow_sha256 Fingerprint of the saved .tds file at the start of the Run. workflow_uuid The workflow's identity; it stays the same across saves and renames. graph_sha256 Fingerprint of the nodes, settings and connections as they were in memory. It exists even for unsaved workflows. workflow_modified_since_save true if the window had unsaved changes: the file on disk is then not exactly what ran. Compare graph_sha256, not only the file hash. options The effective recording options and the row-count mode that was actually used. inputs, outputs File fingerprints (below). nodes One entry per node, in run order (below). baseline The previous run and the list of input files that changed since it. null on the first run. warnings Notes such as "run log stored in fallback folder" or an input that changed. generated_code, generated_code_sha256 The Python code that ran, and its fingerprint. The text is left out if you turned off Store the generated code; the fingerprint is always there. schema_version, hash_algo Version of this record layout and of the hashing method. prev_record_hash, record_hash Chain links (below).
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Each input and output file
items.text: Field Meaning role input or output. node_id The File Input or File Output node. path, sheet Where it is, and the Excel sheet when relevant. size_bytes, modified_time, mtime_ns Size and modified time at the moment it was read or written. sha256 The file's SHA-256 fingerprint: change one byte and it changes completely. sha256_status computed (hashed now), cached (same size and modified time as an earlier hash), skipped_size_limit (above the size limit), disabled (switched off), missing, error, cancelled. row_count, row_count_method Rows in the file and how that was found (for example materialized for an input counted while reading, output_file for an output counted by reading it back).
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Each node
items.text:
Field Meaning node_id, op, title, label Which node. op is a stable name such as audit.duplicates. seq Its position in the run order. status ok, failed or skipped. started_at, duration_s, peak_memory_mb Timing and memory. duration_s is the node's wall time (code plus row counting). peak_memory_mb is empty (null): memory is not measured. Records written by earlier builds show 0 for both. settings The node's settings as they were. seed The random seed, for nodes that use one (Sample, Split). code_sha256 Fingerprint of the node's generated code. rows_in For each input socket: the node it came from, the row count and the variable name. rows_out, columns_out, dtypes_out, count_method For each output: row count, column names and types, and how the count was obtained. Column lists are capped at 500. warnings Node-level warnings. error For a failed node: code, title, detail, hint, technical text (capped at 8,000 characters), and where known the row and values. test_summary The result of an audit test, or null (see below).

A status of ok for an Audit node means that the node ran. Whether the audit test passed is in test_summary.status.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: The hash chain and tamper evidence
items.text:
Each record carries two hashes:

  • record_hash: a fingerprint of the whole record (with the record_hash field left out), made from a canonical form of the JSON so that spacing and key order cannot matter.
  • prev_record_hash: the record_hash of the record before it (all zeros for run 1).

So each record "points at" the previous one. If anyone edits a record afterwards, its own hash no longer matches. If anyone deletes or swaps a record in the middle, the next record no longer points at what comes before it. Verify run log walks the whole store and reports:

Problem Meaning record_hash_mismatch A record was changed after it was written. prev_hash_mismatch A record does not follow the previous one in the chain. missing_record A record listed in the index is not on disk. index_mismatch A record does not match its line in the index. seq_gap A run number is skipped. schema_invalid A record is missing required fields or has wrong values. unreadable A record file cannot be read. index_corrupt The index is damaged, or records exist without an index.

It also gives non-fatal warnings: an orphan_record (a record file that the index does not list), an incomplete_run (a .started marker with no record, meaning a run that never finished), a clock_skew and an unfinished last index line.

What this does not protect against, and what to do about it:

  • Removing the newest records. If the last record or records, and their index lines, are deleted, what is left is still a perfectly valid chain. Verification cannot know they ever existed. After a significant Run, note the head hash shown after Verify ("head xxxxxxxx", full value in the report and the failure dialog) somewhere outside the folder: in your workpaper, an email, or the engagement file. Later, a verified chain whose head hash differs from your note, or that is shorter, has been truncated.
  • A determined rewrite. The chain proves that records were not changed piecemeal. It is a fingerprint chain, not a digital signature. Someone with full write access who recomputes every hash can produce a different valid chain. Keep the store on a protected location, and keep the head hash elsewhere.
  • The files themselves. Records say what the input fingerprint was. They cannot stop an input file being replaced afterwards. Use Check inputs to see that.

A verified chain means: "these records are exactly as written, in this order, with nothing missing before the last one I know of".
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Row counting and the preferences that control it
items.text:
Counting rows costs time and memory, because a lazy node's result must be computed to know its size. You choose how much to count in Edit > Settings > General > Audit trail.

Mode (Row counts) What it does Auto (default) Looks at the combined size of all input files. If it is at most Count every node up to (MB) (default 256), behaves as "All nodes"; otherwise as "Sinks only". All nodes Every node's output is computed once and held in memory, so every node has exact row counts. Fastest overall for small data; needs memory for big data. Sinks only Nothing is held. Input files are counted with one cheap pass; outputs are counted by reading the written file. Off No row counts.

The mode that was actually used is in options.row_count_mode_effective (and the Summary pane's "Row counts"); the one you asked for is in row_count_mode_requested.

All the Audit-trail preferences:

Preference (Preferences label) Default Effect Record every run (run history) On Off = no records at all. Run log folder empty (next to each workflow) Keep every store under one folder instead. Record the user and machine name On Off leaves user and machine empty. Fingerprint input files (SHA-256) On Off sets sha256_status to disabled. Fingerprint output files (SHA-256) On Same for outputs. Skip hashing files above (MB) 2048 Larger files get skipped_size_limit. Row counts Auto See above. Count every node up to (MB) 256 The Auto threshold. Store the generated code in each record On Off keeps only generated_code_sha256. Warn when an input changed since the previous run On Adds a line to the Logs for each input file that changed. Never blocks a Run.

Details of each are in Preferences.

Hashing a large input takes time on every Run the first time; a repeat Run on an unchanged file reuses the earlier hash (cached) when the size and modified time are the same.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Audit-node test results in the record
items.text:
Audit nodes (Benford, Duplicates, Gaps, Risk Filters, Sample) do two things. They produce tables, and they produce a test summary: one structured result. In the record, the node's test_summary holds:

Field Meaning test_id, test_name For example audit.duplicates#<node id> and "Duplicates". status pass, warn, fail or error. population_rows, exception_rows, exception_rate How many rows were tested, how many were exceptions, and the proportion. population_value, exception_value The same in amount terms, when the test has an amount column. criteria The rule in plain words. parameters The settings used, so the result can be repeated. message The one-sentence outcome, as shown in the node's Result section. code TD-AUDIT-101, -102 or -103 when a warning applies. details Test-specific extras (for Duplicates: number of groups). exceptions_var The internal name of the exceptions table.

The summary is recorded when the Run executes the node on the whole data. The sample-based number you see in a node while editing is not the one that is recorded.

The Run History dock shows the result in the Test column of the Nodes table, and the HTML report has a Tests section with the test name, result, population, exceptions, rate, criteria and message. The full summary is in the record itself (Export selected run as JSON).
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Symptom What to do "No runs recorded yet" after a Run Recording is off (check Record every run), the workflow was moved since (its history is in the old .runs folder), or the record went to the fallback folder. Look at the Logs for "Run log saved: ". The Logs say "The run log could not be saved" The run itself was not affected. Check disk space and whether you may write to the workflow's folder, or set a Run log folder you own. Verification FAILED Read the dialog. record_hash_mismatch or prev_hash_mismatch mean files were edited or replaced. Keep the folder as it is and tell the engagement lead; do not delete anything. Verification reports incomplete_run A Run was interrupted (crash, power loss). It is a note, not tampering. "chain not verified" in the status line You have not pressed Verify in this session. Check inputs says MODIFIED The input file changed after the Run. Either that was intended (a refreshed extract) or the file was replaced; compare with the HTML report's fingerprint. Compare is greyed out Select exactly two runs. An export fails The status line says "Export failed: ..." and gives the reason, usually a locked or read-only target. Run times in the Nodes table are all 0 ms Known: per-node timing is not recorded yet. The run total is correct.
path: Run history and the audit trail

items.title: Running workflows
items.text:
While you build, the app shows you quick results on a small sample. When you press Run, it processes the whole data and writes your output files. This page explains the difference and what Run does, step by step.

Preview first, Run last

Every node reads the first 100 rows while you edit. A count you see before a Run is a count of that sample, not of your file. Press Run before you quote a number or hand over a result.

Back to the guide index

items.title: On this page
items.text:
• Live evaluation and the 100-row sample

items.title: Live evaluation and the 100-row sample
items.text:
Live evaluation is what happens while you edit. Whenever you open a workflow, change a setting, or connect or disconnect nodes, the affected nodes recompute so that you can see their results in the Data Preview and any problems straight away.

Three rules make live evaluation fast and safe:

  1. It reads a sample. Each node reads at most the first 100 rows of each input and shows at most 100 rows of each output. A "from Run" or "evaluated - not run" badge on the Data Preview tells you which kind of table you are looking at. Counts you see while editing describe the sample. For example, a Count node says "First 100 rows only: full count at Run".
  2. It never writes files. File Output nodes only check their settings while you edit. Files are written only when you Run.
  3. It recomputes in order, once. If you change a node, the nodes after it recompute in dependency order, a single time each, rather than once per click.

Some inputs are read in full even in live mode, because the reading library cannot read part of them: Excel files, JSON arrays and SQLite or DuckDB databases. See Limits and performance.

Most nodes also wait until you leave the node before they recompute (the amber "!" mark, see Reading the signs on a node). This is called deferred evaluation: your edit is saved and undoable straight away, but the work happens when you select another node or click the empty canvas.

While a Run is in progress, live evaluation is paused. Edits you make during a Run are queued and applied when it ends.

items.title: Run Workflow
items.text:
The Run workflow button is the round play button at the top-left of the workflow window. There is no menu entry or keyboard shortcut for it.

Only one Run per workflow window can be in progress. Pressing the button while one is running does nothing. While a Run is in progress the play button is replaced, in the same place, by the Cancel run (stop) button.

items.title: What a Run does, in order
items.text:
1. Settle your edits. Any text you have typed that is still waiting for its short delay is committed, and any queued live evaluation is flushed.
  2. Order the nodes. The nodes are sorted so every node comes after the nodes that feed it. If the workflow contains a loop, nothing runs: the edges of the loop are selected on the canvas and the Logs say "The workflow has a cycle. Remove the connection that loops back." The play button is restored.
  3. Clear the last Run's marks. Previous Run problems and red marks are removed.
  4. Recompute every node (live evaluation of everything). Each node is marked out of date and recomputed in order, so the Run starts from settings that match exactly what is on the screen. A node that is still invalid keeps its red mark; the Logs say "Warning: N step(s) have problems and may fail or produce empty output", naming up to five.
  5. Run any preparation hooks. An internal step for nodes that need to prepare before running. Most nodes have none, and a failing hook never stops the Run.
  6. Start the run record (see Run history). If recording fails for any reason, the Run still goes ahead.
  7. Run the nodes, one at a time, in order, on a background thread. The window stays responsive. For each node:
  8. The node's purple ring shows it is running.
  9. The node's generated code is executed against the whole input, not the sample. Most nodes build a lazy plan (a description of the work); the data is actually read and processed when something at the end of the plan, such as a File Output, writes it.
  10. Plans are verified. After a node's code runs, every lazy result has its column layout resolved. This catches a bad column name or a join key that does not exist right at the node that caused it, without reading any data, instead of surfacing later at some distant File Output.
  11. If the node succeeded, it gets a green ring and its outputs are kept for the Data Preview. If it failed, it gets a red ring and an error (see Errors and problems).
  12. Finish. Live evaluation resumes, the run script is written, the run record is sealed, and the Logs show a summary:
  13. the result (completed, failed or cancelled),
  14. how long this Run took, the number of runs in this session and the average time,
  15. "Run log saved: ".

    If any node failed, the Logs dock comes to the front.

    Green rings fade about a second after a successful Run. Red rings stay until the problem is fixed.

items.title: When a step fails
items.text:
What happens next depends on Edit > Settings > General > Error messages > "Keep running independent branches after a failure" (on by default).

  • On (default). The Run carries on with every node that does not depend on the failed one. A node whose upstream failed, or was itself skipped, is not executed: it gets the warning TD-RUN-008 "Skipped because 'X' failed" (not a red error; the node is not marked invalid) and its status in the run record is skipped. The failed node is recorded as failed, the independent branches as ok, and the Run as a whole is failed. Files written by the independent branches stay on disk.
  • Off. The Run stops at the first failed node. Nodes after it do not run and are not marked as skipped (in the run record they are listed as skipped). Files written by nodes that finished before the failure stay on disk.

The Logs dock lists the failed node as the problem; the skipped nodes' TD-RUN-008 warnings are knock-on entries that clear when you fix the first node and Run again. The command-line runner has its own flag for the same behaviour; see cli.md.

After a failed Run:

  1. Open Logs, pick the Errors chip, and click the first row. It selects the failing node.
  2. Read the message and fix. See Errors and problems.
  3. Run again.

A failed Run is recorded too: its status is failed and the failing node has the error.

items.title: Cancel
items.text:
Click the stop button (tooltip "Cancel run (stops after the current step)").

Cancel is cooperative:

  • The node that is executing right now finishes. It is not interrupted.
  • Every node after it is skipped.
  • The button greys out and its tooltip changes to "Cancelling after the current step finishes". The Logs say "Cancel requested - stopping after the current step finishes", then "Run cancelled".
  • Files that earlier nodes had already finished writing stay on disk. A node that was in the middle of writing a file when you pressed Cancel completes its write.
  • The run record is sealed with status cancelled.

Cancel is only looked at between steps, never inside one. If a single step is very long (for example a very large write), Cancel will seem to do nothing until that step ends or hits its time limit (30 seconds for most steps; see below). A step that hits the limit is abandoned, not stopped: the app stops waiting for it and reports TD-RUN-001, but the work it was doing carries on in the background until it finishes by itself, and it may still write its output file after the Run has been reported as failed. After a timeout, wait for the computer to go quiet before starting another Run that writes the same files.

Closing the workflow window or the app during a Run cancels it the same way and waits up to five seconds for the current step.

items.title: The run script
items.text:
Every Run writes a plain Python script containing exactly the code that ran, one block per node, in run order. Use it if you or a colleague want to see what the app did, or to rerun the steps outside the app.

Where %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\last_run\check_output.py (the last_run folder inside the app data folder; setting the environment variable TRIGGER_DESIGNER_DATA_DIR moves it) When it is written At the end of every Run, successful or not What it overwrites The previous script. There is one script per app, not one per workflow, so copy it if you want to keep it. Contents A header, then each node's code. For a node that did not run (for example after a failure) the code is generated freshly; a node that cannot produce code gets a comment line. Running it With a Python environment that has polars and the trigger_designer package. When the app runs from source, the header adds the source folder to the path for you. A packaged installation has no source folder, so the package must be installed in the Python you use.

The script is also embedded in the run record (unless you turn that off in Preferences), together with a hash of it.

The script reads the same files and writes the same output paths as the workflow. Running it overwrites those outputs.

items.title: Time and memory limits
items.text:
Limit Value What happens Time per node 30 seconds (Workpaper Output: 10 minutes) The node is stopped from the app's point of view and reports TD-RUN-001 "This step took longer than 30 seconds and was stopped" (the message states the limit that applied to that step). Workpaper Output is given 10 minutes because writing a very long Excel exception list can take well over 30 seconds. The Run stops with that failure. The work already in progress on the background thread cannot be forcibly ended, so it may keep using the CPU until it finishes; start a new Run only after it has quietened, and consider filtering earlier or writing to Parquet. Time for a SQL Query 25 seconds Interrupted cleanly with TD-SHAPE-115. SQL Query memory 2 GB TD-SHAPE-113 with the engine's message. Out of memory No fixed cap If the computer runs out of memory the step fails with TD-RUN-002. Preview 1,000 rows or 2 MB Display only; it does not limit processing.

See Limits and performance for advice on large files.

items.title: Workflows with no output node
items.text:
A workflow without a File Output (a "sink") can be Run, but there is nothing at the end of the plan to pull the data through. In that case:

  • Nodes are checked: a plan that refers to a column that does not exist fails at the node that caused it. This is the "plans are verified" step above.
  • Audit nodes still compute their summary, and the run record still counts rows according to your Row counts preference.
  • Nothing is written to disk, and a Run that succeeds does not prove that the data would have written without problems.

When you only want to look at results, select a node and use the Data Preview; you do not need to Run.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Symptom What to do Pressing Run does nothing A Run is already in progress (look for the stop button), or the workflow has a loop (check the Logs and the selected edges). "The workflow has a cycle" Delete one of the connections in the selected loop. The Run stops at the first red node The preference "Keep running independent branches after a failure" is off (see When a step fails). Fix that node and Run again, or turn the preference on. "This step took longer than 30 seconds" Reduce the data earlier in the workflow (a Filter or Select Records near the input), or write to Parquet instead of CSV or Excel. The preview is still showing 100 rows after Run The node was edited after the Run, so the preview went back to the sample. Run again. The Run finished but the output file is missing Check that the File Output node has a path and is connected to a node; check the Logs for "Run log saved" and open Problems. A warning about steps with problems appears at the start of a Run Some nodes were invalid when you pressed Run. They will probably fail; open Problems to see why. Nothing happens when I cancel The current step is still running; Cancel acts after it.

items.title: Security and privacy
items.text:
This page says plainly what the app is built to guarantee, how it does it, and what it does not promise. It is written for people who handle client data and workflows from other people.

Nothing leaves this computer

The program has no update check, no telemetry and no cloud feature, and it contains no networking library. Your files, workflows and run records stay on your machine.

Back to the guide index

items.title: On this page
items.text:
• The short version
  • Your text is treated as data, never as code
  • SQL is read-only and locked down
  • Databases are opened read-only
  • No network access
  • What the run records contain
  • Hiding data values in messages
  • What is not guaranteed
  • Opening a workflow you did not create
  • If something goes wrong

items.title: The short version
items.text: The app does The app does not Keep your data on your computer. It has no feature that sends data anywhere. Encrypt your files, workflows or run records. Turn what you type into settings, not into program code. Stop a workflow from reading files you can read, or writing files where you can write. Let SQL only read, and only the tables the node gives it. Prove who a person is. The user name in a record is whatever Windows reports. Open databases read-only. Guard against someone with write access to the run-record folder who rewrites the whole chain. Keep data values out of run records. Keep every value out of every log (see below).

items.title: Your text is treated as data, never as code
items.text:
A workflow is a set of settings. When you press Run (or while you edit, on the live sample), the app generates Python code from those settings and executes it. That is what the run script shows.

The rule that protects you is in core/codegen_safe.py: text you type is never pasted into code as code. Every value, such as a column name, a find-and-replace text, a file path or a filter value, is turned into a quoted literal (using Python's own repr or JSON string rules) before it is put in a code string. A column called x'); import os # is just a column with a strange name. Line breaks in a label or a comment cannot end a code comment and start a statement either.

How it is checked: the unit tests feed hostile text (quotes, backslashes, line breaks, null characters, fake code) to these helpers and confirm that it comes back identical and stays on one line, and a test scans the code generators for the unsafe patterns '{x}' and "{x}", which are the classic ways to let text escape.

This is a property of the app's built-in nodes. There is no custom-code node in the application, so a workflow cannot contain a Python script of its own.

items.title: SQL is read-only and locked down
items.text:
Several nodes accept SQL text from you: SQL Query, Formula, Multi-Field Formula and the expression mode of Filter. All of them go through one guard (core/sql_guard.py) that applies two independent defences:

1. The text is checked first. A query is rejected unless it is exactly one read-only SELECT. In particular:

Rejected Code Empty SQL TD-SHAPE-001 More than one statement (anything after a ;) TD-SHAPE-110 Anything that is not a SELECT, including INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP, ATTACH, COPY, INSTALL, LOAD, SET, PRAGMA, DESCRIBE, SHOW, EXPLAIN TD-SHAPE-111 Functions or syntax that touch files, the system or randomness: read_*, glob, *_scan, sniff_csv, query, duckdb_*, pragma_*, current_setting, getenv, random, uuid, setseed; FROM 'file.csv' and FROM "dir/file.csv"; dollar-quoted and escape strings; control characters TD-SHAPE-112 SQL that does not parse TD-SHAPE-113 More than 20,000 characters TD-SHAPE-114

Comments and string contents are blanked before the rules are applied, and look-alike characters (full-width letters, ligatures) are normalised, so they cannot be used to dodge the rules.

2. The query then runs in a locked sandbox. It runs on a fresh, in-memory DuckDB connection with external access switched off (no files, no network), configuration locked (the query cannot change its own settings), one thread, and, for the SQL Query node, a 2 GB memory limit. The only data it can see is the frames the node hands to it.

3. It is time-limited. A query that runs longer than 25 seconds is interrupted (TD-SHAPE-115).

Either layer alone could be bypassed. Together, the SQL of a workflow cannot read a file, write a file, load an extension, or change the engine's settings.

items.title: Databases are opened read-only
items.text: A File Input that reads an SQLite or a DuckDB file opens it read-only (SQLite in read-only mode, DuckDB with the read-only flag), and only accepts a table name or a single SELECT. The app cannot change a database it reads.

items.title: No network access
items.text: The application does not contact the internet, a license server, or any other computer: it has no update check, no telemetry and no cloud features, and the code contains no networking library (the only use of socket is to read your computer's name for the run record). SQL and databases are sandboxed from the network as described above. Your input files can of course live on a network drive, and the app reads and writes them like any other path.

items.title: What the run records contain
items.text:
Run records are designed to prove what happened without holding your data.

In a record Not in a record File paths, sizes, modified times and fingerprints (SHA-256) The rows or cell values of any file Column names and column types, row counts Any table data Node settings (including filter text, find-and-replace text, thresholds) Passwords (the app does not handle any) The generated code (optional) User name and computer name (optional) For a failed node: the error and, unless hidden, a few of the offending values For an audit test: counts, rates, parameters and aggregate results

Two things to be aware of:

  • Settings can hold sensitive text. If you type a customer's name into a Filter or a Find and Replace rule, it is in the settings, and so in the record and in the embedded code. Treat records as you would the workflow file itself.
  • Failed-node errors can carry sample values. See the next section.

You can also turn off the user and machine name, the embedded code, and the whole recording in Preferences.

items.title: Hiding data values in messages
items.text:
Error messages can quote the bad values they found ("contains 'abc' in row 3"). Tick Edit > Settings > General > Error messages > Hide data values in error messages to remove those values from:

  • the node tooltip and the Logs dock,
  • the text you copy with Copy details,
  • the error stored in the run record,
  • the technical text and stack trace (the offending values are scrubbed),
  • the session log, which receives the same message.

The code, the column and the row number remain, so you can still find the problem.

What it does not do: it does not remove values from the Data Preview, from your output files, from the clipboard when you use Copy as TSV, or from values you typed into settings. The session log file (see Files and formats) is a diagnostic record: it can contain file paths, settings and detailed messages. Keep it with the same care as the workflow, and review it before sending it to anyone.

items.title: What is not guaranteed
items.text:
Be clear-eyed about the limits:

  • No encryption. Workflows, run records, logs and preferences are plain files. Use disk or folder encryption and file permissions to protect them.
  • Tamper evidence, not tamper proofing. The run-record chain detects edits, swaps and deletions in the middle. It cannot detect that the newest records were removed, and it is not a digital signature: someone who can write to the folder and recomputes every hash can make a different, valid-looking chain. Note the chain's head hash outside the folder after important runs. See the hash chain.
  • Identity is not verified. The "user" and "machine" in a record are what Windows reports, and can be switched off.
  • A workflow can read and write what you can. A File Input can point at any file you may read; a File Output at any path you may write, and overwrites an existing file without asking.
  • The 30-second step limit and SQL limits are safety nets, not security boundaries. A very heavy step can still use a lot of CPU or memory until it ends.
  • The preview is not redacted. If someone can see your screen, they can see your data.
  • Spreadsheet formulas. When you write data that begins with =, +, - or @ to a CSV or Excel file and open it in Excel, Excel may treat it as a formula. Review output that came from untrusted data before opening it in Excel. (The workpaper export has its own handling; see workpaper.md.)
  • Dependencies. The app relies on third-party libraries (Polars, DuckDB, Qt and others). Keep your installation up to date with your administrator.

items.title: Opening a workflow you did not create
items.text:
A .tds file is text that someone else wrote. What can it do?

Safe by design:

  • It cannot contain code to run. The nodes in it are looked up by name from the nodes built into the app; an unknown node name becomes an inert Unknown placeholder.
  • Its settings become literals in generated code (see above), and its SQL goes through the sandbox.
  • Opening it does not write any file and does not send anything anywhere.

Still worth care:

  • Opening it reads files. The live preview reads the first rows of the files its File Input nodes point at, and Excel, JSON and database inputs are read whole. If a workflow points at a huge file, opening it will be slow.
  • Running it writes files. A File Output node can point at any location you can write to, replacing a file there. Before you press Run on a workflow from someone else, click each File Output node and read where it writes, and check each File Input for what it reads.
  • Paths are theirs. The absolute paths were set on their computer. If a relative path exists on yours, it is used first (see How file paths are stored). Check that you are about to process the data you think you are.
  • Read the settings. A workflow can contain filters or formulas that silently drop or change rows. Open each node, or compare against the run script.
  • Newer files. A file saved by a newer version loads with a warning and may drop settings this version does not understand; use Save As so the original stays intact.

A safe routine for an unknown workflow: copy it to a folder of your own, open it, check every File Input and File Output path, look at the Logs and Problems, and only then Run.

items.title: If something goes wrong
items.text: Symptom What to do A SQL node says "Only SELECT queries are allowed" or "not allowed (files, system or random)" That is the guard working. Rewrite as a single SELECT without file functions. I need random sampling in a query Use the Sample audit node (with a seed) instead of random(). A message shows a client value I must not share Turn on Hide data values in error messages, recompute, and copy the details again. Delete the old copy. A record shows a name I want removed Records are write-once and read-only on purpose. Turn off Record the user and machine name for future runs. I opened a workflow and I am worried about where it writes Close it without running. Check each File Output. Nothing is written until Run.

items.title: SQL expressions
items.text:
Three nodes accept SQL expressions: Formula, Filter (expression mode) and Multi-Field Formula. This page explains the shared rules: how to reference columns, what you can write, and the most common traps.

For a full function lookup, see the Formula reference.

items.title: Where expressions appear
items.text:
Node What you write What it produces Formula A value expression, one per card A new column value or a replacement for an existing column Filter (expression mode) A condition expression true or false per row; true rows go to the T output Multi-Field Formula A value expression using {col} The same formula applied to every ticked column

You write the expression only, not a full query. The app wraps it into a SQL statement and runs it on the DuckDB engine.

items.title: Column references
items.text:
Put a column name in square brackets:

[Invoice Amount]
[Order Date]
[first_name]
  • Spaces in names are fine.
  • Case is ignored: [AMOUNT] finds Amount.
  • Spaces just inside the brackets are trimmed: [ Amount ] finds Amount.
  • An unknown name is not treated as a column: the engine reports Referenced column "x" not found.

Text goes in single quotes, not brackets:

[status] = 'Paid'          -- correct: 'Paid' is a text value
[status] = [Paid]          -- wrong: [Paid] would look for a column named Paid

items.title: What you can write
items.text:
Any single SQL expression that returns a value (for Formula and Multi-Field Formula) or a boolean (for Filter):

Category Examples Arithmetic [price] * [qty], ([total] - [discount]) / [qty] Comparisons [amount] > 1000, [status] <> 'void' Boolean logic [amount] > 100 AND [status] = 'Paid' Ranges [score] BETWEEN 80 AND 100 Lists [region] IN ('US', 'CA', 'MX') Patterns [name] ILIKE '%smith%', [code] LIKE 'A%' Null checks [email] IS NULL, [amount] IS NOT NULL Conditional CASE WHEN [age] >= 18 THEN 'Adult' ELSE 'Minor' END Type conversion TRY_CAST([amount_text] AS DOUBLE) String functions UPPER([city]), TRIM([name]), LEFT([code], 3) Date functions YEAR([date_col]), DATEDIFF('day', [start], [end]) Null handling COALESCE([email], 'none') Regular expressions REGEXP_REPLACE([sku], '[^0-9]', '', 'g')

Two shorthand spellings the app translates for you:

You type Meaning Works in strip(x) TRIM(x) Filter and Formula x in_between (a, b) x BETWEEN a AND b Filter only

items.title: The critical pitfall: CSV text columns
items.text:
CSV columns arrive as text

Every column in a CSV file is text, even when the values look like numbers or dates. DuckDB does not guess.

These fail on a text column: 

[order_value] + 1               -- No function matches '+(VARCHAR, INTEGER)'
[order_value] > 200             -- Cannot compare VARCHAR and INTEGER
YEAR([date_text])               -- expects a DATE, got VARCHAR

Fix: cast the column before using it.

Use TRY_CAST to handle messy data safely

TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) + 1
TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) > 200
YEAR(TRY_CAST([date_text] AS DATE))

TRY_CAST returns empty (null) when a value cannot be converted, instead of stopping the node. Plain CAST stops at the first bad value.

Or set the column type once in Select and avoid casts everywhere else.

items.title: Parse an amount that has commas
items.text:
TRY_CAST(REPLACE([amount], ',', '') AS DOUBLE)

"1,200.50" becomes 1200.5. An unreadable value becomes empty.

items.title: Parse a non-ISO date
items.text: STRPTIME([date_col], '%d/%m/%Y')::DATE   -- e.g. "31/01/2024"

items.title: Categorise with CASE
items.text:
CASE
    WHEN TRY_CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE) >= 10000 THEN 'Large'
    WHEN TRY_CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE) >= 1000  THEN 'Medium'
    WHEN TRY_CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE) IS NULL  THEN 'Unreadable'
    ELSE 'Small'
END

items.title: Flag nulls with a fallback
items.text: COALESCE([email], 'no-email@example.com')

items.title: Build an identifier
items.text: [vendor_prefix] || '-' || LPAD(CAST([id] AS VARCHAR), 6, '0')

items.title: Days between two dates
items.text: DATEDIFF('day', TRY_CAST([start_date] AS DATE), TRY_CAST([end_date] AS DATE))

items.title: The read-only guard
items.text:
Expressions can only read the table that flows into the node. The engine rejects anything that writes data, reads files or calls system functions:

What is blocked Code More than one SQL statement (anything after ;) TD-SHAPE-110 File or database reads (read_csv, read_parquet, ATTACH, …) TD-SHAPE-112 System and random functions (random(), uuid(), getenv(), …) TD-SHAPE-112 A query over 20,000 characters TD-SHAPE-114 A query that runs longer than 25 seconds TD-SHAPE-115

random() and uuid() are blocked because a workflow must give the same result every time it runs on the same data, which is a requirement for audit evidence. For reproducible random splits, use the Split node with a fixed seed.

A semicolon inside a quoted string or a -- comment is fine: [note] LIKE '%;%'.

items.title: Keyboard shortcuts in the editor
items.text: Key Action Ctrl+Space Open suggestions for functions, keywords and column names Ctrl+Enter Re-evaluate the formula

  • Formula node: how to add cards, set targets and chain sections.

  • Multi-Field Formula: applying one formula to many columns at once.

items.title: Troubleshooting and FAQ
items.text:
The problems people meet most often, with the fix for each, followed by a list of the dialogs you may see and a glossary.

items.title: A file is locked or open in Excel
items.text:
What you see: TD-IN-002 ("'orders.xlsx' cannot be read: it is open in another program or access is denied") when reading, or TD-OUT-002 ("cannot be written: it is open in another program or read-only") when writing. A failed Export Excel... from the preview shows an Export failed dialog.

Why: Windows does not let two programs write a file at once, and Excel locks a workbook that it has open. A folder source also sees Excel's temporary ~$name.xlsx files; those are excluded by default (the default exclude patterns include ~$*).

Fix:

  1. Close the file in Excel (or any program that has it open, including a preview pane in File Explorer).
  2. Run again. For an output, you can also give the File Output node another file name.
  3. If it is read-only, clear the read-only flag or write somewhere else.
  4. On a network drive, check that you still have the connection and permission.

items.title: My numbers are treated as text
items.text:
What you see: sums fail with TD-TYP-003 ("Column 'Amount' is text, so it cannot be ..."), a conversion fails with TD-TYP-001, a filter like [Amount] > 100 gives odd results, or sorting puts "1000" before "200".

Why: a CSV has no types. The app reads every CSV column as text on purpose, so that nothing is silently changed (a leading zero in an account number such as 00123 stays).

Fix:

  1. Add a Select node after the File Input. In its table, set Data Type for the column: Int64 for whole numbers, Float64 or Decimal for amounts, Date or Datetime for dates, and keep String for identifiers.
  2. If some values cannot convert, the error names the first bad row and values (see Row numbers and values). Common culprits: a thousands separator or currency sign ("1,250.00", "USD 10"), a comma used as the decimal mark ("12,5"), text such as "n/a", or stray spaces. Clean those first with Cleansing or Find and Replace.
  3. In a Formula, TRY_CAST([col] AS DOUBLE) turns bad values into empty cells instead of stopping the node.

Parquet, JSON and database inputs keep their own types and do not need this.

items.title: My dates are not recognised
items.text: Dates in a CSV arrive as text. In Select, change the column to Date or Datetime, and where the node offers a date format, choose the one that matches the text (for example year-month-day versus day/month/year). Audit nodes that take a date column have their own Date format list; the text must match one of the formats. If values do not match, you get TD-TYP-001 or an audit warning "N values could not be read as dates and were skipped" (TD-AUDIT-102).

items.title: The result is empty or has fewer rows than I expect
items.text:
Work through these in order:

  1. Are you looking at the sample? While you edit, every node sees only the first 100 rows. A filter for "Region = West" gives an empty preview if the first 100 rows contain no West. The preview's badge says "evaluated - not run". Run the workflow and check again.
  2. Did the preview change after Run? If the badge says "from Run" and the table is still empty, the result really is empty.
  3. Is it the filter? Check the case of text, spaces around values, and whether the column is text or a number (a number column does not equal the text "100"). Use Trim spaces and Ignore case where a node offers them.
  4. Is it a join? Keys must match exactly. Check the key columns on both sides for type (text versus number), spaces and case. A join on Customer_Id (text) and customer_id (number) matches nothing. Add a Select or Normalize on each side so the types agree.
  5. Is a header row being read as data, or the wrong sheet or delimiter? Check the File Input settings (first row holds field names, delimiter, sheet, start row).
  6. Count at each step. Select a node and read the counts chip in the Data Preview, then move one node back.
  7. After a Run, open Run History, select the run, and read the In and Out columns of the Nodes table: they show rows in and out of every node.

items.title: A test found nothing in the editor but something after Run
items.text: This is expected, and it is the most common surprise with Audit nodes. In the editor an Audit node tests only the first 100 rows. Duplicates and gaps are rarely in the first 100 rows. Press Run; the test then runs on all rows and the result in the run record and the output tables is the real one. (In the example in the first-workflow tutorial, the editor shows no duplicates and the Run finds 790 groups.)

items.title: A run is slow or stops after 30 seconds
items.text:
See Limits and performance. In short:

  • A single step may take at most 30 seconds. Filter and drop columns early; write big results as Parquet or CSV.
  • Excel and JSON inputs are read in full every time a workflow opens: convert them to CSV or Parquet.
  • If a Run stops with "ran out of memory", set Row counts to Sinks only in Preferences, filter earlier, and avoid holding huge intermediate tables.

items.title: Cannot find the file after moving a workflow
items.text:
What you see: TD-IN-001 ("The file 'orders.csv' was not found"), with a "Looked for:" path, or a File Input with a red mark and "No file selected".

Why: a workflow stores each input twice: the full path, and the path relative to the workflow. When it opens, the relative path is tried first, then the full one. If you moved only the .tds (not the data), the relative path breaks, and if the data also moved or the drive letter differs, the full path breaks too.

Fix:

  1. Select the File Input node and click Browse for file (the folder icon next to Source). Pick the file again. Save the workflow so the new relative path is stored.
  2. To move a project, move the workflow and its data together, keeping the folder layout.
  3. Network drive letters can differ between computers; a UNC path (\\server\share\...) is more portable.
  4. Do the same for File Output nodes: their path is also a full path you may need to update.

Records of earlier runs stay in the old .runs folder; move that folder with the workflow if you want the history to follow (see Run history).

items.title: Odd characters, or everything in one column
items.text: You see Cause Fix Question marks or strange letters (CafÃ©), or TD-IN-004 "is not UTF-8 text" The file is in an older encoding (Latin-1 or Windows-1252), typical of old Excel exports. In File Input set Encoding to UTF-8 (replace bad bytes), or re-save the file as "CSV UTF-8" from Excel. One wide column holding everything Wrong delimiter (for example a semicolon file read as comma). Set Delimiter in File Input (;, \t for tab, \|). TD-IN-007 "Some rows have more fields than the header" An unquoted delimiter inside a value, or the wrong delimiter. Check the delimiter, and that values containing it are wrapped in quotes. Column names have spaces or odd capitals The source headers. Add Normalize (trim spaces, spaces to underscores, optional case). A leading zero disappeared It was converted to a number somewhere. Keep the column as String in Select; in Excel, format the column as text before saving.

items.title: Excel export is missing or fails
items.text:
• In the Data Preview: choose Options > Export Excel.... If it fails you get an Export failed dialog with the reason. A locked target file is the usual cause (see above).
  • In a File Output node: choose Excel in Format and a file name ending in .xlsx. If you get TD-OUT-003 "Excel export is not available in this installation", the Excel writer is missing from the installation: write CSV or Parquet in the meantime and ask your administrator to reinstall the application.
  • Too big for Excel: a sheet holds at most 1,048,575 data rows and 16,384 columns (TD-OUT-013, TD-OUT-011). Write CSV or Parquet, or filter first.
  • Export from the preview writes only what the preview holds (up to 1,000 rows or 2 MB, and only the rows matching the preview's search box), not the whole result. Use a File Output node and Run to get everything.
  • For a formatted workpaper (header block, index sheet), see workpaper.md.

items.title: Run does nothing, or my output file is not there
items.text: Check Fix Is the stop button showing instead of play? A Run is in progress. Wait, or cancel. Did the Logs say "The workflow has a cycle"? Remove one connection of the loop (the loop's edges are selected). Is there a File Output node, connected, with a path? Without one, a Run writes nothing. See Workflows with no output node. Did a node fail? The Logs dock opens by itself after a failed Run; fix the first problem. Is the file where you think? Open the File Output node and read the path in File. Use a full path so there is no doubt where it goes. Check the run record's outputs, which lists the exact paths written. Is the run record there? Run History lists it. "Run log saved: " in the Logs says where it went.

items.title: The Logs dock and the log file are quiet
items.text:
The program keeps routine detail out of the Logs dock and the log file. You see warnings, errors and the main steps of a Run. To see every detail, including the technical trace, start the program with the environment variable TRIGGER_DESIGNER_LOG_LEVEL set to DEBUG:

$env:TRIGGER_DESIGNER_LOG_LEVEL = "DEBUG"
& "C:\Tools\TriggerDesigner\TriggerEditor.exe"

Use TRACE for the most detail. Any other value, or no value, means INFO. The setting applies to the Logs dock, the console and the log file written to %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer\logs. Set the variable only while you investigate: the trace is long.

items.title: Panels and layout
items.text: Problem Fix The Config Dock, Logs or Preview has disappeared Open it from the Window menu, or Window > Reset Layout. The window opens off-screen or too big Window > Reset Layout, or turn off Restore window and dock layout on startup in Preferences > Layout. The text is too small Edit > Settings > Appearance > Application text. I want a lighter or darker look Edit > Settings > Appearance, choose a theme.

items.title: Dialogs you may see
items.text: Title When What to do Welcome to Trigger Designer At startup (can be switched off) Open a recent file, New Project, or Browse.... Please wait While a workflow opens ("Reading...", "Validating workflow...", "Evaluating workflow...") Wait; large workflows and Excel inputs take longer. Error loading  The workflow could not be read See Files and formats. Workflow Validation Warnings After opening a file saved by a newer version, or one with unknown nodes, a loop or invalid settings Read it. Unknown nodes keep their settings; save under another name if unsure. About to loose your work? (sic) Closing a workflow with unsaved changes Save, Discard or Cancel. Recent file not found A file in Open Recent is gone It is removed from the list. Set Node Label Right-click a node > Set Label... Type the label; empty removes it. Export failed An Excel export from the preview failed Close the target file, or choose another name. Run log verification failed After Verify run log found a problem See the hash chain. Check inputs After Check inputs against selected run Read the state of each file. Export run as JSON / HTML report Saving from Run History Choose a name. Reset all preferences Preferences > General > Reset Confirm to restore defaults. User themes are kept. Theme unavailable, Import failed, Export failed, Delete theme, Duplicate Theme Theme management in Preferences The message says what to fix. Preferences Edit > Settings See Preferences. About Help > About Version information.

items.title: Quick FAQ
items.text:
Does Run change my input files? No. Inputs are only read. Databases are opened read-only.

Does Run overwrite my outputs? Yes, a File Output replaces a file of the same name without asking.

Does editing change my data? No. The workflow stores settings only. Editing shows you a preview computed from a sample.

Can I undo a Run? No: Run writes files and records. Undo covers edits to the workflow. Keep outputs in a folder per version, or use different file names.

Where is my work saved? Only when you save (Ctrl+S). The title shows an asterisk while there are unsaved changes. The app does not autosave workflows.

Can I run the same workflow without the window? Yes, with the command-line runner: see cli.md.

Is my data sent anywhere? No. See Security and privacy.

How do I prove what I ran? Use Run History: verify the chain, export the HTML report, and note the head hash.

Why did the preview change by itself? The preview follows your selection and your edits. Pin it to freeze it on one node.

How do I share a result with someone who does not have the app? Write a CSV, Parquet or Excel file with a File Output node, and send it together with the HTML report of the run.

items.title: Glossary
items.text: Term Meaning Audit node A node that tests data for something an auditor looks for (duplicates, gaps, Benford conformity, risk filters, samples) and produces a pass/warn/fail summary as well as tables. Badge The small round sign on the bottom edge of a node: normal state, red "!" error, amber "!" warning or changes pending. Canvas The workspace where nodes and connections are drawn. Chain (hash chain) The link from each run record to the one before it, so that edits to the history can be detected. Config Dock The panel (Node Configuration) that shows the settings of the selected node. Deferred evaluation A node's recomputation waits until you leave the node; the amber "!" shows meanwhile. Edge A connection from one node's output to another node's input. Eager / lazy An eager node holds its whole table in memory; a lazy node describes work and lets data stream through. Fingerprint (hash, SHA-256) A code computed from a file's contents. Change one byte and the code changes completely, so it proves a file is the same one. Group A coloured box around nodes that belong together. Head hash The hash of the newest record in the chain; note it elsewhere to detect later removal of the latest records. Knock-on error An error shown on a node only because an earlier node failed. Label A short note floating above a node. Live evaluation The quick recomputation while you edit, on a 100-row sample. Node One step in a workflow. Output / Input (socket) The connection points on the right and left of a node. Pin Freeze the Data Preview on one node. Plan The description of the work a lazy node builds; data is read only when something at the end asks for it. Logs dock The log stream and the nodes that currently have an error or warning. Record (run record) The sealed file that describes one Run. Run Process the whole data with the workflow and write the outputs. Sample (live sample) The first 100 rows used while editing. Sink A node that writes data out (File Output). Source badge The tag on the Data Preview: "from Run" or "evaluated - not run". Store The folder holding one workflow's run records. Test summary The structured result an Audit node adds to the run record. TD- code A stable error code such as TD-SCH-001. .tds The workflow file. Workpaper A formatted Excel file produced for audit documentation; see workpaper.md.

items.title: Workpapers (Excel)
items.text:
A workpaper is the Excel file you file with your audit working papers: what you tested, on which data, how, what you found, and enough evidence for someone else to repeat it. Trigger Designer writes one for you, formatted, with the numbers tied together by formulas and with the evidence (file fingerprints, the steps that ran) already filled in. You add your conclusion and your tick marks.

Run before you file it

The Workpaper Output node writes its file during a Run, never from the live preview. File > Export Workpaper... works from the last recorded run, so Run again after changing a setting.
