items.title: What a workpaper is, and why
items.text:
A workpaper is reperformable evidence. A reviewer who opens it should be able to answer, without asking you:

Question Where the workpaper answers it Who prepared it, for whom, for which period? Summary (Engagement block, logo) What was the test and what rule was applied? Summary (Objective, Procedure, Criteria) How many items were tested and how many failed? Summary (Results, with formulas tied to the Exceptions sheet) Which items failed? Exceptions (one row each, with space for a tick mark and a comment) Which data was used? Is it the same file I have? Summary (Source files with SHA-256 fingerprints) and Run log What steps turned the raw file into the exceptions? Workflow (every step and its settings) What was the result of the review? Summary (Conclusion and Auditor notes: yellow cells you fill in)

The four sheets are Summary, Exceptions, Run log and Workflow. The workpaper is a normal .xlsx file: you can annotate it, print it (the sheets are set to landscape, one page wide, with a footer) and attach it to your engagement file. It does not need Trigger Designer to be read.

The fingerprints are SHA-256 values: a short code that changes if even one byte of a file changes. If your copy of an input file has the same SHA-256 as the one in the workpaper, it is the same file.

items.title: Two ways to produce one
items.text:
Workpaper Output node File > Export Workpaper... Covers One test: the exceptions of one audit node The whole last run: every audit test of it When it is written During Run, as the node's step When you choose the menu entry, from the last recorded run Sheets Summary, Exceptions, Run log, Workflow Summary (one row per audit test), Run log, Workflow. No Exceptions sheet. The Run log is A snapshot taken while the run is in flight The completed run Needs Nothing special (the Run log needs run recording on) A recorded run (Record every run on in Preferences) Use it for The workpaper of one test, with the exception list to tick A one-page overview of everything the run did

Use the node for each test you will file separately. Use the menu entry for a cover sheet of the whole run.

items.title: The Workpaper Output node
items.text:
Find Workpaper Output on the Input tab of the node palette, next to File Input and File Output. It is an end point: it has three inputs and no output.

Socket Letter Carries Required Input 1 E Exceptions: the rows to list (for example the Duplicates output of a Duplicates node) Yes Input 2 P Population: everything that was tested (for example the File Input), used to count the population and its value No Input 3 S Summary: the one-row result of an audit node, so the test name, rule and counts are copied and reconciled No

With nothing on E the node is red, its tooltip says "Connect the Exceptions input" and the Config Dock shows the same words. If P or S is connected but has failed upstream, the node is red too ("Population input has no data" / "Summary input has no data"): it does not silently ignore a broken input.

Nothing is written while you edit. The workbook is written by Run workflow, as a step of the run. In the live preview the node produces nothing.

If the Amount column you chose is not in the Exceptions input, the node's tooltip says "The amount column 'x' is not in the Exceptions input".

items.title: The Config Dock, setting by setting
items.text: Select the node to open its Config Dock. The header shows three chips (xlsx, the row limit such as 100,000 row limit, and the "If it exists" choice in lower case) and the file name. The dock has six sections, in this order. Edits take effect on the next Run; every change is one undo step named "Workpaper Setting Changed".

items.title: File
items.text: Control Default What it does File (text box, with a Browse for save location icon button) empty (placeholder "Enter file path (.xlsx)") The workbook to write. Must end in .xlsx, and the folder must exist. The browse button opens a Save dialog ("Save workpaper", filter "Excel workbook (*.xlsx)"), adds .xlsx if you leave it off, starts in the folder of the last workpaper, and remembers the folder you choose. If it exists New version What to do when the file is already there. New version keeps the old file and writes name (2).xlsx (then (3)...). Replace overwrites. Stop with error refuses (TD-OUT-010). Hover text: "New version keeps a workpaper you already annotated".

items.title: Engagement (open by default; can be collapsed)
items.text:
These fill the header of the Summary sheet. A box you leave empty uses the matching Preferences value, which is shown in grey inside the box as its placeholder.

Control Default What it does Reference empty (placeholder "e.g. C.3.1") Your workpaper reference. Shown as "Workpaper reference". Empty cells stay yellow for you to complete. Client empty, then Preferences > Client The client. Also stored as the file's Company property. Engagement empty, then Preferences > Engagement The engagement name. Period empty, then Preferences > Period The period covered, as free text. Prepared by empty, then Preferences > Prepared by, then your Windows user name The preparer. Also stored as the file's Author property. Prepared on empty (placeholder "today (YYYY-MM-DD)") The preparation date. Empty means the day of the Run. Anything that is not a valid YYYY-MM-DD date stops the run with TD-OUT-012. Logo (with a Browse for logo image icon button) empty (placeholder "PNG or JPG"), then Preferences > Logo An image shown at the top right of the Summary. PNG or JPG only. It is scaled to at most 200 by 36 pixels. A logo that cannot be read does not stop the workpaper; a line in Notes and limitations says "Logo not added: ...".

items.title: Test
items.text: Control Default What it does Test name empty The title of the workpaper (first line of the Summary) and "Test performed". If empty, the name from the S input is used for "Test performed", and the title says "Audit workpaper". Objective empty What the test is meant to show. Several lines allowed. An empty Objective leaves a yellow cell on the Summary for you to type in. Procedure empty What you did. Same behaviour as Objective. Criteria empty The rule applied. If empty, the S input's rule is used; if there is none, the cell says "Not provided - complete manually".

items.title: Values
items.text: Control Default What it does Amount column none (blank allowed) The column of the E input to total. It drives the Value column of the Results block and the formatting of that column on the Exceptions sheet. Pick a number column, or a text column that holds amounts (see Amounts). Hover text: "Column summed for the value statistics". Decimals 2 Decimal places (0 to 6) used to show values on the Summary and in the amount column.

items.title: Sheets
items.text: Control Default What it does Row limit 100,000 The most exception rows listed in the workbook (1 to 1,048,574). More than that is not cut silently: see Excel's limits. Hint under the box: "Large workpapers can take minutes; this step may run up to 10 minutes." Exceptions sheet Exceptions The name of the listing sheet. Illegal characters ([ ] : * ? / \) become spaces, it is cut to 31 characters, and it cannot be Summary, Run log, Workflow or Tests (a number is added, for example Summary (2)). Include run log On Adds the Run log sheet. Include workflow On Adds the Workflow sheet.

items.title: Sources (collapsed by default)
items.text:
Control Default What it does Extra source files empty (placeholder "One path per line") Files that were read outside the workflow (for example a policy document or a manual extract). Each is listed on the Summary with its size, date and SHA-256, computed when the workpaper is written. Hover text: "Files read outside the workflow; they are hashed when the workpaper is written".

The files read by the workflow itself (every File Input upstream of the node) are listed automatically.

items.title: Engagement defaults in Preferences
items.text:
Open Edit > Settings, page General, section Engagement. Fill in once, and every Workpaper Output node and the export dialog start from these:

Field Placeholder Stored as Client Client name engagement/client_name Engagement Engagement or audit name engagement/engagement_name Period Period covered engagement/period Prepared by Defaults to your Windows user name engagement/preparer Logo (with a Browse button) PNG or JPG shown on the Summary engagement/logo_path

Each box is saved when you leave it. A value typed in the node always wins over the Preferences value. The folder last used for a workpaper is remembered as export/workpaper_dir. See Preferences.

A node picks up the Preferences values when you press Run, so a change in Preferences takes effect for the next Run without touching the node.

items.title: File > Export Workpaper...
items.text:
Choose File > Export Workpaper... (available while a workflow window is open). It writes a workpaper of the most recent recorded run of the workflow in front.

  1. If the workflow has no recorded run, a message says "There is no recorded run for this workflow yet. Run the workflow first (and keep run recording on in Preferences), then export the workpaper." Nothing is written.
  2. Otherwise the Export workpaper dialog asks for:
  3. File (with a Browse for save location button). The suggestion is <workflow name> workpaper.xlsx in the last workpaper folder, or the workflow's own folder.
  4. If it exists: New version (default), Replace or Stop with error, as above.
  5. Engagement: Reference, Client, Engagement, Period, Prepared by (empty boxes use the Preferences values shown in grey).
  6. Test: Objective and Procedure.
  7. Export and Cancel buttons.
  8. On success a message gives the path. The logo comes from Preferences. The export never touches the run history: the sealed records are only read.

The workbook has Summary, Run log and Workflow. Its Summary has a Test results table with one row per audit test of the run:

Column Meaning Test The test's name Status pass, warn, fail or error (a failing status is shown in red) Population rows Rows tested Exceptions Rows flagged Exception rate Exceptions divided by population Result The rule and the outcome sentence of the test

If the run had no audit test, the table says "No audit tests were recorded in this run." In this layout the Test performed row reads "Whole run: N tests" (counted from the run record; "Whole run: no audit tests recorded" when there are none) unless you typed a test name, and there are no tick marks (there is no exception list to tick).

items.title: Summary
items.text:
The first sheet, protected so the evidence cannot be changed by accident (no password: Review > Unprotect Sheet removes it). Only the yellow cells can be edited. Top to bottom:

Block What is in it Title and logo The test name (or "Audit workpaper"), then "Audit workpaper generated by Trigger Designer version on date time". The logo sits at the top right. Engagement Workpaper reference, Client, Engagement, Period, Test performed, Prepared by, Prepared on, Reviewed by and Review date (always yellow, for the reviewer). Objective and procedure Objective, Procedure performed, Criteria applied. Results The table described below. Conclusion A drop-down: No exceptions, Exceptions - explained or Exceptions - require follow-up, and Auditor notes (free text). Tick marks The legend with a live count of how many rows you marked with each tick (see below). Source files One row per input file (see below). Notes and limitations Everything the writer changed or could not do, in plain sentences. "None." if nothing. Workbook contents The sheets of the workbook, and why a sheet was left out.

Results columns: Measure, Rows, Value, % of population rows, % of population value, Basis. Its rows:

Row Rows / Value Basis column says Population tested Counted from the P input; if there is none, taken from the S input; if neither, a yellow cell for you ("Not provided - enter manually"). Value is the total of the amount column on P, or "n/a" when no Amount column is set. "Counted from the Population input" / "Reported by the test node" / "Not provided - enter manually" Exceptions found Rows and value of the exceptions, as formulas (=B24) so they follow what the sheet lists. If the list is truncated, the true totals are written as numbers. The two percentages are exceptions divided by population (n/a when there is no population). "No exceptions noted" or "Counted from the Exceptions input" Exceptions listed in this workbook =COUNT(...) and =SUM(...) over the Exceptions sheet. "All exceptions are listed", or "TRUNCATED: first N of M listed" in red Full exception list (CSV) Name, row count and SHA-256 of the CSV file, or "Not needed - all exceptions are listed in this workbook". Reconciliation to test result Compares the exceptions received with the count the audit node reported on S: "Agrees to the test node (6 exceptions)", or in red "DIFFERENCE: the test node reported X exceptions but Y were received". With no S: "No test result supplied".

Every figure has a cached value as well as the formula, so previewers that do not recalculate (a phone, a mail preview) still show numbers.

Tick marks are fixed: ✓ Agreed to source document, X Exception confirmed, E Explained - see comment, F Follow-up required, N/A Not applicable. You choose them from a drop-down in the Exceptions sheet; the Summary counts them with COUNTIF.

Source files columns: File, Sheet, Rows read, Size (bytes), Modified (UTC), SHA-256. The list is the input files recorded by the run (their fingerprints are taken before the file is read), then your Extra source files, de-duplicated. A file that has since been moved keeps its row, and the SHA-256 cell says "file not found or not computed". Files larger than 4 GB are not hashed. Rows read comes from the run record; while the run is still going (a single-test workpaper) the count is taken from the rows the input step produced, and says "not recorded" only when that is not known either (for example a folder of several files, where one count cannot be split).

items.title: Exceptions
items.text:
The listing of the E input.

Column Contents A: Ref 1, 2, 3...: a stable reference to quote in comments. B: Tick mark A drop-down (✓, X, E, F, N/A) for you. C: Auditor comment Free text for you. D onwards Your columns, in their order.

Row 1 is a banner: "Showing all 6 exception rows." (or "No exceptions noted."), or in red "TRUNCATED - showing the first N of M exception rows. The complete list is in file." (and the tab turns red). Row 2 holds the headers (a column called Ref, Tick mark or Auditor comment in your data gets " (data)" added; an unnamed column becomes Column 3). The headers, and the Ref column, are frozen; there are filter buttons; the sheet repeats its header when printed. This sheet is not protected, so you can sort, tick and comment.

How values are shown: numbers as numbers, dates as yyyy-mm-dd, times and timestamps as Excel dates (time zones removed; the clock time is kept, and the Summary says which columns), durations as seconds (header ends "(seconds)"), blanks as truly empty cells, true/false as booleans. Whole-number columns whose name looks like an identifier (id, no, number, ref, code, account, invoice, po...) have no thousands separator. Whole numbers of 15 digits or more are kept as text, because Excel keeps only 15 significant digits.

items.title: Amounts
items.text: The Amount column is shown with your Decimals and totalled. If the column is text, amounts such as 1,234.50, (12.00) (read as -12) and 7 are read as numbers. European and Swiss forms are understood too: 12,5 and 1.234,50 are read as 12.5 and 1234.5, 1'234.50 as 1234.5. A single comma followed by exactly three digits (1,234) is a thousands separator. Values that cannot be read at all stay as text, are not totalled, and are counted in a line of Notes and limitations. The totals are sums of floating point numbers.

items.title: Run log
items.text:
The evidence of the run: who ran what, with what, and what each step did.

Block What it shows Banner "Completed run." or "Snapshot taken while the workflow was running: steps up to and including X are listed; this step is listed as in progress at the end; later steps are not." The node's workpaper is written during the run, so it is a snapshot (status running, no finish time); the last row, Workpaper Output (this workpaper), has the status "in progress" and stands for the workpaper step itself. Run header Run ID, Status, Started and Finished (UTC), Run by (user@machine), Application version, Python, Polars, Workflow file, Workflow SHA-256. Files One row per file: Role (input or output), Path, Sheet, Size, Modified (UTC), SHA-256. Steps Step, Node, Type, Status, Started (UTC), Duration (s), Rows out, Message (the warnings, or for a failed step its plain-language error and hint; failed steps are shaded red). Rows out is "not counted" when the run did not count rows for that step.

The sheet is protected like the Summary. When the run was not recorded, the sheet is left out and the Summary says why: "no run record is available (run recording is off or not installed)". Switching off Include run log leaves it out too ("turned off in the node settings").

items.title: Workflow
items.text: "Steps that produced the data in this workpaper, in the order they ran." One row per step upstream of the node: Step, Node, Type, What it does (settings) (one Label: value line per setting, long values cut at 300 characters; a File Input step reads, for example, Source, Source type, Delimiter, Encoding, Sheet or Sheets, Row limit and the folder or pattern options, and leaves out internal bookkeeping) and Takes data from (the nodes feeding it). Below, under Notes in the workflow, every Comment node on the canvas is copied word for word, so your explanations travel with the evidence. Protected like the Summary. If no workflow information is supplied the sheet is left out with the reason on the Summary.

items.title: File names, versions and replacing
items.text:
• New version (the default) never overwrites. The first Run writes wp.xlsx; the next writes wp (2).xlsx, then wp (3).xlsx. Your annotated copy is safe. The CSV list, when there is one, is versioned the same way.
  • Replace overwrites the workbook. If the old file is open in Excel (Excel makes a hidden ~$wp.xlsx lock file next to it) the Run stops with TD-OUT-002, "open in Excel".
  • Stop with error refuses to write when wp.xlsx (or its CSV) exists: TD-OUT-010.
  • The workbook is built in a temporary folder and moved into place last, so a failure never leaves a half-written file, and an existing file is never damaged by a failed Run.
  • The run record names the workbook that was really written, with the version number (see below).

items.title: Safe by construction: formulas in your data
items.text:
Data from other people can contain text that Excel would run as a formula, for example =HYPERLINK(...), or -2+3. Opening such a cell, or re-entering it, can run the formula, open a link or leak data. The workpaper protects you:

  • Every piece of text from your data is stored as text, never as a formula, number or link. The workbook is created with those conversions switched off.
  • Text that starts with =, @, a tab or a carriage return, or with + or - followed by anything other than a plain number, also gets Excel's quote prefix format, so editing the cell and pressing Enter keeps it as text. A plain signed number such as -12.50 or +5 is not touched.
  • The CSV list gets the same treatment: the risky cells begin with an apostrophe ('=1+1).
  • Control characters in text are replaced by the replacement character (U+FFFD) and a line in the Summary counts them.
  • The only formulas in the workbook are the ones the writer itself created (the Summary's COUNT, SUM, COUNTIF and IFERROR).

You can see it in the worked example: a note =1+1 in the data is still the text =1+1 in the Exceptions sheet.

items.title: Excel's limits and what happens at them
items.text:
Limit What the workpaper does Code Rows. A sheet holds 1,048,576 rows; the workpaper uses 2 for the banner and header, so at most 1,048,574 exceptions can be listed. The Row limit (default 100,000) lists the first rows. Above it the sheet lists the first N rows and says so: the red banner, the red tab, the red "TRUNCATED" line and the totals on the Summary, and a note. Every row is written to <workbook name>_exceptions_full.csv next to the workbook (its row count and SHA-256 are on the Summary). Nothing is dropped silently. none (a warning in the Logs) Columns. 16,384 per sheet; the workpaper adds three. More than 16,381 data columns: the Run stops. Select fewer columns first. TD-OUT-011 Text in a cell. 32,767 characters. Longer text is shortened with a marker ("...[shortened from N characters; full text in the CSV file]"), a note is added, and the full list goes to the CSV even if the row limit was not reached. none Sheet names. 31 characters, no [ ] : * ? / \. The name is cleaned and cut, and kept unique. none Whole table to one sheet. (File Output as Excel, and the Data Preview export, not the workpaper.) Refused rather than cut: more than 1,048,575 data rows. TD-OUT-013 Excel cannot create the file (unusable cell content or sheet name). The Run stops; nothing is written. TD-OUT-014

The workpaper never refuses for rows: it lists what fits and writes the rest to the CSV. TD-OUT-013 applies to the one-sheet exports only.

Size and time: a 500,000-row exception list (8 columns) took between 34 and 47 seconds and about 205 MB extra memory in the benchmark on the developer's machine (more than the editor's usual 30-second step limit, which is why this step gets 10 minutes); memory stays bounded however long the list is, because rows are written in batches. The editor stops most steps at 30 seconds but waits up to 10 minutes for Workpaper Output (TD-RUN-001 if even that is exceeded); see Time and memory limits. For a very long list, lower the Row limit, which keeps the workbook small and quick to open; the CSV still carries every row.

items.title: How a workpaper ties to the audit trail
items.text:
Every Run is recorded in the run history (when Record every run is on). The Workpaper Output node adds to it:

  • The workbook is an output of the run. The run record lists it with its SHA-256, the same value you get by hashing the file afterwards. Open Window > Run History, select the run, and compare. If somebody edits the workbook later, its fingerprint no longer matches the record, so you can show which version came out of the run. (Annotating your own copy, of course, changes it: keep the original, which New version does for you.)
  • The workpaper's Run log sheet carries the matching evidence: the run ID, the workflow's SHA-256, and the input files with the fingerprints taken before they were read.
  • Because the node's workpaper is written during the run, its Run log is a snapshot. The sealed, final record is in Run History; File > Export Workpaper... gives a workpaper of that final record.

items.text: After the Run, Window > Run History lists the run with the workbook as an output. Its SHA-256 (bce72a5c...8370a in this run) is the SHA-256 of duplicate_payments.xlsx, as you can check with certutil -hashfile duplicate_payments.xlsx SHA256.

File > Export Workpaper... on the same run gives Summary, Run log and Workflow (no Exceptions). Its Test results table:

items.title: From the command line
items.text:
A workflow with a Workpaper Output node runs unattended with trigger-designer-cli like any other (see Command line). Approve it once, then run it:

> trigger-designer-cli approve dup_payments.tds --yes
...
operations:
  audit.duplicates: 1
  input.file_input: 1
  input.workpaper_output: 1
  report.comment: 1
writes:
  ...\gui\duplicate_payments.xlsx

> trigger-designer-cli run dup_payments.tds --output-dir D:\audit\out --create-output-dirs
... INFO    node.started node_id=... title=Workpaper Output op=input.workpaper_output index=2 total=4
... INFO    node.finished ... title=Workpaper Output status=ok duration_s=0.266
... INFO    output.committed path=...\duplicate_payments.xlsx size_bytes=11526 sha256=1823177c...
... INFO    run.finished status=ok exit_code=0 ... nodes_ok=4 nodes_failed=0

What was checked in a real run:

  • --output-dir moves the workbook. The file was written to D:\audit\out\duplicate_payments.xlsx and not to the folder saved in the workflow. The output.committed line gives the SHA-256 of the workbook, and it equals the hash of the file.
  • approve and info list the workbook under writes, so a reviewer approving the workflow sees where it will write.
  • The Exceptions, Summary and Workflow sheets are the same as from the editor. The workflow still carries the Comment notes. The Engagement defaults come from the Preferences of the Windows user who runs the command, unless the node has its own values.
  • The Run log sheet is there. The command line gives the workpaper a snapshot of the run in flight, exactly as the editor does: the steps before the workpaper with status, start time and duration. With --no-record the sheet is left out and the Summary says "The Run log sheet was omitted: no run record is available (run recording is off or not installed)". The command line also writes its own run record (record_path on the run.finished line).
  • A truncated list works as in the editor. When the exceptions exceed the Row limit, duplicate_payments_exceptions_full.csv is written next to the final workbook (in the --output-dir folder) and the Summary names it.
  • Versions work too. A second run with If it exists on New version writes duplicate_payments (2).xlsx and duplicate_payments (2)_exceptions_full.csv beside the first ones. The numbered name is chosen before the write, and Stop with error refuses an existing file before anything runs.
  • Extra source files follow --input-dir, like a File Input.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text:
Code What it means What to do TD-OUT-001 The output folder does not exist. Create it, or choose an existing folder. TD-OUT-002 The workbook is open in Excel (or read-only). Close it and run again, or choose another name. TD-OUT-003 The Excel writer component (xlsxwriter) is missing from this installation. Export CSV or Parquet instead, or reinstall. TD-OUT-010 A workpaper with this name already exists and If it exists is Stop with error (or the CSV list already exists). Choose another file name, or set If it exists to New version. TD-OUT-011 Too many columns: the Exceptions input has more than 16,381 columns (16,384 less the three the workpaper adds). Select fewer columns before Workpaper Output. TD-OUT-012 The settings are not valid: no file chosen, the file does not end in .xlsx, or Prepared on is not a YYYY-MM-DD date. Fix the named setting. TD-OUT-013 A table is too large for an Excel sheet (more than 1,048,575 data rows). Raised by File Output as Excel and the Data Preview export. The workpaper lists what fits and writes the rest to a CSV instead. Save as CSV or Parquet. TD-OUT-014 Excel could not create the workbook: a sheet name or cell content that Excel refuses. Rename the sheet (Exceptions sheet) or shorten the offending text. TD-OUT-015 Excel output must use the .xlsx extension (File Output with Excel selected and a name ending in .xls; not raised by Workpaper Output, which reports TD-OUT-012). Rename the file to end in .xlsx. TD-OUT-005 The disk is full. Free space or use another drive.

Also: Workpaper Output has no output file; choose one before running. (a workflow with an empty File is flagged when it is opened and before Run). A Workpaper Output step that takes more than 10 minutes in the editor (30 seconds for other steps) stops with TD-RUN-001 (Running workflows); the workpaper step notices that the run has given up on it and does not write the workbook afterwards, so no file appears from a failed run. Lower the Row limit and run again.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Set your Preferences > Engagement once per engagement, and leave the node's Client, Engagement, Period and Prepared by empty.
  • Connect all three inputs when you can. P gives you the population and its value, S gives the rule and proves the exception count agrees.
  • Fill Test name, Objective and Procedure in the node, so the workpaper needs only your conclusion.
  • Keep If it exists on New version while you work and Replace only for a scratch file.
  • Put a Comment node on the canvas near the steps you want to explain. It is copied to the Workflow sheet.
  • Hash and keep the original: the version you annotate is a different file from the one in the run record.
  • Do the sampling, then the workpaper: connect a Sample node's output to E to document the items selected for testing.

items.title: Node reference
items.text:
Every node in the Trigger Designer palette, grouped by the six tabs you see above the canvas (the same groups appear in the Shift+A menu). Each node has its own page: what it is for, every setting in the Config Dock, a worked example, and the messages it can show.

Every number before a Run is a sample

The canvas preview reads the first 100 rows of each input. A Count that says 100 means 100 rows in the sample. Run the workflow before you quote a count, a total or an audit result, and before you hand over a file.

items.title: The six families
items.text:
• Input and Output nodes

    File Input, File Output and Workpaper Output: where a workflow starts and ends.

  • Preparation nodes

    Sixteen nodes that clean, reshape and enrich a table before you analyse it.

  • Join nodes

    Join, Append, Union, Reconcile and Fuzzy Match: combine two or more tables.

  • Transform nodes

    Count, Running Total, Transpose, Pivot, Unpivot, Window and SQL Query.

  • Report nodes

    Graph, Data Profile and Comment: look at the data and explain it. The table passes through unchanged.

  • Audit nodes

    Duplicates, Gaps, Benford, Sample and Risk Filters: the tests auditors run on ledgers.

items.title: Choosing a node
items.text: I want to... Use Load a file, or save a result File Input, File Output Tidy messy text, spaces or types Cleansing, Find and Replace, Normalize, Select Keep only some rows Filter, Select Records, Unique Add a calculated column Formula, Multi-Field Formula, Date Helper Total or count per vendor, account or month Aggregate (Preparation) Count the rows of a table Count Add a running balance Running Total (numbers) or Window (any running figure) Compare each row with the previous one, or rank within a group Window Rotate month columns into rows Unpivot (or Transpose) Build a matrix of two categories Pivot Add records from one file to another Append, Union Look up values from another table Join Match payments to invoices with a tolerance Reconcile Match names that are spelled differently Fuzzy Match Write a query that no node covers SQL Query Find repeated invoices Duplicates Find missing cheque or journal numbers Gaps Test whether amounts look natural Benford Select items to test Sample Spot weekend, round-sum or just-under-limit entries Risk Filters Understand a new file Data Profile Show a chart or leave a note Graph, Comment

items.title: Live preview versus Run
items.text:
You work on the canvas with a preview; you get the real answer when you press Run.

The preview is a 100-row sample. As soon as a file is opened, each node calculates its output so you can see the effect. To keep a large workbook responsive, File Input and every node after it work on the first 100 rows of each table in this preview, and show at most 100 rows of each output. The limit is the same for every node (LIVE_SAMPLE_ROWS in the code). In the preview, a Count says "100", a total is a total of the sample, and a Pivot may be missing a header that first appears on row 5,000. Some nodes warn you (Count shows "First 100 rows only: full count at Run"; Data Profile, Reconcile, Fuzzy Match and Date Helper say the same in their own words).

Run uses every row. Run recalculates every node in order, reading the whole input, writes the File Outputs and records the run. Trust the Run, not the preview, for counts, totals, audit results and the files you hand over. After a Run, the Data Preview dock labels each table from Run; a preview table is labelled evaluated · not run, and its tooltip repeats the 100-row rule.

A node runs when you leave its settings. Changing a setting saves it at once and marks the node with a yellow "!" (tooltip "Changes pending - the node runs when you click away"). The node recalculates when you select another node, click the empty canvas, or close the document, and then everything after it updates. So after typing, click away to see the result. Save and Run keep the pending change in the workflow and Run recalculates everything anyway.

Exceptions to the "click away" rule: Data Profile and Comment update as soon as you change a setting. A few nodes do not run on 100 rows even in the preview: Benford reads up to a million rows, and Sample does not draw at all on more than 200,000 rows until you Run.

If a preview result disagrees with the Run, believe the Run.

items.title: Audit nodes
items.text:
The Audit tab in the node palette (and the Audit group in the Shift+A menu) holds five tests that auditors run on ledgers and transaction lists. Each test splits the incoming rows into the ones that tripped the test and the rest, and produces a one-row Summary that says what was tested, how many rows were in scope, how many were flagged, and whether the test passed. (Sample is the exception: its third output is a Selection log, see below.)

All five icons are amber, the colour of the Audit family.

The Excel workpaper of a test (Summary, Exceptions, Run log, Workflow) is described in the Workpapers guide.

items.title: Nodes in this family
items.text:
• Duplicates

    Finds exact and near-duplicate rows.

  • Gaps

    Finds missing, repeated and out-of-order numbers, and days with no entry.

  • Benford

    Tests the leading digits of an amount column against Benford's law.

  • Sample

    Draws a random, systematic, monetary-unit or stratified sample that can be repeated with its seed.

  • Risk Filters

    Flags entries that trip classic journal-entry risk indicators.

items.title: Common to every audit node
items.text:
Wiring. Connect one table into the node's single input. The sockets are labelled with the letters in the table above. Connect any output to a File Output, a Data Profile, or another node. A node whose input is not connected shows "Input has no data" in its tooltip and passes nothing on.

Live preview versus Run. In the preview, upstream nodes (File Input and the Transform and Preparation nodes) pass only the first 100 rows of each table, so every audit node tests that small sample and the numbers you see are a preview. Press Run and every audit node tests all rows. Benford and Sample have their own limits, noted in their sections. The Data Preview dock labels a table evaluated · not run (preview) or from Run. Details: Live preview versus Run.

Changes apply when you leave the node. Like the Transform and Preparation nodes, an audit node re-tests when you select another node or click the empty canvas, not after every change. Typing in a text box counts as a change after about a third of a second. Until the node re-tests it shows the yellow "!" mark, and its Result section does not show a result for the new settings (a node with a refresh button says "Not counted yet"). Save keeps your settings. Run keeps them too and re-tests every node anyway.

Reading the result. Click the node, then look at the Result section at the bottom of the Config Dock.

  • Duplicates, Gaps and Risk Filters do not count exceptions while you edit, because counting reads every row. The Result line says "Not counted yet. Use the refresh button to count." Press the refresh icon (tooltip "Count exceptions now") beside the Result line. Any setting change clears the count again.
  • Benford and Sample count every time the node re-tests, so their result appears once you leave the node. They have no refresh button. Benford also draws a chart.
  • Click an output socket's data in the Data Preview dock to see the rows.

A counted Result line reads STATUS: message, for example FAIL: 4 of 6 rows are in 2 duplicate groups.

The Summary table. Every Summary (Duplicates, Gaps, Benford, Risk Filters) has the same first eleven columns, so you can stack summaries from several tests with Union:

Column Meaning test_name, criteria What ran, and the rule in one sentence of plain language parameters The settings as JSON, so the test can be repeated exactly status pass, warn or fail (see the table below) code, message A TD-AUDIT-1xx warning code (blank when none) and the outcome in a sentence population_rows, population_value Rows in scope, and their gross value (sum of absolute amounts); blank when the test has no amount exception_rows, exception_value, exception_rate The flagged rows, their gross value and their share of the population

After these eleven columns each test adds its own facts (listed in its section).

Gross value is used on purpose: debits and credits cancel in a net sum and would hide exposure.

Status Used by Meaning pass all Nothing flagged (and nothing skipped) warn all Risk Filters: something was flagged (indicators are not misstatements). Others: the result is indicative only, or some values were skipped, or Benford is only marginally acceptable fail Duplicates, Gaps, Benford Duplicates or gaps were found, or the leading digits are nonconforming

Errors versus warnings. A mistake in the settings stops the node with a plain sentence, for example "Choose the amount column." The node turns red and the message, a hint and its code appear in the Logs dock. Unreadable amounts or dates do not stop a test: those values are skipped, the status is raised to at least warn and the message says how many were skipped.

Code Stops the node? Meaning and fix TD-AUDIT-001 yes A required column is not chosen ("Choose the amount column."). Pick it. TD-AUDIT-002 yes The chosen column is no longer in the input (renamed upstream). Pick it again. TD-AUDIT-003 yes The column holds nested values (lists or structs). Choose a plain text, number or date column. TD-AUDIT-004 yes A number or option is outside its range ("Tolerance must be 0 or more."), also a bad holiday date in Gaps and an empty keyword list in Risk Filters. TD-AUDIT-005 yes The input already has a column that the node adds (for example dup_group_id, risk_score, sample_seq). Rename it first. TD-AUDIT-006 yes Risk Filters: a date you typed is not YYYY-MM-DD. TD-AUDIT-007 yes The date format is not one of the five offered. TD-AUDIT-008 yes Risk Filters: no test is switched on. TD-AUDIT-009 yes Sample (stratified): the edges or sizes list is wrong (count or order). TD-AUDIT-010 yes Sample (monetary unit or stratified): no row has a readable amount. TD-AUDIT-101 no (warning) Benford: too few rows were tested for a reliable result. TD-AUDIT-102 no (warning) Some amounts or dates could not be read and were skipped. Clean them or convert the column with a Select node. TD-AUDIT-103 no (warning) Sample: more rows were requested than exist; the whole population was selected.

Undo. Every setting change is one undo step, and typing in a text box counts as one step.

Amounts and dates. Amounts stored as text are cleaned first, then read as numbers. Whitespace, $, £, € and the apostrophes used as group separators are removed, and (x) means -x. Dates may be real dates or text in one of five formats. Their labels in the dock are the format codes %Y-%m-%d, %d/%m/%Y, %m/%d/%Y, %d-%m-%Y and %Y%m%d (Risk Filters shows them as friendly examples such as 31/03/2024 (day/month/year)). A time after the date (2024-03-02 14:05:00) is ignored.

How a text amount is read (verified against the code; the same reader is used by all five tests):

Text in the cell Read as Rule 1,234.50 and 1,234,567.89 1234.5 and 1234567.89 Comma and point both present: the last one is the decimal mark (1,234.50) -1234.5 Brackets mean negative $5, £1,000.00 5 and 1000 Currency symbols are removed -1,234 and 1,234 -1234 and 1234 A lone comma followed by exactly three digits is a thousands separator 1.234,50, 1 234,50, 1'234,50 1234.5 European forms: the comma is the decimal mark 1234,5, 12,50, 0,123 1234.5, 12.5, 0.123 Any other single comma is a decimal comma 1.5 and 1.234 1.5 and 1.234 A lone point is always a decimal point, so 1.234 is not 1234 1.234.567, 1,2,3, abc unreadable Mixed or malformed forms are skipped (TD-AUDIT-102 warning) instead of producing wrong digits

A single comma followed by exactly three digits is always read as a thousands separator, so 1,234 is one thousand two hundred thirty-four, even in a file that means 1.234. If your file uses decimal commas, check the Summary's population_value against a control total.

Audit trail. Each test is also a record for the run history. After a Run, the Summary (for Sample, the Selection log) is turned into a test summary: test id (audit.duplicates#<node id>), name, status, population_rows, exception_rows, exception_rate, population_value, exception_value, criteria, parameters, message, the warning code and the node's extra facts (for example groups, mad, n_weekend). The Run recorder stores it in that node's entry of the run record (test_summary), next to the node's settings, its input and output row counts and the Sample seed. A node that failed has no test summary. Recording is on by default (Preferences > Record every run) and the record is saved beside the workflow; the Run History dock lists the runs. Today the dock shows each node's status, row counts and errors; the test results themselves live in the saved record and in the Excel workpaper (guide). A preview (live) result is never recorded, only a Run.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Tests whether the leading digits of an amount column follow Benford's law. Large departures can point to invented, rounded or manipulated numbers. It is a prompt for questions, not proof of fraud.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. Outputs T Table, S Summary, D Drill-down.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Label Default Effect Amount Column none The amount column (required). The sign is dropped. Text amounts are read as described above. Test Digits First digit First digit (1 to 9) or First two (10 to 99). Test Minimum 10.00 Amounts smaller than this (in either sign) are not tested, because tiny amounts distort the leading digits. Zero is never tested. Result chart and text Bars show the share of rows per digit, the dotted line the share Benford predicts, and digits flagged as out of line are drawn in the danger colour. Below it: the verdict sentence and "Chi-square x (df n), p = ...". Drill-down digits Digits that stand out (automatic) on Automatic: the drill-down gets the digits that are over-represented and statistically significant. Untick it to tick digits yourself (each row shows the digit, its z-score and its row count). Manual digits outside 1-9 (or 10-99) stop the node (TD-AUDIT-004).

Outputs.

  • T Table: one row per digit (9 or 90). Columns: digit, count, proportion, expected_proportion, expected_count, difference, z_statistic, significant (z above 1.96, with a continuity correction), chi_square_contribution.
  • S Summary: the standard eleven columns (test_name is "Benford first digit" or "Benford first two digits"; population_rows counts every row read, exception_rows the rows whose digit stands out) plus digits, tested_rows, mad, conformity, chi_square, chi_square_df, p_value, flagged_digits and unparseable_rows.
  • D Drill-down: the input rows whose leading digit is in the drill-down set, with one added column, benford_digits.

The verdict uses the mean absolute deviation (MAD) between the observed and expected shares (Nigrini's bands):

conformity First digit MAD First two digits MAD status close up to 0.006 up to 0.0012 pass acceptable up to 0.012 up to 0.0018 pass marginal up to 0.015 up to 0.0022 warn nonconforming above above fail

At least 100 tested rows are needed for first digit and 1,000 for first two digits; with fewer, a pass becomes warn and the code is TD-AUDIT-101 ("Only n rows were tested; at least m are needed for a reliable result."). If no row has a usable amount the status is warn with the same code.

Preview limits. In the preview, the node reads at most the first 1,000,000 rows of its input (in practice the upstream node already hands over 100), and says so in the message. Run reads everything, so run the full file for the real result.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
300 invoice amounts, first digit, minimum 10. Digit counts: 1: 90, 2: 52, 3: 36, 4: 28, 5: 60, 6: 20, 7: 6, 8: 5, 9: 3. The table T (rounded):

digit count proportion expected_proportion difference z_statistic significant 1 90 0.300 0.301 -0.001 0.04 false 2 52 0.173 0.176 -0.003 0.05 false 3 36 0.120 0.125 -0.005 0.17 false 4 28 0.093 0.097 -0.004 0.11 false 5 60 0.200 0.079 +0.121 7.64 true 6 20 0.067 0.067 0.000 0.02 false 7 6 0.020 0.058 -0.038 2.69 true 8 5 0.017 0.051 -0.034 2.58 true 9 3 0.010 0.046 -0.036 2.83 true

S says fail, "Mean absolute deviation 0.0268: nonconforming with Benford's Law (300 rows tested, chi-square p-value 1.103e-13).", flagged_digits 5. Only digit 5 is flagged: 7, 8 and 9 are significantly under-represented, but a deficit is only a symptom, so only over-represented digits go to the drill-down. D holds the 60 rows starting with 5 (exception_rows 60, rate 0.2).

Back to the Audit node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Finds rows that repeat.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. Outputs D Duplicates, U Unique, S Summary.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
(defaults in brackets):

Section Label Default Effect Match on column list with All / None none ticked The columns that together identify a duplicate (for example vendor and invoice_no). At least one is required (TD-AUDIT-001). Match on Trim spaces on Ignore spaces before and after text, so "ACME " and "ACME" match. Match on Ignore case off Treat acme and ACME as equal. Match type Exact / Near Exact Exact: every ticked column equal. Near: the ticked columns equal and the amount and/or the date are close. Near match (Near only) Amount blank Column compared with a tolerance. Near match Tolerance and Amount / Percent 0, Amount How far apart two amounts may be. Amount: a fixed difference. Percent: a percent of the larger absolute amount. Near match Date blank Column compared with a window. Near match Window 0 days How many days apart two dates may be (0 to 3660). Near match Date format %Y-%m-%d How text dates are written. Ignored for real date columns. Value Value blank Optional column whose absolute values are totalled in the Summary (population_value, exception_value). Near mode falls back to the Amount column. With neither, the values stay blank.

Near needs at least the Amount or the Date column (TD-AUDIT-001 otherwise). If both are set, a row must satisfy both. Near matching also groups rows linked through a chain of close neighbours (A close to B, B close to C puts all three in one group), as the tooltip on the Near button says.

Outputs.

  • D Duplicates: every row of every group of two or more, with all the input columns plus dup_group_id (1, 2, ... in order of first appearance) and dup_count (rows in that group).
  • U Unique: all the other rows, input columns only, in input order. A row with an empty key cell, or with an unreadable amount or date in Near mode, can never be a duplicate and lands here.
  • S Summary: the eleven standard columns plus groups (duplicate groups), skipped_rows (rows that could not be compared) and unparseable_rows (unreadable amount or date cells). Status is fail when any duplicate exists, otherwise pass (warn if values were skipped).

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Exact match on vendor and invoice_no, Trim on, Ignore case on. Input (6 rows):

vendor invoice_no amount date Acme INV-1 1,200.00 2025-01-03 ACME␠ INV-1 1,200.00 2025-01-03 Beta INV-2 350.00 2025-01-04 Acme INV-3 1,200.00 2025-01-05 Gamma INV-4 80.00 2025-01-05 Beta INV-2 350.00 2025-01-04

(␠ marks a trailing space.) D holds four rows: both INV-1 rows with dup_group_id 1 and dup_count 2, and both INV-2 rows with dup_group_id 2 and dup_count 2. U holds INV-3 and INV-4. S says fail, "4 of 6 rows are in 2 duplicate groups.", groups 2, exception_rate 0.667. Switch Ignore case off and Trim spaces off and only the INV-2 pair remains (1 group, 2 rows).

Near example: key vendor, Near, Amount amount with tolerance 1.00, Date date with a window of 3 days. Acme rows at 1000.00 on 2025-01-03 and 1000.50 on 2025-01-05 form one group, while Acme's 1200.00 on 2025-01-04 (200 apart) and Beta's 1000.00 do not. With Value left blank the Summary reports population_value 4200.5 and exception_value 2000.5 (the amount column is used).

Typical use: pick vendor, invoice_no, amount, exact match, to find invoices paid twice. Then switch to Near with a small tolerance to find the same invoice keyed with a typo.

Back to the Audit node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Finds what is missing from a sequence, such as cheque or journal numbers, or days without entries.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. Outputs G Gaps (the findings) and S Summary.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Label Default Effect Sequence Column none The column holding the numbers (or, for Date, the dates). Required. Sequence Type Prefixed Number: whole numbers (1042, 1042.0). Prefixed: text then digits, such as JE-000123; the series is the prefix. Date: calendar days with no entry. Group by column list with All / None none Check each series separately, for example one per ledger or branch. Also report (not Date) Repeated numbers on Report a number that appears more than once. Also report (not Date) Numbers out of order on Report a number lower than a higher one seen earlier in the same series. This depends on the order the rows arrive in. Expected range (not Date) First / Last blank ("Lowest seen" / "Highest seen") The first and last number you expect, so a gap at the very start or end is reported too. Last may not be below First (TD-AUDIT-004). Dates (Date only) Format %Y-%m-%d How text dates are written. Dates Smallest gap 1 day Ignore gaps shorter than this many days (1 to 3660). Dates Skip weekends off Saturdays and Sundays are not expected, so they do not count as missing. Dates Holidays empty One date per line, YYYY-MM-DD; shown only when Skip weekends is on. A bad line stops the node (TD-AUDIT-004).

Prefixed numbers keep their zero padding: JE-0003 is reported, not JE-3, as long as the series has zero-padded numbers. A series written 1, 2, ... 12 stays unpadded. Cells that are empty are ignored; text that does not fit the pattern is counted as unreadable (TD-AUDIT-102 warning).

Outputs.

  • G Gaps: one row per finding, never one row per missing number. Columns: the Group by columns, then prefix, finding, from, to, count, source_row. finding is gap (a missing range from from to to, count numbers), duplicate (count times; source_row is the 1-based input row of the first occurrence), out_of_order (source_row is the offending row) or date_gap (days with no entry). source_row is blank for gaps. Rows are sorted by group, prefix, finding and then by the numeric value of from, so 6..7 comes before 11..12 (dates sort chronologically).
  • S Summary: the eleven standard columns (population_value and exception_value are blank; an "exception" is one finding row) plus series, gap_ranges, missing_items, duplicate_values, out_of_order_rows, unparseable_rows. Status is fail when there is any finding.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Type Prefixed, column je, Group by ledger. Input:

ledger je GL JE-0001 GL JE-0002 GL JE-0005 GL JE-0006 GL JE-0006 GL JE-0004 AP JE-0100 AP JE-0102

G returns:

ledger prefix finding from to count source_row AP JE- gap JE-0101 JE-0101 1 GL JE- duplicate JE-0006 JE-0006 2 4 GL JE- gap JE-0003 JE-0003 1 GL JE- out_of_order JE-0004 JE-0004 1 6

S: fail, "2 gap ranges covering 2 missing numbers; 1 repeated numbers; 1 numbers out of order." (series 2, exception_rows 4 of 8 rows).

Expected range: for the numbers 3, 4, 5, 8, 9, 10 with type Number, First 1 and Last 12, G reports the gaps 1..2, 6..7 and 11..12.

Date example: type Date, column posting with 2025-03-03, 03-04, 03-07, 03-12 and 03-12 again: G has two date_gap rows, 2025-03-05..2025-03-06 (2 days) and 2025-03-08..2025-03-11 (4 days). Switching on Skip weekends with one holiday, 2025-03-10, leaves 2025-03-05..2025-03-06 (2) and 2025-03-11..2025-03-11 (1): the weekend and the holiday are not missing days.

Back to the Audit node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Runs several classic journal-entry red flags at once and tells you which rows tripped which test.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. Outputs F Flagged, N Not flagged, S Summary.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
First the Columns section:

Label Default Used by Posting date none Weekend posting, Public-holiday posting, Posted after period end (required for those) Effective (optional) none Posted after period end Amount none Round amount, Just below approval limit (required for those); optional otherwise Description none Keyword in description Manual flag none Manual journal Date format 2024-03-31 (year-month-day) How text dates are written: five choices

Then seven sections, one per test. Each has an Enabled switch (all off by default; switch on at least one, TD-AUDIT-008), its options and a Weight (1 to 10, default 1). The options of a test that is switched off stay in the node, greyed out, so turning it off and on loses nothing.

Test Flags an entry that was... Options (default) Weekend posting posted on a Saturday or Sunday none Public-holiday posting posted on a date in your list Dates, one YYYY-MM-DD per line (at least one) Round amount a non-zero whole multiple of a round number Multiple of (1000) Just below approval limit within a margin under a limit (the limit itself is not flagged) Limits, comma separated, such as 5000, 10000; Within (2 %) Keyword in description described with one of your words (any word, ignoring case, anywhere in the text: adjust matches "Adjustment") Words, one per line (at least one) Posted after period end dated after Period end (YYYY-MM-DD). With an Effective date column chosen, only when the effective date is on or before the period end, that is, back-dated into the closed period Period end Manual journal marked manual in the Manual flag column (trimmed, ignoring case) Values, one per line (manual, m, y, yes, true, 1)

An empty or unreadable cell never trips a test.

Outputs.

  • F Flagged: the rows that tripped at least one test, all input columns plus risk_tests (the names of the tests tripped, separated by ;) and risk_score (the sum of the weights of the tests tripped).
  • N Not flagged: the other rows, input columns only.
  • S Summary: the eleven standard columns (values are gross absolute amounts when an Amount column is chosen) plus flagged_two_or_more, total_score, unparseable_rows (rows with at least one unreadable amount or date; a row with two bad cells counts once) and one count per test: n_weekend, n_holiday, n_round_amount, n_just_below_limit, n_keyword, n_after_period_end, n_manual_journal (blank for a test that is switched off). Status is warn when anything is flagged and never fail; unreadable dates or amounts add the TD-AUDIT-102 note.

A row tripping several tests is usually worth more attention than one tripping a single test.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Tests on: weekend (weight 1), round amount (multiple of 1000, weight 1), just below limit (limit 10000, within 2 %, weight 3), keyword (reversal, adjust, weight 2), posted after period end (2025-03-31, weight 3), manual journal (m, weight 1). Input:

je posted amount memo source J1 2025-03-01 5,000.00 Accrual M J2 2025-03-04 9,900.00 Reversal of prior S J3 2025-04-02 1,234.56 Misc M J4 2025-03-05 10,000.00 Adjustment S J5 2025-03-06 250.00 Office supplies S

F has four rows: J1 (Weekend posting; Round amount; Manual journal, score 3), J2 (Just below approval limit; Keyword in description, score 5), J3 (Posted after period end; Manual journal, score 4) and J4 (Round amount; Keyword in description, score 3; 10,000 is the limit itself, so it is not "just below"). N has J5. S is warn, "4 of 5 entries were flagged by at least one risk test.", exception_value 26134.56 of population_value 26384.56, total_score 15, n_round_amount 2, n_keyword 2.

Back to the Audit node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Draws a sample that someone else can re-perform and get the same rows.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. Outputs S Sample, N Not sampled, L Selection log.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Label Default Effect Method Method Random Random: every row has an equal chance. Systematic: every n-th row from a random start. Monetary unit: larger amounts are more likely to be picked (needs an Amount column). Stratified: split by amount bands and draw a set number from each band. Size (not Stratified) Kind Count A number of rows, or a percent of the population. Size Rows (Count) 100 Rows to draw (1 or more). Size Percent (Percent) 10 % 0.01 to 100. The result is rounded up and is at least 1 row. Seed Seed and a refresh button ("New random seed") 42 The same seed and the same data always give the same sample, on any machine and any version of the app. Change the seed, or press the button, to draw a different sample. Columns Key all columns The stable key: the columns that identify a row. Rows are put in a fixed order by them before the draw, so a re-sorted file gives the same sample. Pick a column that is unique per row (for example the journal number) to keep memory small. Columns Amount none Required for Monetary unit and Stratified; optional otherwise (then the log reports population and sample value). Strata (Stratified only) Edges empty Ascending band edges for the absolute amount, for example 1000, 10000. An amount equal to an edge falls in the higher band. Strata Sizes empty One size per band, so one more than the edges, for example 20, 20, all; all takes the whole band. Result text One sentence such as "Selected 5 of 20 rows (random, seed 7)." plus the note, if any.

Stratified sizes ignore Kind and Size. A row with an unreadable amount belongs to no stratum.

Outputs.

  • S Sample: the selected rows in input order, all input columns plus sample_seq (the row's position in the sorted population the draw was made on; with a unique, already sorted key it equals the row number), sample_basis (Monetary unit only: high_value, a row so large it is audited for certain, or interval) and sample_stratum (Stratified only).
  • N Not sampled: every other row, input columns only, in input order.
  • L Selection log: one overall row (and, for Stratified, one stratum row per band) with scope, stratum, method, seed, algorithm (always td-sample-1), population_rows, population_value, requested_size, sample_size, sample_value, interval, start, high_value_items, lower_bound, upper_bound, key_columns, amount_column, parameters and note. Keep L in the workpaper so a reviewer can redo the draw: same data, same key, same settings, same seed, same rows.

Warnings. Asking for more rows than exist selects the whole population and writes TD-AUDIT-103: Requested 50 but only 20 rows exist; the whole population was selected. in note. Zero or unreadable amounts cannot be picked by Monetary unit, and the note says how many. Sample's status in the run record is always pass; the 103 code marks the capped draw.

Preview limit. In the preview, a population over 200,000 rows is not sampled on the canvas. The Result line says "Population has more than 200,000 rows: the sample is drawn when you Run." and the outputs are empty. Run always draws.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Twenty journal lines JE-001 to JE-020 with amounts 120, 80, 9500, 45, 300, 15, 60, 22000, 75, 410, 18, 90, 35, 5200, 66, 140, 25, 380, 12, 700; key je, seed 7, count 5.

Method Rows selected Notes in L Random JE-001, 008, 012, 015, 017 sample_size 5 Systematic JE-002, 006, 010, 014, 018 interval 4.0, start 1.559 Monetary unit (Amount amount) JE-003, 005, 008, 014, 018 interval 1285.5; JE-003, 008 and 014 are high_value, the others interval; sample_value 37380 of 39271 Stratified, edges 100, 1000, sizes 2, 2, all JE-003, 005, 006, 008, 010, 012, 014 three stratum rows (11, 6 and 3 rows in the bands) Random, Percent 10 JE-005, 006 10 % of 20 is 2 rows

Back to the Audit node index.

items.title: Input and Output nodes
items.text: These nodes connect your workflow to files. File Input reads data in. File Output writes the result out. Workpaper Output writes an audit workpaper (a formatted Excel file with the evidence). Every workflow starts with at least one File Input.

items.title: Nodes in this family
items.text:
• File Input

    Reads a CSV or text file, an Excel workbook, Parquet, JSON, JSON Lines, SQLite or DuckDB (one file, a folder or a pattern; matching files are stacked by column name). CSV columns arrive as text.

  • File Output

    Writes the incoming table to a CSV, Parquet or Excel file when you Run.

  • Workpaper Output

    Writes a formatted Excel workpaper with the test results and the evidence behind them.

items.title: Live preview and Run
items.text:
This applies to every node in the app, so it is explained once, here.

While you edit, the app works on a small sample. Run works on everything.

While you edit (live preview) When you press Run Rows each node reads from each input The first 100 rows All rows Rows each node shows on each output At most 100 All rows are processed; the Data Preview shows up to 1,000 rows (or 2 MB, whichever is smaller) Files are written Never Yes (File Output, charts, reports)

What this means for you:

  • Counts, totals and matches in the live preview describe the sample, not your data. A Join can show "no matches" in the preview because the matching row is row 101. A Count node shows at most 100. Treat the preview as a way to check that your settings are wired correctly; read the real numbers after a Run.
  • A problem hiding in row 5,000 will not appear until you Run. An unexpected text value in a number column, a Reconcile that finds too many candidate pairs, or a bad byte deep in a file only show up when the full data is read.
  • Excel, JSON and database inputs are read in full even while editing. Only what happens downstream of them is limited to 100 rows.
  • The Data Preview tells you which one you are looking at. It says "from Run" for the result of the last Run, and "evaluated, not run" for a live preview.
  • To Run, press the Run workflow button (the play icon at the top-left of the canvas). While a run is in progress the same spot shows a Cancel run button; cancelling stops after the current step finishes.

If you need a number you can quote, Run the workflow and read it from the run result, not from the preview.

For how a Run works step by step (and what happens when a step fails), see Running workflows.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: File Input reads one file, every matching file in a folder, or every file that matches a pattern such as D:\data\2025-*.csv, and hands the rows to the next node. It reads CSV, text, Excel, Parquet, JSON, JSON Lines, SQLite and DuckDB files. When it reads several files it stacks them into one table and tells you which files had different columns.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• You start a workflow from a file, a folder of monthly exports, or a database.
  • You need to stack many files that share a layout (twelve monthly ledgers, one file per entity) into one table, with a column telling you which file each row came from.
  • You need only part of a database: write a read-only SELECT.

If you already have a table inside the workflow and want to put two tables together, use Append, Union or Join instead.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Direction Carries (none) Input File Input has no input socket. It is a starting point. Output (one socket on the right) Output The table read from the source.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The Config Dock shows only the controls that matter for the source you chose. Until there is a path, only the Source box is shown.

All edits apply on their own, about a third of a second after you stop typing. There is no Apply button. Each change is one entry in the undo history (for example "Source Path Changed", "Delimiter Changed", "Bad File Mode Changed").

items.title: Source
items.text:
Control What it does Default Source (text box, with two icon buttons) The file, folder or pattern to read. Type or paste a path, or use the buttons. A path that is a folder reads the folder; a path containing *, ? or [ reads every match; anything else is a single file. Icon buttons: Browse for file and Browse for folder. Empty Type How to read the source: CSV, Text, Excel, Parquet, JSON, JSON Lines, SQLite or DuckDB. Appears once there is a path. CSV

Details:

  • The type is detected for you from the file extension, as long as you have not picked a type yourself: .csv and .tsv become CSV; .txt Text; .xlsx, .xlsm, .xls Excel; .parquet, .pq Parquet; .json JSON; .ndjson, .jsonl JSON Lines; .sqlite, .sqlite3 SQLite; .duckdb, .ddb DuckDB. A .db file is opened and its first bytes are checked, so it becomes SQLite or DuckDB correctly. Anything else is treated as CSV. Once you choose a type yourself, typing another path no longer changes it; picking a file with the browse button detects the type again.
  • Browse for folder picks the folder, sets the type to the most common file type found directly in it, and turns on Output filename as field (see below).
  • A file that exists wins over pattern characters. If your real file name contains [ or ], it is read as a file, not as a pattern.
  • Very long Windows paths (over about 240 characters) are handled.

items.title: How the path is saved in the workflow
items.text: When you save a workflow, File Input stores the full path and also the path relative to the workflow file's folder. When you open the workflow, the relative path is used if the file is found there; otherwise the full path is used. So a workflow and its data folder can be copied together to another PC or share and still open. The relative form is not stored when the workflow has never been saved, when the data is on a different drive, or when it sits more than six folder levels above the workflow.

items.title: Files (folder and pattern sources)
items.text:
The Files section only appears when the Source is a folder or a pattern. It is how you control which files are read and how a mismatch is handled.

Control Shown for What it does Default Include Folder Name patterns (separated by ;) that a file name must match, for example part_*.csv; sales*.csv. Empty means "every file of this Type" (see the table below). Case does not matter. Empty Exclude Folder and pattern Name patterns to skip, separated by ;. ~$*; .*; Thumbs.db; desktop.ini (Excel lock files, hidden files, Windows clutter) Include subfolders Folder Also read files in folders below the Source. Shortcuts (symbolic links) to folders are not followed. Off Order Folder and pattern The order in which files are stacked: Name (natural) or Modified date. Name (natural) Columns Folder and pattern What to do when files do not have the same columns: Union by name or Must match. Union by name Bad file Folder and pattern What to do with a file that cannot be read: Stop with error or Skip and report. Stop with error Max files Folder and pattern The most files the source may match, 1 to 100,000. A source that matches more stops with TD-IN-012; raise the number to read it. 10,000 Files read (table) Folder and pattern One row per file (and per sheet): File, Status, Columns. Hover a row for the details.

What "Include" means when empty: the files of the chosen type.

Type Files read when Include is empty CSV *.csv Text *.txt Excel *.xlsx, *.xlsm, *.xls Parquet *.parquet, *.pq JSON *.json JSON Lines *.ndjson, *.jsonl

.tsv files are not in the CSV list. To read a folder of .tsv files, set Include to *.tsv and Delimiter to \t.

Patterns. In a pattern source, * matches any characters within one folder level, ? one character, [abc] one of those characters, and ** crosses folder levels (so D:\data\**\*.csv reads all subfolders). Without ** a pattern only looks as deep as it is written. Matching ignores upper and lower case. Because a pattern already says which files to read, the Include box and Include subfolders are hidden for pattern sources.

Natural name order. Numbers inside names sort as numbers and case is ignored, so part_2.csv comes before part_10.csv (a plain alphabetical sort would put part_10 first). Files in subfolders are ordered by their relative path. Modified date reads the oldest file first, with ties broken by name. The order matters: with Union by name, columns appear in the order they are first seen, and with stacked rows the first file's rows come first.

Columns: Union by name. All files are stacked. Where a file lacks a column, the cells are empty (null). A column that only some files have is added after the columns of the first file. When the same column has different types in different files (for example whole numbers in one Parquet file and text in another), numbers with numbers combine to a common number type, and anything else becomes text. The Files read table shows "missing N", "+N column(s)" or "types differ" next to files that differ, and the node's tooltip gives a summary such as 3 files, 3 differ (first: part_1.csv: missing Region).

Columns: Must match. The Run stops with TD-SCH-011 as soon as any file has a column the others lack or lacks one the others have. The message names the file that introduces the difference and the column. Use this when a different layout means something is wrong and you want to be told.

Bad file: Skip and report. A file that cannot be opened or recognised is left out, the Files read table shows "skipped: " and the reason, and the node chip shows "N skipped". If every file is skipped you get an error (TD-IN-014, "None of the N files ... could be read"). Skipping covers problems found when a file is opened and its header read, and, for CSV, text and JSON Lines files, problems in the first 2,000 rows of the body (an invalid byte, a row with too many fields): such a file is skipped and named. A problem deeper in a file is found later, when the rows are actually read, and then still stops the run even with Skip selected. See Edge cases.

The node holds at most Max files files (default 10,000). A source that matches more stops with TD-IN-012; raise Max files in the Files section.

items.title: Columns and rows
items.text:
These controls apply to all file types.

Control Shown for What it does Default Output filename as field (checkbox) All Adds a column that says which file each row came from. Off for a single file; on automatically when you pick a folder with the folder button Column name When the box above is checked Name of the added column. FileName Value When the box above is checked What goes in it: File name (part_1.csv), Full path (D:\data\jan\part_1.csv) or Relative path (the path from the Source folder, for example sub/part_5.csv; for a single file it is the file name). File name Read all columns as text Every type except CSV and Text Turns every column into text, including nested values. Useful when you want to keep leading zeros, or compare values exactly as stored. Off Row limit All Read only the first N rows. All (0) reads everything. For several files or sheets, the limit applies to the combined table, not to each file. All

If the file already has a column with the added name, the run stops with TD-SCH-010 ("already has a column named 'FileName'. Rename the filename column in File Input."). Change Column name to something else.

The added columns (filename and sheet name) are placed after the data's own columns.

items.title: CSV and text files
items.text:
Types CSV and Text read the same way. These controls appear:

Control What it does Default Delimiter The character that separates fields. Type \t for a tab. One character only; a longer entry makes the read fail. , First row holds field names On: the first row is the header. Off: there is no header and the columns are named column_0, column_1, and so on (counted from 0). On Encoding UTF-8, or UTF-8 (replace bad bytes). UTF-8

Important behaviours:

  • Every CSV column arrives as text. Numbers, dates and amounts are not converted. This is deliberate: it keeps leading zeros (007), long account numbers and odd values exactly as they are in the file. Convert columns with a Select node when you need numbers or dates.
  • Empty cells become null. A cell with nothing between the delimiters is an empty (null) value.
  • Blank header cells get a name. A header cell that is empty is named column_N, where N is its position counted from 1 (column_2 for the second column), so the column is not lost. This differs on purpose from a file with no header row at all, whose columns count from 0 (column_0 is the first). If that name is taken, a suffix is added.
  • Duplicate header names are renamed by the reader (for example Amount_duplicated_0) and the node reports a note that mentions TD-SCH-002. Fix the source file or rename the columns with a Select node.
  • Encoding. The app reads UTF-8. A file saved as Windows-1252 or Latin-1 (accented letters such as é stored as one byte) is not valid UTF-8 and stops with TD-IN-004. Choose UTF-8 (replace bad bytes) to read it anyway: the unreadable characters are replaced by a placeholder character (�), nothing is dropped. Re-saving the file as "CSV UTF-8" in Excel is the clean fix.

items.title: Excel files
items.text:
Control Shown when What it does Default Sheets Always for Excel One sheet, All sheets, or Chosen sheets. One sheet Sheet One sheet Which sheet. The list comes from the workbook; the first sheet is picked when you choose the file. First sheet Chosen Chosen sheets A checklist of the workbook's sheets. At least one must be ticked. None ticked Start row Always for Excel The row in the sheet where the table starts (the header row). Use it to skip title lines above the table. 1 Add sheet name column Always for Excel Adds a column holding the name of the sheet each row came from. Off Column name Add sheet name column is on Name of that column. SheetName
  • Excel columns keep their types (numbers are numbers, dates are dates), unlike CSV. Whole-number cells come in as decimal numbers (10.0).
  • The header is the row at Start row; rows above it are skipped. There is no control for reading Excel without a header: the First row holds field names box is only shown for CSV and Text.
  • With All sheets or Chosen sheets, every sheet is read with the same Start row and stacked following the Columns rule. Sheets with different layouts produce mostly-empty columns, as in the example below. Use Must match to be told, or read the odd sheet on its own.
  • A folder or pattern of workbooks reads the chosen sheet (or all sheets) of each workbook. The sheet list shown in the dock comes from the first workbook.
  • Excel files are read completely, even while you edit. A very large workbook is slow to open for this reason; Parquet or CSV is much faster.
  • A workbook that is locked by another program stops with TD-IN-002.

items.title: Parquet files
items.text: No type-specific controls. Parquet files carry their own column types, which are kept. Folder and pattern settings, Output filename as field, Read all columns as text and Row limit all work. Parquet is the fastest format to read and the one to prefer for large intermediate files.

items.title: JSON and JSON Lines files
items.text:
Control What it does Default Nested values How to treat a column that holds a list or a record (for example "tags": ["x","y"] or "addr": {"city": "Oslo"}). As text turns it into a JSON text value. Keep as is leaves it as a nested value. As text
  • JSON must be a file containing a list of records ([{"id": 1, ...}, {...}]). The whole file is read at once.
  • JSON Lines (.ndjson, .jsonl) has one record per line and is read without loading the whole file first.
  • Column types come from the data (1 is a whole number, 10.5 a decimal).

items.title: SQLite and DuckDB databases
items.text:
A database section appears with the note "Read-only. One SELECT statement. The database is never modified."

Control What it does Default Read Table or SQL query. Table Table (with a Reload table list icon button) The table or view to read. The list is filled from the database and the first one is chosen for you. Click the reload button after the database changes. First table Query A single SELECT statement, for example SELECT vendor, SUM(amt) AS total FROM payments GROUP BY vendor. Empty
  • The database is opened read-only. A statement that tries to change data, or use files, is refused. Only one statement is allowed (a second one after a ; is refused).
  • Row limit is applied inside the query (as a LIMIT).
  • A database source takes exactly one file. Giving it a folder or pattern is an error.
  • A database that is open for writing in another program cannot be read: you get TD-IN-002 with the message "the database is open for writing in another program".
  • SQLite and DuckDB files are read whole, even while editing.

items.title: Worked examples
items.text:
1. One CSV file. Source inv.csv:

Invoice,Amount,Date
INV-001,100.50,2025-01-03
INV-002,2000,2025-01-04
INV-003,,2025-01-05

Output (note that everything is text, and the empty amount is null):

Invoice Amount Date INV-001 100.50 2025-01-03 INV-002 2000 2025-01-04 INV-003 null 2025-01-05

With Row limit set to 2 and Output filename as field on, you would get only the first two rows plus a FileName column holding inv.csv.

2. A folder of monthly files with a changed layout. Source is a folder containing part_1.csv, part_2.csv, part_10.csv, a leftover ~$part_3.csv (Excel lock file) and notes.txt. part_10.csv has an extra Region column.

part_1.csv: Invoice,Amount / A1,10 / A2,20 part_2.csv: Invoice,Amount / A3,30 part_10.csv: Invoice,Amount,Region / A4,40,North

Settings: Type CSV, Columns = Union by name, Output filename as field on. The lock file and notes.txt are ignored. Files are stacked in natural order (1, 2, 10). Output:

Invoice Amount Region FileName A1 10 null part_1.csv A2 20 null part_1.csv A3 30 null part_2.csv A4 40 North part_10.csv

The Files read table shows part_1.csv "missing 1", part_2.csv "missing 1", part_10.csv "+1 column", and the node tooltip reads 3 files, 3 differ (first: part_1.csv: missing Region). With Columns = Must match, the same folder stops with: The files have different columns: 'part_10.csv' differs at 'Region'. (TD-SCH-011).

3. One workbook, two chosen sheets. book.xlsx has sheets Jan (Invoice, Amount), Feb (Invoice, Amount, Note) and Notes. Settings: Type Excel, Sheets = Chosen sheets with Jan and Feb ticked, Add sheet name column on. Output:

Invoice Amount Note SheetName A1 10.0 null Jan A2 20.0 null Jan B1 30.0 late Feb

If the real table on a sheet starts below a title (say the headers are in row 3), set Start row to 3.
