4. A database query. Type SQLite, Read = SQL query, with payments holding (1, Acme, 10.5), (2, Beta, 20.0), (3, Acme, 5.0) and the query SELECT vendor, SUM(amt) AS total FROM payments GROUP BY vendor ORDER BY vendor:

vendor total Acme 15.5 Beta 20.0

5. A JSON file with nested values. [{"id":1,"name":"A","tags":["x","y"],"addr":{"city":"Oslo"}}, {"id":2,"name":"B","tags":[],"addr":{"city":"Rome"}}], with Nested values = As text:

id name tags addr 1 A ["x","y"] {"city":"Oslo"} 2 B [] {"city":"Rome"}

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Live preview shows 100 rows; Run reads all rows. See Live preview and Run. CSV, Parquet and JSON Lines are read lazily while you edit, so opening a workflow with big files stays quick.
  • No row cap. There is no fixed limit on rows or file size. The practical limit is memory: Excel, JSON and database sources are loaded whole. The folder limit is Max files (10,000 by default).
  • Empty file. An empty file (no header and no rows) stops with TD-IN-005, or is skipped when Bad file is Skip and report. A file with a header and no rows is read as a table with no rows.
  • Nulls. Empty CSV cells and missing columns are null. They are not zeros or empty strings.
  • Types differ across files. With Union by name: numbers combine, everything else becomes text for that column, and the Files read table marks the files "types differ".
  • Errors deep inside a file body are found late. With Skip and report, the first 2,000 rows of each CSV, text or JSON Lines file are test-read, so a bad byte or an over-long row there skips (and names) that file. An invalid byte or a row with too many fields further down is found only when all rows are read, and it still stops the run. Reading every row of every file just to check them would cost a full extra pass. When it happens with several files, the error names the file when it can find it, otherwise it says "one of the N input files".
  • Files that disappear. If the source path is missing the node is marked invalid and its tooltip says so ("File '...' does not exist" or the TD-IN-001 message). The app logs this a few times, then stops repeating itself.
  • Workflow opened later. When a saved workflow is opened, File Input checks that the file, sheet and columns still match what was saved and warns you about missing or new columns and changed types.
  • Column order. Columns follow the first file's order; columns found only in later files follow, in the order first seen; Filename and Sheet name columns come last.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text:
The node tooltip shows the plain message. When you Run, the error list shows the code, a plain-language explanation and the fix.

Code What it means What to do TD-IN-001 The file was not found, or the folder/pattern matched no files (No files in '...' match ...). Check the path; check that the drive or network share is reachable; check Include and Exclude. TD-IN-002 The file is open in another program, or access is denied. Close the file in Excel (or whichever program), or ask for permission to the folder. TD-IN-003 The chosen sheet does not exist in the workbook. Pick one of the available sheets in the node settings. TD-IN-004 The file is not UTF-8 text. Set Encoding to UTF-8 (replace bad bytes), or save the file again as "CSV UTF-8". TD-IN-005 The file is empty. Check the export that made it finished, then reload. TD-IN-006 The file is not a readable Excel workbook (damaged or not really Excel). Open it in Excel and save it again as .xlsx. If it is really text, rename it .csv and set Type to CSV. TD-IN-007 Some rows have more fields than the header. Check the Delimiter; make sure values that contain the delimiter are quoted. TD-IN-010 The data in a file could not be read; the details name the column when known. Check the file Type and Delimiter. TD-IN-011 The input file could not be opened. Check the path and your access rights. TD-IN-012 The source matches more files than Max files (10,000 by default). Narrow the Include pattern or the folder, or raise Max files. TD-IN-013 The database could not be read as asked (unknown table, not a single SELECT, a statement that tries to change data). Check the table name; use one SELECT. TD-IN-014 The File Input settings need attention. Examples: Choose a file, folder or pattern., Choose a table., Write a SELECT query., Choose at least one sheet., Database sources take exactly one file, not a folder or pattern, or every file was skipped. Open File Input and fix the named setting. TD-SCH-010 The added filename or sheet-name column has the same name as a column already in the data. Change Column name. TD-SCH-011 Columns is Must match and files have different columns. Use Union by name, or fix the odd file the message names.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Put one File Input per source and give the real work to other nodes. A File Input followed by a Select node that sets the types is the standard start.
  • For a folder of exports, turn on Output filename as field. Later you can see which file a suspicious row came from.
  • Keep Columns on Union by name while you explore, and switch to Must match once the process is stable so a changed layout stops the run instead of quietly adding empty columns.
  • Check the Files read table after pointing at a folder. Make sure the file count is what you expect, and that no file says "skipped".
  • Prefer D:\data\2025-*.csv over a folder if the folder also holds files you do not want.
  • Convert large CSV inputs to Parquet once (File Output, Parquet) and read the Parquet afterwards.

Back to the Input and Output node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: File Output writes the table it receives to a file on disk. It writes CSV, a custom-delimited text file, Excel, Parquet, JSON, JSON Lines (NDJSON) or Arrow IPC. It does not change the data.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• You want the result of the workflow as a file you can open in Excel or hand to someone.
  • You want to save an intermediate result in a fast format (Parquet) to read back with File Input.
  • You want to export an exception list from an audit node.

For an audit workpaper (Summary, exception list with tick marks, run log, workflow and file fingerprints in one Excel file), use Workpaper Output instead; see Workpapers.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Direction Carries Input (one socket on the left) Input The table to write. (none) Output File Output has no output socket. It is an end point.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The Config Dock has two sections.

Destination

Control What it does Default File (text box) with a Browse for save location icon button The full path of the file to create, for example D:\out\exceptions.csv. The folder must already exist. The browse button opens a Save dialog filtered to the current format (for Excel the filter is *.xlsx only). Empty (placeholder "Enter file path")

Typing a path changes the Format for you when the extension is recognised:

Extension Format picked .csv, .txt CSV .xlsx, .xls Excel (a typed .xls is changed to .xlsx, see below) .parquet Parquet .json JSON .ndjson NDJSON .ipc, .arrow Arrow IPC

Other extensions (for example .jsonl or .tsv) leave the format unchanged. The write is always based on the Format setting, not on the extension, so a file called report.xlsx with Format CSV would contain CSV text.

Format

Control Shown for What it does Default Format Always One of CSV, Excel, Parquet, JSON, NDJSON, Arrow IPC, Custom delimited. CSV Delimiter CSV and Custom delimited The separator between values; a single character. A blank box means a comma. , Encoding: Include BOM CSV and Custom delimited Writes a byte-order mark at the start of the file so that Excel recognises UTF-8 text. Off Compression Parquet only The Parquet compression: Snappy, Zstandard, Gzip, LZ4 or None. The control is hidden for every other format. Snappy

What each format writes:

Format What you get CSV A text file with a header row and one line per row. UTF-8. Empty (null) values are written as nothing between the separators. The Delimiter and BOM settings apply. Custom delimited The same as CSV, for any separator (for example \| or ;). Pick the extension yourself (for example .txt); typing .txt switches the Format to CSV, which writes the same bytes. Excel A new .xlsx workbook with one sheet named Sheet1. The header row is bold with a light fill, frozen, and has filter buttons. Numbers, dates and times are real Excel numbers and dates, empty values are blank cells, and text is never treated as a formula (a value starting with = stays text). Column widths are set from the data. Parquet A compressed, typed binary file. Fast and compact; keeps column types. Compressed with Snappy unless you pick another Compression (Zstandard, Gzip, LZ4, or None for no compression). Snappy is the default; choose another only if the program that reads the file asks for it. JSON One JSON document: a list of records, [{"Invoice":"A1","Amount":10.5}, ...]. The whole table is built in memory first. NDJSON JSON Lines: one record per line. Arrow IPC An Arrow file that other data tools read quickly; keeps column types.

Excel is .xlsx only. The writer cannot produce the old .xls format. When you type a path that ends in .xls and leave the field, the dock changes it to .xlsx and shows the new name; the Save dialog only offers *.xlsx. An old workflow file that still holds an .xls name for Excel output does not write a wrong file: the Run stops before anything is written, asking for a name that ends in .xlsx (see TD-OUT-015 below).

Streaming is not an option. CSV, Parquet, NDJSON and Arrow IPC are always written in a streaming way (a table bigger than memory can still be written), so there is no switch for it. Workflow files saved by an earlier version that carry a streaming setting still open; the setting is ignored. A file that stored no compression (or an empty one) is read as Snappy. An unknown compression name in a hand-edited file stops the Run with a message that lists the valid choices.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
The table arriving at File Output:

Invoice Amount A1 10.5 A2 null

With Format CSV the file contains:

Invoice,Amount
A1,10.5
A2,

With Delimiter ; and Include BOM on, the same data is written as Invoice;Amount, A1;10.5, A2; preceded by the UTF-8 byte-order mark. With JSON it is [{"Invoice":"A1","Amount":10.5},{"Invoice":"A2","Amount":null}], and with NDJSON it is two lines, one record each.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• It only writes on Run. While you edit, nothing is written and the node produces no output. After you press Run workflow the file appears. See Live preview and Run.
  • The whole table is written, not the 100-row preview.
  • An existing file is overwritten without asking for CSV, Custom delimited, Parquet, JSON, NDJSON and Arrow IPC. Excel is written to a temporary file and then moved into place, so a failed Excel write does not damage an existing workbook.
  • The folder is not created. If the folder does not exist, the Run stops with TD-OUT-001. Create it first.
  • Nothing connected. With no input the node shows the tooltip "Input is not connected" and the Run stops with TD-OUT-006.
  • No path. The Run stops with the message File Output: choose an output path.
  • Excel is .xlsx only. A file name ending in .xls is refused (TD-OUT-015) with Excel selected; rename it to .xlsx.
  • Excel limits. An Excel sheet holds at most 1,048,575 data rows and 16,384 columns. A larger table is refused, never cut short (TD-OUT-013 for rows, TD-OUT-011 for columns). Write it as CSV or Parquet instead, or select fewer columns first.
  • Table with no columns cannot be written as Excel.
  • JSON loads the entire table into memory before writing.
  • Nested values (lists, records) are not suitable for CSV. Convert them to text first.
  • Dates in Excel are real Excel dates formatted yyyy-mm-dd; whole numbers use #,##0 and decimals #,##0.00. A text cell longer than Excel's 32,767-character limit is shortened.
  • Empty text and missing values are both written as blank cells, because Excel cannot store an empty string; reading the file back gives blanks for both.
  • Leading zeros survive CSV (they are text in the file) but Excel will drop them when you open the CSV and Excel guesses it is a number. Write the file as Excel or open the CSV with column type Text.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text: Code What it means What to do TD-OUT-001 The output folder does not exist. Create the folder, or choose an existing one. TD-OUT-002 The file cannot be written: it is open in Excel or another program, or it is read-only. Close the file, choose a different name, or clear the read-only flag. TD-OUT-003 Excel export is not available in this installation (the Excel writer component is missing). Export as CSV or Parquet instead, or reinstall the application. TD-OUT-004 The path is not a valid file name (unsupported characters, or a folder was given). Remove characters such as < > : " \| ? *, keep the path short, and choose a file, not a folder. TD-OUT-005 The disk is full. Free space or write to another drive. TD-OUT-006 Nothing is connected to this output. Connect the node whose result you want to save. TD-OUT-011 The table has more than 16,384 columns, the Excel maximum. Select fewer columns before writing. TD-OUT-013 The table has more than 1,048,575 data rows, which an Excel sheet cannot hold. Save as CSV or Parquet instead. TD-OUT-014 Excel could not create the workbook (for example, unusable cell content). Shorten or fix the offending text and try again. TD-OUT-015 Excel output was given a file name ending in .xls. The writer only creates .xlsx files. Change the name to end in .xlsx.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Write exception lists as Excel for reviewers and as Parquet for anything another workflow will read back.
  • Give each output a dated name by hand; File Output never adds a date or version to the name.
  • If Excel shows strange characters when you open a CSV, switch on Include BOM.
  • If you open the CSV in Excel and amounts look wrong, check the regional list separator: many European setups expect ; as the delimiter.

Back to the Input and Output node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text:
Workpaper Output writes the exceptions of one audit test as a formatted Excel workpaper of four sheets: Summary (engagement, objective, results tied to the exception list by formulas, conclusion, source files with SHA-256), Exceptions (the rows, with a tick-mark drop-down and a comment column), Run log and Workflow (what ran, with what, and every step's settings). It is the evidence file you attach to your working papers. It does not change the data and has no output socket.

The full description of the sheets, the rules and the limits is in Workpapers. This section is the node's reference.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• You ran an audit node (Duplicates, Gaps, Benford, Sample, Risk Filters) and need a file for the engagement file with space for tick marks and comments.
  • You need a reviewer to be able to check which data you used (file fingerprints) and what steps produced the result (the Workflow sheet).
  • You want one workpaper per test. For a one-page overview of the whole last run, use File > Export Workpaper... instead.

If you only want the rows in a file, use File Output.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text:
Socket Direction Carries E Exceptions (input 1) Input The rows to list. Required. Typically the Duplicates, Gaps or Flagged output of an audit node. P Population (input 2) Input Everything that was tested; counted for the population and its value. Optional. S Summary (input 3) Input The one-row Summary of the audit node: the test name, the rule, the status and the counts. Optional; lets the workpaper reconcile its exception count with the test's. (none) Output Workpaper Output has no output socket. It is an end point.

Without E the node is red with the tooltip "Connect the Exceptions input". A connected P or S that has failed upstream turns the node red as well ("Population input has no data" / "Summary input has no data"); it is never ignored.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The Config Dock has six sections. The header shows the chips xlsx, the row limit and the "If it exists" choice. Empty Engagement boxes use Preferences (Edit > Settings > General > Engagement), shown in grey inside the box.

File

Control What it does Default File with a Browse for save location icon button The .xlsx workbook to write. The folder must exist. Empty (placeholder "Enter file path (.xlsx)") If it exists New version writes name (2).xlsx and keeps the old file; Replace overwrites; Stop with error refuses (TD-OUT-010). New version

Engagement (can be collapsed)

Control What it does Default Reference Your workpaper reference (placeholder "e.g. C.3.1"). Empty Client, Engagement, Period Header of the Summary. Empty, then Preferences Prepared by The preparer. Empty, then Preferences, then your Windows user name Prepared on YYYY-MM-DD; an invalid date stops the Run (TD-OUT-012). Empty = the day of the Run (placeholder "today (YYYY-MM-DD)") Logo with a Browse for logo image icon button PNG or JPG for the top right of the Summary. Empty, then Preferences

Test

Control What it does Default Test name Title of the workpaper and "Test performed". Empty (the S input's test name is used) Objective, Procedure Several lines each. Empty ones become yellow cells for you to fill in. Empty Criteria The rule applied. Empty (the S input's rule, or "Not provided - complete manually")

Values

Control What it does Default Amount column Column of the Exceptions input to total (number, or text holding amounts such as 1,234.50). Tooltip: "Column summed for the value statistics". None Decimals Decimal places (0 to 6) shown for values. 2

Sheets

Control What it does Default Row limit The most exceptions listed in the workbook, 1 to 1,048,574. More rows go to a CSV file next to the workbook, and the workpaper says so. 100,000 Exceptions sheet Name of the listing sheet (cleaned to Excel's rules, 31 characters). Exceptions Include run log Adds the Run log sheet. On Include workflow Adds the Workflow sheet. On

Sources (collapsed by default)

Control What it does Default Extra source files One path per line: files read outside the workflow. They are listed and hashed on the Summary. Empty

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
A File Input reads payments.csv (10 payments). Duplicates with Key columns vendor, invoice_no, amount finds 6 rows in 3 groups. Connect Duplicates' Duplicates output to E, the File Input to P and Duplicates' Summary output to S. Set File to D:\audit\duplicate_payments.xlsx, Test name to "Duplicate vendor payments" and Amount column to amount, then press Run workflow.

The Summary of the workbook reads, in part:

Measure Rows Value % of population rows % of population value Basis Population tested 10 14,196.50 Counted from the Population input Exceptions found 6 12,861.00 60.00% 90.59% Counted from the Exceptions input Exceptions listed in this workbook 6 12,861.00 All exceptions are listed Reconciliation to test result Agrees to the test node (6 exceptions)

The Exceptions sheet lists the 6 rows with empty Tick mark and Auditor comment columns for you. Run it a second time and duplicate_payments (2).xlsx appears next to the first one. See the worked example in Workpapers for every sheet.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• It only writes on Run. While you edit, nothing is written and the node produces no output.
  • Never overwrites by accident. With New version a second Run makes a numbered copy. The workbook is built in a temporary folder and moved into place last, so a failed Run leaves no half-written file.
  • A file open in Excel stops a Replace with TD-OUT-002.
  • More exceptions than the Row limit: the workbook lists the first rows with a red "TRUNCATED" banner and writes every row to <name>_exceptions_full.csv next to it. Nothing is dropped silently.
  • Text starting with =, +, - or @ is stored as text, never as a formula.
  • No recorded run (Preferences > Record every run off): the Run log sheet is left out and the Summary says why.
  • Big lists are slow. About 500,000 rows take 35 to 45 seconds, more than the 30 second limit per step; lower the Row limit (see Limits and performance).
  • From the command line the Run log sheet is left out (the command-line run installs no run-record source). If the file exists is obeyed there too, --output-dir and --param can redirect the workbook, and Source files follow --input-dir; see The command line and Workpapers.
  • The workpaper node is not a way to write the whole table: use File Output for that.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text:
Code What it means What to do TD-OUT-001 The output folder does not exist. Create it, or choose an existing folder. TD-OUT-002 The workbook is open in Excel or read-only. Close it, or choose another name. TD-OUT-003 The Excel writer component is missing from this installation. Reinstall, or use CSV or Parquet. TD-OUT-010 A workpaper with this name already exists and If it exists is Stop with error. Choose another name or set New version. TD-OUT-011 The Exceptions input has more than 16,381 columns (Excel's 16,384 less three). Select fewer columns first. TD-OUT-012 The settings are not valid: no file, a file not ending in .xlsx, or Prepared on not YYYY-MM-DD. Fix the named setting. TD-OUT-014 Excel could not create the workbook (a sheet name or a cell it refuses). Rename the Exceptions sheet or shorten the text. TD-RUN-001 The step took more than 30 seconds. Lower the Row limit; check the file before running again.

The node also shows "Workpaper Output has no output file; choose one before running." when File is empty.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Fill in Preferences > Engagement once and leave the node's Engagement section empty.
  • Connect P and S whenever you can: the population, the rule and the reconciliation line then fill themselves in.
  • Keep New version while you work: your annotated copy is never overwritten.
  • Add a Comment to the canvas to explain a step; it is copied to the Workflow sheet.

Back to the Input and Output node index.

items.title: Join nodes
items.text:
These nodes combine two or more tables. Pick the one that matches the question you are asking.

If you want to... Use Put the rows of one table under the rows of another (two inputs) Append Stack any number of tables, with control over how columns line up Union Look up matching rows by an exact key, and see what matched, what only the left has and what only the right has Join Match two lists on keys plus an amount (with a tolerance) and a date window, and report the differences Reconcile Match names or descriptions that are almost, but not exactly, the same Fuzzy Match

items.title: Nodes in this family
items.text:
• Join

    Combines two tables on matching key columns and also gives the unmatched rows from each side (outputs L, J, R).

  • Append

    Puts the rows of a second table underneath the first.

  • Union

    Stacks two or more tables, matching columns by name or by a mapping you set.

  • Reconcile

    Matches two tables on keys plus an amount tolerance and/or date window; gives matched pairs, both unmatched sides and a summary.

  • Fuzzy Match

    Pairs similar text (such as vendor and supplier names) from two tables by similarity score.

items.title: Before you start: left, right and the 100-row preview
items.text:
• Left and right. Append, Join, Reconcile and Fuzzy Match have two input sockets. The first socket (top) is the left input and the second socket is the right input. "Input 1" in an error message means the left one and "Input 2" the right one. Swapping them changes which side's columns come first and which outputs are "left only" and "right only".
  • Output sockets are lettered. Join has L, J, R. Reconcile has M, L, R, S. Fuzzy Match has M, L, R. Connect each socket to the node you want to receive that output. The summary line at the top of the Config Dock spells out what each letter means.
  • Live preview versus Run. While you edit, each input is cut to its first 100 rows, so a match that needs row 101 will not appear in the preview. Run uses all rows. See Live preview and Run.
  • Row order is not guaranteed. After a join or match, rows may come out in a different order from run to run. If order matters, add a Sort node (see Preparation nodes) after it.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Append puts the rows of the right input underneath the rows of the left input. It always handles exactly two inputs.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• You have two tables with the same layout (this year and last year) and want one table.
  • You want to place two tables side by side (Horizontal), row for row.

For more than two inputs, or when you want to line up columns that have different names, use Union.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input 1 (left, top) The first table. Its rows come first. Input 2 (right, bottom) The second table. Output Out The two tables combined.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
One section, Append, with the note "Vertical requires identical schemas."

Control What it does Default Method Diagonal (relaxed): stack the rows; match columns by name; a column missing on one side is filled with empty values; a column with different types on the two sides is widened to a type that holds both (for example whole numbers and decimals become decimals; numbers and text become text). Vertical (same columns): stack the rows, but only if both tables have exactly the same columns and types; otherwise stop with an error. Horizontal (side by side): put the right table's columns next to the left table's columns, row by row. Diagonal (strict): like Diagonal (relaxed), but columns that appear on both sides must have exactly the same type. Diagonal (relaxed)

The chip in the Config Dock shows the method and "rows stacked, left then right".

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Left input (open invoices):

Invoice Amount A1 100.0 A2 250.0 A3 75.0

Right input (payments, with an extra column):

Invoice Amount Paid A1 100.0 Y A3 80.0 N A9 10.0 Y

With Method = Diagonal (relaxed), the output Out is:

Invoice Amount Paid A1 100.0 null A2 250.0 null A3 75.0 null A1 100.0 Y A3 80.0 N A9 10.0 Y

With Vertical (same columns) the same two tables stop with TD-SHAPE-004: schemas differ (right-only: ['Paid']). Try 'diagonal_relaxed'.

With Horizontal, two tables of the same length, Invoice (A1, A2) and Paid (Y, N), give:

Invoice Paid A1 Y A2 N

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Row cap: none. The live preview shows 100 rows; Run appends everything. See Live preview and Run.
  • Empty input: an empty table contributes no rows; its columns still count for Diagonal methods.
  • Nulls stay null.
  • Different types. Diagonal (relaxed) widens (a column of numbers on one side and text on the other becomes text, so 3 and "x" coexist). Vertical and Diagonal (strict) refuse.
  • Horizontal needs the same number of rows on both sides and different column names on both sides. Otherwise it stops (see errors).
  • The Vertical error says what differs: columns only on one side (left-only: [...], right-only: [...]), a column with different types ('Amount' is Int64 on the left but String on the right), or the same columns in a different order.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text: Code What it means What to do TD-SHAPE-004 Vertical was chosen and the two tables are not identical in columns and types. Choose Diagonal (relaxed), or make the inputs match with Select nodes. TD-SCH-004 Diagonal (strict) was chosen and a shared column has different types, or the columns differ. Make both inputs have the same columns and types, or use Diagonal (relaxed). TD-SCH-005 Horizontal: the two tables have different numbers of rows. Make sure both come from the same step, or use Diagonal. TD-SCH-002 Horizontal: a column name appears on both sides. Rename one of them with a Select node first. TD-SHAPE-005 An input has no data ("Input 1 has no data"). Connect and fix the upstream node.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Use Append for "this year plus last year". If the second table has a column the first lacks, keep Diagonal (relaxed) and check the new column for empty cells in the first table's rows.
  • To keep track of where each row came from, add a column to each side first (for example a Formula that writes "2024" or "2025").

Back to the Join node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Fuzzy Match pairs rows whose text is similar but not identical: Acme Inc. and ACME, Inc, Initech LLC and Initec. Each pair gets a score between 0 and 1 (1 is identical), and only pairs at or above your minimum are kept.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• Vendor names typed differently in two systems (vendor master to payments).
  • Employee names, customer names, addresses and descriptions where an exact Join misses real matches.

Use Join or Reconcile when the key is exact. Fuzzy results are suggestions: review them.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input 1 (left) The first list. Input 2 (right) The second list. Output M Matched. Match_ID, Match_Score, then every left column, then every right column (a right column with the same name as a left column gets _right). Output L Left unmatched. Left rows with no pair at or above the minimum score (and rows with empty text). Output R Right unmatched. The same for the right.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Compare

Control What it does Default Left text / Right text The text columns to compare. Only text columns are listed. Empty Algorithm Jaro-Winkler: gives extra credit to names that start the same way; good for names. Levenshtein ratio: counts the single-character edits between the texts; good for codes and descriptions. Jaro-Winkler Minimum score Pairs scoring below this are dropped. 0.01 to 1.0 in steps of 0.01. Hint: "1.0 is identical; pairs scoring below are dropped." 0.85 Ignore Inc/Ltd/LLC (checkbox) Removes company-form words before comparing: inc, incorporated, ltd, limited, llc, plc, corp, corporation, co, company, gmbh, ag, sa, pty, pvt, bv, nv, lp, llp. On Pairs One to one: each row is used at most once; the best-scoring pairs win. Best per left row: each left row gets its best right row (a right row can be used several times). All pairs: every pair at or above the minimum. One to one

Hint on the form: "Text is lower-cased and punctuation is ignored before comparing. Empty text never matches."

Speed

Control What it does Default Block on Only rows that share a "block" are compared, which keeps large inputs fast. First characters: rows must start with the same first few letters. First word: rows must share the first word. Nothing (small data): compare everything with everything. First characters Characters How many leading characters count for the block (1 to 10). Shown for First characters. 3 Must also match (list, up to 5) Extra column pairs (a Left column and a Right column) that must be equal, for example country or city. Trimmed and compared as lower-case text. Empty

Hint: "Only rows that share the block are compared, which keeps large inputs fast. Extra columns are trimmed and compared as lower-case text."

Limits & output (collapsed): "Up to 5,000,000 candidate pairs (1,000,000 with no blocking). The live preview uses the first 100 rows of each input; Run gives the full result."

How text is prepared before scoring: lower-case; every character that is not a letter or digit becomes a space; the company words above are removed (if the checkbox is on); repeated spaces are collapsed. So ACME, Inc and Acme Inc. both become acme.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Left (vendor master):

Vendor Spend Acme Inc. 100 Globex Corporation 200 Initech LLC 300 Umbrella Ltd 400

Right (suppliers):

Supplier Country ACME, Inc US Globex Corp DE Initec US Wayne Enterprises UK

Settings: Left text Vendor, Right text Supplier, defaults otherwise. Output M:

Match_ID Match_Score Vendor Spend Supplier Country 1 1.0 Acme Inc. 100 ACME, Inc US 2 1.0 Globex Corporation 200 Globex Corp DE 3 0.9714 Initech LLC 300 Initec US

Output L:

Vendor Spend Umbrella Ltd 400

Output R:

Supplier Country Wayne Enterprises UK

With Algorithm Levenshtein ratio, the third pair scores 0.8571 instead of 0.9714.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Candidate pairs: up to 5,000,000 (1,000,000 with Block on = Nothing). More stops the run. The count is made before any scoring, so it fails fast.
  • Live preview: 100 rows of each input. Run uses all rows and keeps both inputs in memory. See Live preview and Run.
  • Blocking can hide real matches. With First characters = 3, The Acme Trading Co and Acme Trading Company are never compared (they start with the and acm). Use First word, shorten Characters, remove leading words first, or use Nothing on a small table. With Nothing and a minimum of 0.7, that pair is found, with a score of 0.8333.
  • Must also match is exact (after trimming and lower-casing). A wrong spelling in the extra column also hides a match.
  • Empty text (null or only spaces and punctuation) never matches and the row goes to L or R.
  • Only text columns can be chosen. Convert numbers to text with a Select node first.
  • Ties are broken the same way every time (higher score first, then row order), so a re-run gives the same result.
  • Score is rounded to four decimals.
  • Column names. Match_ID and Match_Score are reserved: a left column with one of those names is renamed with a _2 suffix.
  • Internal names. A column named __l or __r in either input stops the node (TD-SHAPE-002); rename it first.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text: Code What it means What to do TD-SHAPE-001 "Pick the text column on both sides". Choose Left text and Right text. TD-SHAPE-004 A setting is out of range (Minimum score must be above 0 and at most 1; Characters 1 to 10; at most 5 extra match columns). Pick a value inside the range. TD-SHAPE-081 More than 5,000,000 possible pairs. Use more Characters, or add a Must also match column. TD-SHAPE-082 Block on is Nothing and the tables have more than 1,000,000 row pairs (for example 1,001 by 1,000). Turn on prefix or first-word blocking. TD-SHAPE-003 A chosen column is no longer in the input. Select the column again. TD-SHAPE-005 An input has no data. Connect and fix the upstream node.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Start at the default 0.85 and read M sorted by Match_Score. Look at the lowest scores: that is where wrong matches live. Raise the minimum until the lowest rows are right, then look at L and R for real names that were missed.
  • Add a Must also match column (country, tax number, city) to cut false matches and make large runs faster.
  • Names with a leading "The" or a title defeat prefix blocking. Use First word, or strip those words with a Find and Replace node first.
  • After matching, use the pairs in M as a mapping table and Join on Match_ID, or keep the pair list as evidence in your working paper.

Back to the Join node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Join matches the rows of two tables on one or more key columns and gives you three results at once: the rows that matched (with columns from both sides), the left rows that have no match, and the right rows that have no match. You never lose a row silently, which is what you want in an audit.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• You want to bring information from one table into another (add the vendor's country to each payment).
  • You want to find what is in one list and not in the other (invoices without payment, payments without invoice), when the keys are exactly equal.

If the keys are not exactly equal (small differences in text, amounts that must agree within a tolerance, dates that may be a few days apart), use Reconcile or Fuzzy Match.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input 1 (left, top) The left table. Input 2 (right, bottom) The right table. Output L Left only. Left rows with no matching right row. Columns: all of the left table's columns. Output J Joined. Rows that matched on the keys, with the columns you chose in Output columns (all by default). Output R Right only. Right rows with no matching left row. Columns: all of the right table's columns.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Until both inputs are connected the Config Dock says "Both inputs must be connected". Then:

Key pairs

Control What it does Default Add key pair (icon) Adds a pair: a column from the left table, an arrow, a column from the right table. Rows match when all pairs are equal. The new pair is pre-filled with the first column combination not already used. One pair is created for you: the first column of each table Each pair: Left key column, Right key column The columns that must be equal. A column that has vanished from the input is shown as name (missing). Remove key pair (icon) Deletes the pair.

Output columns ("Unchecked columns stay out of the joined output.")

Control What it does Default Auto-accept new columns (checkbox) When on, a column that newly appears upstream is ticked automatically. When off, it stays unticked until you tick it. On All / None Tick or untick every column. Column checklist, entries shown as L: name and R: name Which columns the J output contains. L: columns come from the left table, R: from the right. Everything ticked

The output columns control the J output only. L and R always carry every column of their own side.

A summary chip shows the number of keys and the number of columns, with "full outer join".

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Left (invoices):

Invoice Amount A1 100.0 A2 250.0 A3 75.0

Right (payments):

Invoice Amount Paid A1 100.0 Y A3 80.0 N A9 10.0 Y

Key pair: Invoice = Invoice. Everything ticked.

Output L (invoice A2 has no payment):

Invoice Amount A2 250.0

Output J:

Invoice Amount Amount_right Paid A1 100.0 100.0 Y A3 75.0 80.0 N

Output R (payment A9 has no invoice):

Invoice Amount_right Paid A9 10.0 Y

When both tables have a column of the same name (Amount), the right table's column is renamed Amount_right in J and R. In the Output columns list it still appears as R: Amount.

If you tick only L: Invoice and R: Paid in Output columns, J becomes:

Invoice Paid A1 Y A3 N

When the key columns have different names (InvoiceNo on the left, Ref on the right), the key appears once in J, under the left name, and in R the right-only keys also appear under the left name (InvoiceNo).

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Row cap: none in the node. The live preview shows 100 rows; Run joins everything. See Live preview and Run.
  • Exact match only. Keys are compared as they are: ABC and abc do not match, and A1 and A1 (with a space) do not match. Clean keys first (see Cleansing in Preparation nodes) or use Reconcile, which trims and ignores case.
  • Null keys never match. A left row with an empty key goes to L; a right row with an empty key goes to R.
  • One-to-many. If one left row matches several right rows, J has one row per pair, so the left row appears several times. Row counts in J can therefore be higher than either input. Check for duplicate keys with the Duplicates audit node before you join.
  • Key types must be the same. A number key against a text key is refused (see errors). Convert one side with a Select node.
  • Columns that disappear upstream are dropped from the Output columns selection. A key pair whose column no longer exists is dropped too. If you remove every key pair (or the last one disappears), Join puts the default pair back (the first column of each table) the next time it evaluates, so check the key pair after changing the inputs.
  • Renamed columns upstream. If you rename a column in a Select node placed before Join, the key pairs and selections follow the new name.
  • Row order is not guaranteed (a 1-to-many join may list the matches in any order). Add a Sort node if order matters.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text: Code What it means What to do TD-SHAPE-001 "Add at least one key pair". No pair is set (rare: the dock normally re-creates the default pair). Add a key pair. TD-TYP-002 The two key columns have different types, for example whole numbers against text. Add a Select node on one side and set the key column to the same type (usually Text). TD-SHAPE-005 An input has no data. Connect and fix the upstream node.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Join the two tables and check three numbers: rows in L, rows in J, rows in R. They should explain your totals: left rows = L + the left side of J.
  • To get a classic "left join", use J and L together with Append (Diagonal), or just use L to list the exceptions.
  • Join on several columns at once (company and invoice number) with extra key pairs rather than creating a combined key.

Back to the Join node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Reconcile compares two lists (for example the bank statement and the ledger) the way an auditor does: match on reference keys, check that the amounts agree within a tolerance, check that the dates are close enough, and then tell you what matched, what is left over on each side and how much the totals differ. It gives four outputs, including a one-row summary you can quote.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• Bank to ledger, sub-ledger to general ledger, invoices to payments, purchase orders to receipts.
  • The two sides do not agree to the cent, or the dates differ by a few days.
  • One side may have several lines for one line on the other (one invoice paid in instalments).

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input 1 (left) The first list (for example the ledger). Input 2 (right) The second list (for example the bank). Output M Matched. One row per matched pair (or per line in a group), with the left columns followed by the right columns, preceded by Match_ID, Match_Status and the differences. Output L Left unmatched. Left rows with no match, plus Unmatched_Reason. Output R Right unmatched. Right rows with no match, plus Unmatched_Reason. Output S Summary. One row with counts, totals and the net difference.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Four sections.

Match

Control What it does Default Match type (segmented buttons) 1 : 1: each left row is matched with at most one right row. 1 : N: one left row may be matched with many right rows (for example an invoice paid in several instalments). N : 1: many left rows to one right row. N : N: lines are grouped by the keys on each side and the groups are compared. Hint: "Match type controls how many times each side may be used." 1 : 1 Key pairs (list, up to 10) Each pair is a Left column and a Right column whose values must be equal. Every pair must agree for two rows to be candidates. Add pairs with the Add icon. Rows with an empty left or right column are ignored. Hint: "Keys are trimmed and compared as lower-case text. Null keys never match." Empty

Amount

Control What it does Default Left amount / Right amount Optional. The numeric (or number-like text) columns to compare. Leave both blank to match without checking amounts. Setting only one side is an error. Blank Tolerance (segmented: Amount or Percent) and Value How far apart the two amounts may be and still count as agreeing. Amount: an absolute difference (for example 0.50). Percent: a percentage of the left amount (for example 1 means 1%). Hint: "Leave both amounts blank to skip amount matching. Percent is of the left amount." Amount, 0

Date window (not shown for N : N)

Control What it does Default Left date / Right date Optional date columns (real dates, date-times, or text that reads as a date). Leave both blank to skip date matching. Setting only one side is an error. Blank Window (days) The largest allowed gap, in days, between the two dates (0 to 3,650). Hint: "Leave both dates blank to skip date matching." 0

Limits & output (collapsed): "Up to 5,000,000 candidate pairs. The live preview uses the first 100 rows of each input; Run gives the full result."

items.title: What the outputs contain
items.text:
M (matched). Columns, in order: Match_ID, Match_Status, Amount_Diff (only when amounts are set), Date_Gap_Days (only when dates are set), then every column of the left table, then every column of the right table. A right column with the same name as a left column gets _right added. Rows are ordered by Match_ID.

  • Match_ID numbers the matches, starting at 1. In 1:N, N:1 and N:N, all rows of one group share an ID.
  • Match_Status is Matched when no amounts are set, Within tolerance when the amounts agree, Outside tolerance when they do not. For 1:1, rows only become a match when the amounts agree, so you see Within tolerance. For 1:N, N:1 and N:N, rows are grouped by the keys and compared in total, so a group whose total is off still appears in M, marked Outside tolerance.
  • Amount_Diff is always right amount minus left amount (for a group, the group totals).
  • Date_Gap_Days is right date minus left date, in days.
  • An input column named like one of these outputs (Match_ID, Match_Status, and Amount_Diff or Date_Gap_Days when those are set) is renamed in M with a _2 suffix, for example Match_ID_2 (_3 if that name is taken too).

L and R (unmatched). The original columns plus Unmatched_Reason, one of:

Reason Meaning No candidate with the same key No row on the other side has the same key(s). (With no key pairs, the wording is "No candidate within the date window".) Candidates outside tolerance Rows with the same key exist on the other side but none agrees within the amount tolerance or date window. Candidates already matched A better candidate was used by another row (1:1 and similar).

S (summary), one row:

Column Meaning Match_Type The match type used (one_to_one, one_to_many, many_to_one, many_to_many). Left_Rows, Right_Rows Rows in each input. Matched_Groups Number of matches (distinct Match_ID). Left_Matched_Rows, Right_Matched_Rows Rows matched on each side. Left_Unmatched_Rows, Right_Unmatched_Rows Rows left over. Left_Match_Rate_Pct, Right_Match_Rate_Pct Matched rows as a percentage of rows. Left_Total, Right_Total Sum of the amount column on each side (only with amounts). Matched_Left_Total, Matched_Right_Total Sum of the matched rows on each side. Matched_Net_Difference Matched right total minus matched left total. Matched_Abs_Difference Sum of the absolute differences per match. Left_Unmatched_Total, Right_Unmatched_Total Amount in the unmatched rows. Net_Difference_Total Right_Total minus Left_Total. Within_Tolerance_Groups, Outside_Tolerance_Groups How many matches are inside / outside the tolerance.

Without amounts the total and difference columns are empty (null).

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Left, the ledger:

Ref Amount Date INV-1 100.00 2025-01-03 INV-2 250.00 2025-01-04 INV-3 75.00 2025-01-05 INV-4 40.00 2025-01-09

Right, the bank:

Ref Amount Date inv-1 100.00 2025-01-03 INV-2 (trailing space) 250.00 2025-01-06 INV-3 75.40 2025-01-05 INV-9 10.00 2025-01-09

Settings: Match type 1 : 1; key pair Ref = Ref; Left amount and Right amount = Amount; Tolerance Amount, Value 0.50; Left date and Right date = Date; Window (days) 3.

Output M:

Match_ID Match_Status Amount_Diff Date_Gap_Days Ref Amount Date Ref_right Amount_right Date_right 1 Within tolerance 0.0 0 INV-1 100.0 2025-01-03 inv-1 100.0 2025-01-03 2 Within tolerance 0.0 2 INV-2 250.0 2025-01-04 INV-2 250.0 2025-01-06 3 Within tolerance 0.4 0 INV-3 75.0 2025-01-05 INV-3 75.4 2025-01-05

Case and spaces in the keys were ignored (inv-1, INV-2). Output L:

Ref Amount Date Unmatched_Reason INV-4 40.0 2025-01-09 No candidate with the same key

Output R:

Ref Amount Date Unmatched_Reason INV-9 10.0 2025-01-09 No candidate with the same key

Output S (shown as a list for readability):

Column Value Match_Type one_to_one Left_Rows / Right_Rows 4 / 4 Matched_Groups 3 Left_Matched_Rows / Right_Matched_Rows 3 / 3 Left_Unmatched_Rows / Right_Unmatched_Rows 1 / 1 Left_Match_Rate_Pct / Right_Match_Rate_Pct 75.0 / 75.0 Left_Total / Right_Total 465.0 / 435.4 Matched_Left_Total / Matched_Right_Total 425.0 / 425.4 Matched_Net_Difference 0.4 Matched_Abs_Difference 0.4 Left_Unmatched_Total / Right_Unmatched_Total 40.0 / 10.0 Net_Difference_Total -29.6 Within_Tolerance_Groups / Outside_Tolerance_Groups 3 / 0

If you set Value to 0 and clear the dates, INV-3 (75.00 against 75.40) is no longer a match. It goes to L and R with the reason Candidates outside tolerance, and INV-4 and INV-9 keep No candidate with the same key.

A 1 : N example. Left orders O1 (300) and O2 (50); right payments O1 100, O1 200, O2 45, key Order, amounts Total and Paid, Tolerance Percent 5. M:

Match_ID Match_Status Amount_Diff Order Total Order_right Paid 1 Within tolerance 0.0 O1 300.0 O1 100.0 1 Within tolerance 0.0 O1 300.0 O1 200.0 2 Outside tolerance -5.0 O2 50.0 O2 45.0

The two O1 payments add up to 300 and are one match with two rows. O2 is 5 short, which is 10% of 50, so it is listed as Outside tolerance.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Candidate pairs: up to 5,000,000. Reconcile counts how many row pairs could possibly match before it starts. More than that stops with TD-SHAPE-072. Add key column pairs or narrow the date window.
  • Live preview: 100 rows of each input; Run uses all rows and holds both inputs in memory. See Live preview and Run.
  • Keys are converted to text, trimmed and lower-cased on both sides before comparing. 007 and 7 are different; Inv-1 and inv-1 are the same. There is no fuzziness: for that see Fuzzy Match.
  • Null keys never match.
  • Amounts may be number columns or text that holds numbers. Text amounts are read the way the Audit nodes read them: 1,234.50, 1.234,50 (European) and 1,234 are 1234.5, 1234.5 and 1234; a single comma that is not a thousands group is a decimal comma (1,50 is 1.5); (12.00) is negative; currency signs and spaces are ignored. A mixed or malformed form such as 1,2,3 is read as empty. Text that is not a number is treated as empty and cannot match when amounts are compared. Differences are compared after rounding to six decimals.
  • Date columns may be dates, date-times or text. Text should be in a standard form such as 2025-01-31; text that does not read as a date counts as empty. A date-time is reduced to its date.
  • Without key pairs you can match on dates alone (choose a date pair and a window). Without keys and without dates the node refuses to run (TD-SHAPE-071).
  • N : N ignores the date window (the date boxes are hidden) and compares groups of rows with the same key on each side by their totals.
  • Which pair wins in 1 : 1. The pairs with the smallest amount difference, then the smallest date gap, are taken first; a row can only be used once. The result is the same each time you run it.
  • Ties never depend on row order; the same inputs always give the same answer.
  • Internal names. A column named __l or __r in either input stops the node (TD-SHAPE-002); rename it first.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text: Code What it means What to do TD-SHAPE-071 "Add a key column pair or a date window". There is nothing to match on. Add a key pair, or choose a date pair. TD-SHAPE-070 "Pick the amount/date column on both sides". Only one side is set. Pick it on both sides, or on neither. TD-SHAPE-072 More than 5,000,000 possible matches. Add key column pairs or narrow the date window. TD-SHAPE-003 A chosen column is no longer in the input. Select the column again. TD-SHAPE-004 A setting is unknown or out of range (negative tolerance or window). Pick a value inside the allowed range. TD-SHAPE-050 A date column is neither a date nor text (for example numbers). Choose a date column, or convert the column first. TD-SHAPE-005 An input has no data. Connect and fix the upstream node.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Start with a tolerance of 0 and no dates to see what matches exactly; then widen the tolerance a little at a time and watch Matched_Abs_Difference and Outside_Tolerance_Groups in S.
  • The summary S is the number to put in the working paper: left total, right total, unmatched totals and the net difference all come from one place.
  • Check Unmatched_Reason. "Candidates outside tolerance" means the reference exists on both sides but the amount or date disagrees, which is usually the finding. "No candidate with the same key" means the item is missing on the other side.
  • For many-to-one cases (one bank deposit for several invoices) choose N : 1 and give amounts so that totals are compared.

Back to the Join node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Union stacks any number of tables, one under the other (the SQL "UNION ALL": all rows are kept, duplicates are not removed). It has three ways of lining up the columns.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• You have three or more tables with the same layout (twelve monthly extracts, one table per entity).
  • The tables are almost the same but a few columns are named differently, and you want to say which column lines up with which.
  • You want to stack by column position and ignore headers.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text:
Socket Carries Input (a single socket on the left that accepts any number of connections) Every connected table. Connect as many as you need to this one socket. Output (one, on the right) The stacked table.

The inputs are stacked in connection order (#1 first). The Input order section lets you change it.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The Config Dock shows "Connect at least one input" until something is connected. After that it has up to three sections.

Union mode ("How columns from the inputs are aligned.")

Control What it does Default Mode Auto by Name: columns with exactly the same name (upper/lower case matter) line up. The output has every name found, in the order first seen; a table without a column gets empty values there. Auto by Position: ignore names; the first column of each table lines up, then the second, and so on. The output uses the first table's column names; if another table is wider, the extra columns are named Extra_4, Extra_5..., and shorter tables are filled with empty values. Manual: you build the output columns yourself. Auto by Name

Input order ("Rows stack #1 first. Reorder with Up/Down or reconnect edges.")

One row per connected input, labelled with its number and where it comes from (for example #1 File Input [out 0]), with two icon buttons per row: Move input N earlier and Move input N later. Each move is an undo step ("Input Order Changed").

Column Mapping (only in Manual mode; "Align each input's column to an output. Blank = Null.")

Control What it does Header row Output, then one heading per input. Output column (text box) The name of this column in the result. One drop-down per input Which column of that input goes into this output column. (none) leaves it empty (null) for that input. Add output column (icon) Adds a row, named New_Column, New_Column_2... Remove output column (icon, per row) Removes the row.

The first time you switch to Manual, the grid is pre-filled with the Auto-by-Name result so you can adjust it. Rows with an empty or repeated output name are ignored. Edits apply about a third of a second after you stop.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Three tables:

Table 1

Invoice Amount A1 10 A2 20

Table 2 (the amount is text; has an extra column)

Invoice Amount Note B1 "30" late

Table 3 (reference column has a different name)

Ref Amount C1 5

Auto by Name gives:

Invoice Amount Note Ref A1 10 null null A2 20 null null B1 30 late null null 5 null C1

Amount is whole numbers in two tables and text in the other, so the whole column becomes text (shown as numbers here for readability). The node's tooltip says: Column 'Amount' has conflicting types (Int64, String); coerced to String. Ref is a separate column from Invoice; to line them up use Manual.

Manual with two tables, Table 1 = (Invoice, Amount) and Table 4 = (Ref, Total, Note):

Output Table 1 Table 4 Doc Invoice Ref Value Amount Total Comment (none) Note

gives

Doc Value Comment A1 10 null B1 20 x

(Table 1 supplies A1/10; Table 4 supplies B1/20/x.)

Auto by Position on the same two tables (Table 1 has two columns, Table 4 three) gives column names from Table 1 plus Extra_3:

Invoice Amount Extra_3 A1 10 null B1 20 x

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• One connected input passes through unchanged.
  • Row cap: none. The live preview shows the first 100 rows of the result; Run stacks everything. See Live preview and Run.
  • Type conflicts. When the same column (or position, or Manual row) has different types across inputs, it is converted to text for all of them, and a warning appears in the node's tooltip. Text-to-text and number-to-number needs no conversion.
  • Names are case-sensitive in Auto by Name: Amount and amount become two columns.
  • Disconnected or empty upstream nodes are skipped. If none produces data the tooltip says "Upstream nodes produced no output".
  • Manual with no valid rows falls back to the Auto-by-Name layout.
  • If stacking fails for any reason the node is marked invalid with the tooltip "Union failed" (the technical detail is in the log).
  • Adding or removing a connection while the Manual grid is open rebuilds the grid so that the new input's columns appear.

items.title: Errors and messages
items.text:
Union does not raise TD- codes. It reports on the node tooltip:

Message What it means Connect at least one input Nothing is connected. Upstream nodes produced no output The connected nodes have errors or no data; fix them first. Union failed The tables could not be stacked. Check the column types; look in the log for details. Column 'X' has conflicting types (...); coerced to String. A warning, not an error. The column was turned into text.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Prefer Auto by Name when the tables come from the same system. Use Manual when the tables come from different systems and the same field has different names.
  • To record which table a row came from, add a source column to each input before the Union (a Formula writing the table name), or have File Input add the filename.
  • If you only have two tables, Append is simpler.

Back to the Join node index.

items.title: Preparation nodes
items.text:
Preparation nodes clean, reshape and enrich a table before you analyse it. They are the first nodes you place after an input node: fix the types, remove the rubbish, add the columns you need, then pass the table on to joins, audit tests or reports.

This page covers all 16 Preparation nodes in the palette.

items.title: Nodes in this family
items.text:
• Cleansing

    Per-column clean-up: trim, change case, handle empty values, convert type.

  • Filter

    Keeps or drops rows that meet conditions you set.

  • Formula

    Creates or changes columns from SQL-style expressions.

  • Aggregate

    Collapses rows into groups and totals, counts or averages each group.

  • Select

    Chooses, renames, reorders and changes the type of columns.

  • Sort

    Orders rows by one or more columns.

  • Unique

    Keeps the first row for each key and sends the repeats out separately.

  • Split

    Divides the rows into two sets by percent (an estimation and a validation set).

  • Rows

    Builds a series of rows from ranges, patterns or literal values.

  • Normalize

    Tidies column names: trim, collapse spaces, apply one case rule. (Shares the Select icon.)

  • Record ID

    Adds a numbered column, optionally restarting per group.

  • Select Records

    Keeps the first, last, a range, the largest or smallest rows, and sends the rest out separately.

  • Find and Replace

    Applies an ordered list of text or pattern replacements to chosen columns.

  • Date Helper

    Adds date parts, fiscal periods, day differences and business-day figures.

  • Text to Columns

    Splits one text column on a delimiter or pattern into columns or rows.

  • Multi-Field Formula

    Applies one expression to many ticked columns at once.

items.title: Preview uses 100 rows, Run uses all rows
items.text:
While you edit a node, the app shows a live preview so you can see the effect of every change straight away. To stay fast on big files, the preview reads only the first 100 rows of each input and shows at most 100 rows of each output. When you press Run, the workflow processes every row.

What this means for you:

  • A preview that looks right proves your settings work on the first 100 rows, not on the whole file. A value that only appears on row 40,000 (an unreadable date, a text amount, a duplicate) will not show in the preview.
  • Counts shown in the preview (for example "12 cells change (first 100 rows)") are counts for the sample only.
  • Settings that depend on row position or on the whole table (Select Records, Record ID, Split, Unique, Aggregate totals) show sample results while you edit, and whole-table results after Run. Rely on the Run result.
  • A node can pass the preview and still fail on Run when a bad value sits in the later rows (for example a plain CAST meeting a text value). Use the forgiving TRY_CAST where data is untidy.

Every node below links back to this section.

items.title: Common behaviour
items.text:
• One table in, one or two tables out. Every Preparation node has a single input socket on the left. Filter, Unique, Split and Select Records have two output sockets, labelled on the node (T and F, Unique and Duplicates, E and V, S and R). The others have one output.
  • No input, no settings. If nothing is connected, or the upstream node has no data yet, the Config Dock shows "No incoming data available" and the node reports TD-SHAPE-005 ("Input 1 has no data"). Connect and fix the upstream node first.
  • Settings apply as you edit. Text boxes wait about a third of a second after you stop typing before the node recomputes. Each real change is one step in Undo/Redo.
  • Columns that disappear. If a column you chose is no longer in the input (for example it was renamed upstream), the node reports TD-SHAPE-003 or, for some nodes, skips that setting. A chip or the message names the column.
  • CSV and Excel text. Files read as CSV usually give you text columns, even when the values look like numbers or dates. Many nodes offer fewer choices for text columns. Convert the type first with Select (Data Type column) or with TRY_CAST in a Formula.
  • Nulls (empty cells) stay empty unless a node says otherwise.

items.title: Reading the Config Dock
items.text: The Config Dock is the panel that shows the settings of the selected node. Buttons are icon-only: hover over one to see its name. The paired All and None buttons in Select are the only text buttons.

items.title: Writing SQL expressions
items.text:
Filter (Expression mode), Formula and Multi-Field Formula accept SQL expressions. You do not write a whole query, only the expression:

  • Formula and Multi-Field Formula take an expression that produces a value, for example [Amount] * 1.2.
  • Filter takes a condition that is true or false, for example [Amount] > 100. Think of it as the text after WHERE.

Expressions run on the DuckDB engine, so DuckDB's SQL functions are available.

items.title: Column names: square brackets (Formula and Filter)
items.text:
Put a column name in square brackets: [Invoice Amount]. Spaces in names are fine. Matching ignores upper and lower case, and spaces just inside the brackets are ignored, so [invoice amount] and [ Invoice Amount ] both find Invoice Amount.

  • Only names that exist in the input (and, in Formula, columns created by earlier formulas in the same node) are recognised. An unknown name is not a column, and the engine reports an error such as Referenced column "nope" not found.
  • Brackets inside quoted text are left alone: '[x]' is the text [x].
  • Text goes in single quotes: 'paid'. Double quotes are accepted for text too ("paid" is read as 'paid'), because only [...] means a column.
  • Inside text, write a quote as two quotes: 'O''Brien'.
  • Multi-Field Formula does not use brackets. It uses {col} and {name}; see Multi-Field Formula.

items.title: What you can write
items.text:
Any single SQL expression: arithmetic (+ - * / %), comparisons (= <> < > <= >=), AND / OR / NOT, CASE WHEN ... THEN ... ELSE ... END, IN (...), BETWEEN a AND b, LIKE / ILIKE, IS NULL, casts (CAST(x AS ...), TRY_CAST(x AS ...), x::DATE), || to join text, and DuckDB's functions.

Two spelling conveniences are translated for you:

You type Meaning Works in strip(x) the same as trim(x) Filter and Formula x in_between (a, b) the same as x BETWEEN a AND b Filter only. In a Formula it is a syntax error; write BETWEEN a AND b.

In the editor, press Ctrl+Space to open suggestions for functions, keywords and column names.

items.title: Useful functions
items.text:
Every expression below was run against a small sample table (a text amt column such as "1,200.50", a text posted column such as "2024-01-31").

Goal Expression Result Trim spaces TRIM([name]) " Acme Ltd " becomes Acme Ltd Upper case UPPER(TRIM([name])) ACME LTD Join text and a number CONCAT(TRIM([name]), ' / ', [code]) Acme Ltd / 7 First characters LEFT(TRIM([name]), 4) Acme Pad with zeros LPAD([code], 5, '0') 7 becomes 00007 Replace text REPLACE([vendor], 'Acme', 'ACME Ltd') Remove non-letters regexp_replace([name], '[^A-Za-z]', '', 'g') Acme Ltd becomes AcmeLtd First non-empty value COALESCE([name], 'unknown') an empty name becomes unknown Text to number, safely TRY_CAST([amt] AS DOUBLE) "75" becomes 75.0, "x" becomes empty Number with thousands comma TRY_CAST(REPLACE([amt], ',', '') AS DOUBLE) "1,200.50" becomes 1200.5 Text to date TRY_CAST([posted] AS DATE) "2024-01-31" becomes a date, "bad" becomes empty Date as text strftime(TRY_CAST([posted] AS DATE), '%Y-%m') 2024-01 Days between dates date_diff('day', TRY_CAST([posted] AS DATE), DATE '2024-03-01') 30 for 31 Jan Rounding ROUND(TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) * 1.1, 1) 120.50 becomes 132.6 Parse a non-ISO date strptime([date], '%d/%m/%Y')::DATE 31/12/2024 becomes a date Category CASE WHEN TRY_CAST([v] AS DOUBLE) >= 400 THEN 'Large' WHEN TRY_CAST([v] AS DOUBLE) IS NULL THEN 'Unreadable' ELSE 'Small' END Simple if IF(TRY_CAST([amt] AS DOUBLE) IS NULL, 'check', 'ok') Case-insensitive match [name] ILIKE '%acme%' true, false or empty Month number month([d]) for a date column d Text length LENGTH([vendor])

items.title: The type pitfall: CSV columns arrive as text
items.text:
A column read from CSV is text even when it looks like 120.50. DuckDB does not guess:

  • [order_value] + 1 fails: No function matches the given name and argument types '+(VARCHAR, INTEGER_LITERAL)'.
  • [order_value] > 200 in a Filter fails: Cannot compare values of type VARCHAR and type INTEGER_LITERAL - an explicit cast is required.

Use TRY_CAST:

TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) > 200

TRY_CAST returns empty for a value it cannot read (such as abc) instead of stopping the node. Plain CAST stops at the first bad value, which may only happen on Run if the bad value is beyond the 100-row preview (see Preview uses 100 rows). In a Filter, an empty result counts as "not true", so unreadable rows land on the F output where you can inspect them.

Or set the real type once with Select and avoid casts afterwards.

items.title: The read-only guard
items.text:
Expressions can only read the table that flows through the node. The text is checked first, then run in a locked engine with file and network access switched off. What is rejected:

What Example Code More than one statement (anything after a semicolon) [id] = 1; SELECT 2 TD-SHAPE-110 Only one statement is allowed A statement that is not a plain query (COPY, ATTACH, INSTALL, LOAD, PRAGMA, DESCRIBE, SHOW, EXPLAIN ...) COPY t TO 'x.csv' In an expression box these cannot start a statement, so they fail as a syntax error: TD-SHAPE-113 in Multi-Field Formula, TD-SHAPE-004 with the engine's message in Filter and Formula. TD-SHAPE-111 (Only SELECT queries are allowed) is the code when a whole query box holds such a statement, for example in the SQL Query node. After a semicolon they are TD-SHAPE-110. File, system and random functions: read_csv, read_parquet and every read_*, glob, *_scan, query, duckdb_*, pragma_*, current_setting, getenv, random, uuid, gen_random_uuid, setseed read_csv('x.csv'), random(), uuid() TD-SHAPE-112 This function is not allowed (files, system or random) Reading a file as a table ... FROM 'a.csv' TD-SHAPE-112 Reading files is not allowed Dollar-quoted text ($$...$$), E'...' strings, control characters TD-SHAPE-112 Text the engine cannot parse or run TD-SHAPE-113 in Multi-Field Formula; TD-SHAPE-004 with the engine's message in Filter and Formula Longer than 20,000 characters TD-SHAPE-114 The SQL is too long Running longer than 25 seconds TD-SHAPE-115 The query took too long Multi-Field Formula without {col} TD-SHAPE-120 The formula must contain

Why random() and uuid() are blocked: a workflow must give the same result every time it runs on the same data, which matters for audit evidence. For a reproducible random split use Split with a fixed seed, or the sampling node in Audit nodes.

A semicolon inside quoted text or a -- comment is fine: [note] LIKE '%;%'.

Typical fixes:

You see Do this explicit cast is required or No function matches ... VARCHAR Wrap the column in TRY_CAST(... AS DOUBLE) (or DATE, INTEGER). Referenced column "x" not found The name is misspelt, or the column does not exist at this point in the workflow. syntax error at or near ... Check brackets, quotes and commas. TD-SHAPE-112 Remove the file, system or random function.

items.title: Error codes at a glance
items.text:
When a Preparation node cannot finish, its message starts with a code. These are the codes and what to do:

Code Meaning What to do TD-SHAPE-001 A required setting is missing Fill in the missing setting TD-SHAPE-002 An output column name is empty, duplicated or already exists Choose a unique name TD-SHAPE-003 A selected column is not in the input any more Select the column again TD-SHAPE-004 A setting value is out of range or unknown. Filter and Formula also use it for SQL problems, with the engine's explanation Pick a value from the list or inside the range; fix the expression TD-SHAPE-005 A required input has no data Connect and fix the upstream node TD-SHAPE-040 The pattern is not a valid regular expression Escape special characters with a backslash TD-SHAPE-041 The pattern is too long Shorten the pattern TD-SHAPE-042 Find text is empty Type the text to find TD-SHAPE-043 Too many rules Remove rules or split them over two nodes TD-SHAPE-044 The column must be text Convert the column to text with a Select node TD-SHAPE-050 The column is not a date and not text Choose a date or text column TD-SHAPE-052 A holiday is not a YYYY-MM-DD date Type holidays as year-month-day TD-SHAPE-053 Working days must name at least one weekday Tick at least one weekday TD-SHAPE-101 The split pattern can match nothing Use \s+ not \s* TD-SHAPE-110 Only one statement is allowed Remove everything after the first statement TD-SHAPE-111 Only SELECT queries are allowed Write a read-only query; changing data or settings is not allowed TD-SHAPE-112 The SQL uses a function or file access that is not allowed Remove file-reading, system or random functions TD-SHAPE-113 The SQL could not be parsed or run Check the SQL syntax TD-SHAPE-114 The SQL is too long Shorten the SQL TD-SHAPE-115 The query took too long Simplify the query or filter the data first TD-SHAPE-120 The formula must use the column placeholder Write {col}, for example UPPER({col})

The codes TD-SHAPE-060 to -091 belong to the Join, Transform and Audit nodes and are described on their pages.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Summarises the table: one output row for each combination of the group columns, with counts, totals, averages and similar measures. (Saved workflows and older documents call this node GroupBy.)

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Total by vendor or month, transactions per user, the largest posting per account, the number of distinct approvers per supplier.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The detailed table Out The summary: group columns first, then one column per measure

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Control Default Effect Field picker (drop-down of the input columns) first column The column to add. Add field as group key or measure (plus icon) Adds the picked column to the table below as a group key. A column can be added only once; adding it again does nothing. Remove selected action (minus icon) Removes the selected row(s). Table column Field The input column (not editable). Table column Action GroupBy What to do with the column (list below). Table column Output Field Name the column name, or a prefix plus the name The name in the result. Double-click to rename. Changing the Action resets it to the default name. Action Meaning Default output name GroupBy Use as a group key same as the field Count Number of rows in the group Count_<field> Sum Total Sum_<field> Mean Average Avg_<field> Min / Max Smallest / largest Min_<field> / Max_<field> Std / Var Standard deviation / variance Std_<field> / Var_<field> Median Middle value Median_<field> First / Last First / last value in input order First_<field> / Last_<field> N_Unique Number of distinct values Unique_<field> List The values gathered into a list List_<field>

For a text column only GroupBy, Count, Min, Max, First, Last, N_Unique and List are offered. Sum, Mean, Std, Var and Median need a number column, so a CSV amount that arrived as text must be converted first (Select or Formula).

The dock chips show the number of keys and measures ("2 keys", "1 measure").

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

region rep amount N a 100 S b 50 N a 25 S c 75 N d (empty)

region = GroupBy, amount = Sum, rep = N_Unique:

region Sum_amount Unique_rep N 125 2 S 125 2

With no group key (only amount = Mean and rep = Count) the result is one row: Avg_amount = 62.5 (the empty value is ignored) and Count_rep = 5.

With group keys but no measure, the result has a count column holding the number of rows per group.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows: totals in the preview are totals of the sample.
  • One action per column. To get both the sum and the count of amount, use two Aggregate nodes, or copy the column with a Formula first.
  • Groups come out in order of first appearance, not sorted. Add a Sort after it.
  • Empty cells: Sum, Mean, Min and Max ignore them; Count counts every row of the group.
  • Empty group keys form a group of their own.
  • With no actions, or when none of the fields exist, the table passes through unchanged. A chip "n field(s) missing" warns about missing fields.
  • Output names must be unique and must not repeat a group column name (TD-SHAPE-002).

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-002 (duplicate output name: choose a unique name), TD-SHAPE-004 (unknown action), TD-SHAPE-005 (no input data).

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• To total only a subset, put a Filter in front.
  • Rename output columns to something a reader will understand before they reach a report.
  • Use List to see the values behind a total while you investigate, then remove it before exporting.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Removes empty rows and columns, fills empty cells with neutral defaults, and tidies text (spaces, letters, digits, punctuation, upper or lower case) in the columns you choose.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Right after reading a file with untidy text: stray spaces that stop two vendor names matching, empty cells that break arithmetic, mixed case.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table to clean Out The cleaned table (same columns, unless "Remove all-null columns" removes some)

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The node applies them in this order: remove nulls, replace nulls, whitespace, characters, case.

Section Control Default Effect Fields Clean (column checklist) none ticked The columns the text rules apply to (whitespace, characters, case) and "Remove rows null in selected". With nothing ticked the text rules do nothing, and a warning chip says so. The null replacement rules are not limited to these columns. Nulls Remove all-null rows off Deletes rows where every cell is empty. Nulls Remove rows null in selected off Deletes rows where any ticked Clean column is empty. Greyed out until you tick a column. Nulls Remove all-null columns off Deletes columns where every cell is empty. Nulls Replace null text with '' on Every empty cell in a text column becomes an empty text. Nulls Replace null numbers with 0 on Every empty cell in a number column becomes 0. Whitespace and characters Trim whitespace on Removes spaces at the start and end of the text in the ticked columns. Whitespace and characters Collapse inner spaces on Turns runs of spaces inside the text into one space. It does not trim the ends; that is Trim's job. Whitespace and characters Remove all whitespace off Deletes every space, tab and line break. Wins over collapsing. Whitespace and characters Remove letters off Deletes letters (Latin including accented letters, and basic Cyrillic). Whitespace and characters Remove numbers off Deletes digits. Whitespace and characters Remove punctuation off Deletes punctuation such as . , ; : ! ? - ( ). Case Case None None, Lower Case, Upper Case, or Title Case (first letter of each word upper, the rest lower).

With no column ticked under Clean, only the null rules run. Because the two null replacements are on by default, all empty text cells become blank text and all empty numbers become 0. Untick them if empty cells must stay empty.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

Name Amount Note alice smith 10 a1! BOB jones (empty) b2? (empty) 5 (empty) carol-ann 7 c3.

Settings: Clean = Name and Note; Remove punctuation on; Case = Title Case; everything else at its default.

Name Amount Note Alice Smith 10 A1 Bob Jones 0 B2 (empty text) 5 (empty text) Carolann 7 C3

A second run on the same input: Clean = Name, "Remove rows null in selected" on, both "Replace null ..." options off, other text rules at their defaults. The row where Name is empty is removed and the empty Amount stays empty:

Name Amount Note alice smith 10 a1! BOB jones (empty) b2? carol-ann 7 c3.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows.
  • Text rules only touch text columns. Ticking a number column under Clean does nothing for it.
  • "Replace null text" and "Replace null numbers" leave dates, yes/no columns and other types empty.
  • Removing punctuation also removes hyphens and apostrophes (carol-ann becomes carolann).
  • Title Case lowercases the rest of each word (BOB jones becomes Bob Jones).
  • An empty input returns an empty table.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-005 (no input data). Cleansing has no setting that can be invalid.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Put Cleansing before a Join or Unique: trimming and case-folding key columns prevents "Acme " and "ACME" counting as different.
  • Use Find and Replace for specific substitutions and Cleansing for general tidying.
  • To keep the original next to the cleaned text, use Find and Replace with "Keep original".

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
