items.text: Adds columns derived from dates: weekday, weekend and month-end flags, quarters and fiscal periods, the difference between two dates, adding days or working days, using your own working week and holidays.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Cut-off and timing tests: postings on weekends or public holidays, days from invoice to payment, working days to settle, fiscal quarter reporting.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table (dates may be real dates or text) Out The input columns plus one new column per calculation

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Control Default Effect Calendar Fiscal year starts January The first month of your fiscal year. Calendar Working days (seven buttons M T W T F S S) Monday to Friday The days that count as working days. At least one is required. Calculations Calculation list (each entry collapsible) none One entry per new column. The collapsed entry shows Calculation · Date -> Name. each entry Calculation Weekday name What to compute (table below). each entry Output name (placeholder "Auto") Auto The new column's name. Auto gives <date column>_<calculation>, or <date1>_to_<date2>_<calculation> for the two-date calculations. each entry Date empty The date column (real date or text). each entry Second date blank For the two-date calculations. each entry Days (-100,000 to 100,000) 0 For Add days and Add business days. each entry Days from column blank A column with the number of days per row; overrides Days when set. Advanced date handling (collapsed) Text dates Auto-detect How to read text dates: 2024-12-31, 31/12/2024, 12/31/2024, 31-Dec-2024, 20241231 or 31.12.2024. Advanced date handling Non-working day Forward When an Add business days start date is not a working day, move Forward to the next working day or Backward to the previous one first. Advanced date handling Holidays (text box, placeholder "2024-12-25 (one per line)") empty Holidays as YYYY-MM-DD, separated by new lines, spaces, commas or semicolons. They are skipped by the business-day calculations.

Only the fields a calculation uses are shown.

Calculation Result Weekday name Monday to Sunday (English) Weekday number 1 (Monday) to 7 (Sunday) Is weekend true when the day is not one of your Working days Is month end true on the last day of the month Quarter calendar quarter 1 to 4 Fiscal year the year in which the fiscal year ends. With an April start, 31 Jan 2024 and 2 Mar 2024 are fiscal year 2024 and 25 Dec 2024 is 2025. With a January start it is the calendar year. Fiscal period month number within the fiscal year (1 to 12) Fiscal quarter 1 to 4, counted from the fiscal start Days between Second date minus Date, in days (negative when the second date is earlier) Add days Date plus Days Add business days Date plus working days, respecting Working days and Holidays Is business day true when the date is a working day and not a holiday Business days between Working days from Date up to, but not including, Second date

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input (text dates):

inv_date due 2024-01-31 2024-02-15 2024-03-02 2024-03-01 2024-12-25 2025-01-10

Settings: fiscal year starts April; holiday 2024-12-25; calculations on inv_date: Weekday name, Is month end (named month_end), Fiscal year, Fiscal quarter, Fiscal period, Days between (second date due), Add business days (Days 3, named plus3bd), Is business day, Is weekend.

inv_date weekday name month_end fiscal year fiscal quarter fiscal period days between plus3bd is business day is weekend 2024-01-31 Wednesday true 2024 4 10 15 2024-02-05 true false 2024-03-02 Saturday false 2024 4 12 -1 2024-03-07 false true 2024-12-25 Wednesday false 2025 3 9 16 2024-12-31 false false

The real output also contains inv_date and due, and uses the Auto names such as inv_date_weekday_name and inv_date_to_due_days_between. Note that 25 December is a Wednesday, so "Is weekend" is false, yet "Is business day" is false because the date is in the Holidays list.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows. A chip "n unreadable dates in column (first 100 rows)" reports text that could not be read as a date in the sample.
  • Text that cannot be read as a date gives an empty result, not an error.
  • Auto-detect cannot know whether 03/04/2024 is 3 April or 4 March. When your text dates contain slashes, choose the exact layout under Text dates.
  • The date column must be a real date, a date-time or text; a number column gives TD-SHAPE-050.
  • A time of day on a date-time value is ignored; calculations use the date part.
  • New column names must be unique and must not already exist (TD-SHAPE-002).
  • With no calculations the table passes through unchanged.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: Code When Fix TD-SHAPE-001 A calculation has no date column (or no second date for a two-date one) Pick it TD-SHAPE-002 An output name is duplicated or already exists Give it a unique name TD-SHAPE-003 A chosen column is gone Pick it again TD-SHAPE-004 An unknown value (fiscal month, working day, roll direction, calculation) Pick from the lists TD-SHAPE-050 The column is neither a date nor text Choose a date or text column TD-SHAPE-052 A holiday is not YYYY-MM-DD (the detail quotes it) Type holidays as year-month-day TD-SHAPE-053 No working day ticked Tick at least one weekday

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Add "Is weekend" and "Is business day" columns, then use a Filter to list postings on non-working days.
  • Keep the holiday list in the workflow so the test is reproducible.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Splits a table into the rows that meet a condition and the rows that do not. Nothing is deleted: both groups come out, on two sockets.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Isolate high-value transactions, pull out one vendor, separate postings outside a date window, or list the rows that fail a rule.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text:
Socket Carries Input The table to filter T (true) Rows where the condition is true F (false) Every other row, including rows where the condition could not be decided (empty cells)

T and F together always contain every input row exactly once.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
A switch at the top picks the mode.

Control Default Effect Simple / Expression switch Simple Simple builds one condition on one column. Expression takes a SQL condition.

Simple mode

Control Default Effect Column "(select column)" The column to test. A saved column that is no longer in the input is shown as "name (missing)". Operation Equals The list depends on the column's type (below). Value empty (placeholder "Enter filter value...") The value to compare with. Max value empty (placeholder "Enter max value...") Shown only for In Between: the upper bound. Column type Operations offered Text Equals, Not Equals, Contains Number Equals, Not Equals, Less Than, Greater Than, Less Than or Equal, Greater Than or Equal, In Between Date or time (real dates, not text) the same list as numbers (see the edge cases) Other (for example yes/no) Equals, Not Equals

Expression mode

Control Default Effect SQL editor (placeholder: Filter rows with SQL, e.g.: / [order_value] in_between (0, 500) AND [status] = 'paid') empty A SQL condition; see Writing SQL expressions. Errors show under the editor as you type.

If the condition is empty (Simple mode: no column or no value; Expression mode: no text), every row goes to T and F is empty. A chip says "No condition: rows pass through" or "Incomplete condition: rows pass through".

Worked example (Simple). Input:

id status order_value region 1 paid 120 N 2 open 900 S 3 paid abc N 4 void 450 (empty)

Simple, Column = status, Operation = Equals, Value = paid. T holds rows 1 and 3, F holds rows 2 and 4.

Worked example (Expression). Same input:

TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) in_between (100, 500) AND [status] <> 'void'

T:

id status order_value region 1 paid 120 N

F holds rows 2, 3 and 4. Row 3 (abc) is on F because TRY_CAST made it empty, so the condition could not be true. Row 2 is outside 100 to 500; row 4 is void.

Writing [order_value] > 200 instead fails with Cannot compare values of type VARCHAR and type INTEGER_LITERAL - an explicit cast is required, because the column is text. See the type pitfall.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows; Run filters everything.
  • Empty cells: a comparison with an empty cell is neither true nor false, so those rows go to F. That includes "Not Equals" in Simple mode.
  • Simple mode, numbers: the Value must be a number, otherwise TD-SHAPE-004 ("Filter value must be a number"). In Between includes both ends, and if you type the bigger number first the two are swapped.
  • Simple mode, Contains on text is case-sensitive and the value is searched as plain text: . or ( mean just those characters. For a case-insensitive search use Expression mode: [name] ILIKE '%acme%'.
  • Simple mode on a real date, date-time or time column (not text): type the Value as 2024-01-31 (dates and date-times, optionally with a time such as 2024-01-31 13:30:00) or 13:30:00 (times). A date-only Value on a date-time column means midnight of that day. A Value that cannot be read gives TD-SHAPE-004 ("Filter value must be a date such as 2024-01-31"). For a date held as text, use Expression mode with TRY_CAST.
  • Simple mode tests one column. For several conditions use Expression with AND / OR, or chain two Filters.
  • Expression mode is protected by the read-only guard.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: Code When Fix TD-SHAPE-003 The Simple column is not in the input Pick the column again TD-SHAPE-004 The Value is not a number (or not a date or time on a date column); or the SQL engine rejected the condition (the text after the code is the engine's explanation, for example a missing column or "an explicit cast is required") Correct the value; use TRY_CAST TD-SHAPE-110, -112, -114, -115 The expression breaks the read-only guard Remove the offending part TD-SHAPE-005 No input data Fix the upstream node

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Use the F output as an exception list and connect it to a report.
  • in_between (a, b) works only in Filter. In a Formula write BETWEEN a AND b.
  • A Filter followed by Aggregate gives totals for just the rows you care about.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Applies an ordered list of find-and-replace rules to the text columns you pick, as plain text or as regular expressions.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Standardise names (Ltd. to Limited), strip prefixes, blank out placeholders such as N/A, fix a recurring typo across a column.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Out The same table with the replaced text (in place, or in new columns)

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Control Default Effect Columns Columns (picker) none The text columns to change. Hint: "Text columns only. A numeric column is rejected." Rules Rule (list, up to 50, each card collapsible) none One card per rule. The collapsed card shows a summary such as Find... -> Replace · literal. Rules Find empty The text (or pattern) to look for, up to 500 characters. Rules Replace empty The replacement. Empty deletes the found text. Rules Mode Literal Literal matches the text exactly as typed. Regex reads Find as a regular expression. Rules On on Untick to switch a rule off without deleting it. Rules Match case off Off means upper and lower case do not matter. Rules Whole cell off Replace only when the whole cell equals the Find text (or the whole cell matches the regular expression). Output Keep original and a suffix box (placeholder _clean) off Off: the columns are changed in place. On: the original stays and the result goes to a new column named <column><suffix>; an empty suffix becomes _clean.

A note says "Rules run top to bottom. Each rule sees the previous result." The node shows a chip such as "12 cells change (first 100 rows)" or "No cells change in the first 100 rows".

In Regex mode the replacement can use groups from the pattern as $1, $2, .... In Literal mode a $ in the replacement is just a dollar sign.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

memo amt Paid to ACME Ltd. 1 paid to acme ltd 2 N/A 3 Refund (ACME) 4

Columns = memo; Keep original on (suffix _clean); rule 1: Find N/A, Replace empty, Literal, Whole cell; rule 2: Find ^(?:Paid to|paid to), Replace empty, Regex.

memo amt memo_clean Paid to ACME Ltd. 1 ACME Ltd. paid to acme ltd 2 acme ltd N/A 3 (empty text) Refund (ACME) 4 Refund (ACME)

A single Literal rule with Find acme, Replace Acme Inc, Match case off, in place, changes every case variant: Paid to Acme Inc Ltd., paid to Acme Inc ltd, Refund (Acme Inc).

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows; the "cells change" chip counts the sample only.
  • Only text columns. Pick a number column and the node stops with TD-SHAPE-044; convert it with Select first.
  • Empty cells stay empty.
  • Only switched-on rules are checked. A switched-off rule may have an empty Find or an invalid pattern without stopping the node; the "Rule n" in a message counts all rules, on or off.
  • With no rule switched on, the table passes through unchanged (the columns are still checked).
  • Rules run in order, so a later rule can change what an earlier one produced.
  • A Regex Find that is not valid (for example an unclosed () stops the node with TD-SHAPE-040. Escape special characters with a backslash.
  • With Keep original on, the new column names must not already exist or repeat (TD-SHAPE-002).

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: Code When Fix TD-SHAPE-001 No column picked Pick at least one text column TD-SHAPE-002 A suffixed name already exists or repeats Change the suffix TD-SHAPE-003 A picked column is gone Pick it again TD-SHAPE-040 Invalid regular expression (the detail names the rule number) Escape special characters with a backslash TD-SHAPE-041 Find longer than 500 characters Shorten it TD-SHAPE-042 A switched-on rule has an empty Find Type the text, or remove the rule TD-SHAPE-043 More than 50 rules Remove rules or use two nodes TD-SHAPE-044 A picked column is not text Convert it to text with Select

items.title: Tips
items.text:
Turn Keep original on while you build the rules, compare the two columns, then switch it off when you are happy.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Formula reference
items.text:
Every SQL expression family the Formula, Multi-Field Formula and Filter nodes support, with working examples. For how to open the editor and add formula cards, see Formula. For the broader language rules, see SQL expressions.

New to formulas?

Start with Formula for a guided walkthrough, then use this page as a function lookup.

items.title: Column references
items.text:
Put a column name in square brackets: [Invoice Amount]. Spaces in names are fine. Case is ignored and spaces just inside the brackets are trimmed, so [invoice amount] and [ Invoice Amount ] both resolve to Invoice Amount.

[Amount] * 1.2
[First Name] || ' ' || [Last Name]

Unknown names are not columns: the engine reports Referenced column "x" not found.

items.title: Expression families
items.text:
ArithmeticConditional (CASE)String & textNumericDate & timeNull handlingType conversionComparison & booleanRegular expressionsMulti-section patterns

Standard operators. When a column comes from a CSV file it arrives as text; use TRY_CAST before doing maths on it.

Expression Result [price] + [tax] Sum [amount] - [discount] Difference [price] * [quantity] Product [total] / [count] Quotient [total] % [divisor] Remainder [total] // [divisor] Integer (floor) division

Examples:

[price] * [quantity]

([price] * [quantity]) - [discount]

TRY_CAST([amount_text] AS DOUBLE) * 1.1

Text columns

[order_value] + 1 fails when the column is text. Wrap it first: TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) + 1.

CASE WHEN … THEN … ELSE … END and the shorthand IF.

CASE
    WHEN [age] >= 65 THEN 'Senior'
    WHEN [age] >= 18 THEN 'Adult'
    ELSE 'Minor'
END

CASE
    WHEN [department] = 'Sales' AND [salary] > 75000 THEN 'Senior Sales'
    WHEN [department] = 'Engineering' AND [salary] > 90000 THEN 'Senior Engineer'
    ELSE 'Standard'
END

IF(TRY_CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE) IS NULL, 'check', 'ok')

Multi-section pattern: use an earlier section's output in a later one.

-- Section 1: target "amount_num"
TRY_CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE)

-- Section 2: target "size_band"  (references amount_num)
CASE
    WHEN [amount_num] >= 1000 THEN 'Large'
    WHEN [amount_num] IS NULL THEN 'Unreadable'
    ELSE 'Small'
END
Function What it does Example UPPER(x) Upper case UPPER([city]) → LONDON LOWER(x) Lower case LOWER([name]) → acme ltd TRIM(x) Remove leading/trailing spaces TRIM([name]) LTRIM(x) / RTRIM(x) Trim one side only LENGTH(x) Character count LENGTH([name]) LEFT(x, n) First n characters LEFT([code], 3) RIGHT(x, n) Last n characters RIGHT([ref], 4) SUBSTRING(x, start, len) Extract a slice SUBSTRING([code], 1, 3) LPAD(x, n, pad) Pad on the left LPAD([id], 6, '0') → 000042 RPAD(x, n, pad) Pad on the right REPLACE(x, from, to) Replace all occurrences REPLACE([name], '-', ' ') SPLIT_PART(x, delim, n) n-th token after splitting SPLIT_PART([email], '@', 2) CONCAT(a, b, …) Join strings CONCAT('INV-', [id]) a \|\| b Join strings (operator form) [first] \|\| ' ' \|\| [last] CONTAINS(x, sub) true if substring present CONTAINS([note], 'urgent') STARTS_WITH(x, prefix) true if starts with STARTS_WITH([code], 'A') 

UPPER(TRIM([name]))

[first_name] || ' ' || [last_name]

CONCAT('INV-', LPAD(CAST([id] AS VARCHAR), 5, '0'))

Function What it does ROUND(x, n) Round to n decimal places ABS(x) Absolute value CEIL(x) Round up to next integer FLOOR(x) Round down to next integer POWER(x, n) x to the power n SQRT(x) Square root MOD(x, y) Remainder of x ÷ y GREATEST(a, b, …) Largest of the values LEAST(a, b, …) Smallest of the values LOG(x) / LOG(base, x) Natural or base logarithm EXP(x) e raised to x SIGN(x) −1, 0 or 1 

ROUND(TRY_CAST([score] AS DOUBLE), 2)

ABS([variance])

GREATEST([q1], [q2], [q3], [q4])

Extracting parts:

Expression Returns YEAR([date_col]) Year as integer MONTH([date_col]) Month 1–12 DAY([date_col]) Day 1–31 HOUR([ts_col]) Hour 0–23 MINUTE([ts_col]) Minute 0–59 DAYOFWEEK([date_col]) 0 (Sun) – 6 (Sat) DAYNAME([date_col]) 'Monday' etc. QUARTER([date_col]) Quarter 1–4 EXTRACT(YEAR FROM [date_col]) Year (alternative form) DATE_PART('month', [date_col]) Month (alternative form)

Formatting:

STRFTIME([date_col], '%Y-%m')      -- "2024-01"
STRFTIME([date_col], '%d/%m/%Y')   -- "31/01/2024"

Truncating:

DATE_TRUNC('month', [ts_col])      -- first instant of the month
DATE_TRUNC('year',  [date_col])    -- 1 Jan of the year

Differences:

DATEDIFF('day',   [start_date], [end_date])
DATEDIFF('month', [start_date], [end_date])
DATEDIFF('year',  [start_date], [end_date])

Current values:

CURRENT_DATE          -- today as a date
CURRENT_TIMESTAMP     -- now as a timestamp

Parsing text into a date (when the column is text):

TRY_CAST([date_text] AS DATE)                -- ISO format: 2024-01-31
STRPTIME([date_text], '%d/%m/%Y')::DATE       -- non-ISO: 31/01/2024

Always cast text first

A column from a CSV is text even when it looks like 2024-01-31. Use TRY_CAST([col] AS DATE) before calling date functions.

Expression What it does COALESCE(a, b, …) First non-null value in the list NULLIF(x, val) Returns null when x equals val, otherwise x IFNULL(x, default) Returns default when x is null x IS NULL True when x is null x IS NOT NULL True when x is not null 

COALESCE([email], 'no-email@example.com')

COALESCE(TRY_CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE), 0)

NULLIF([status], 'unknown')

CASE WHEN [value] IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE [value] END

COALESCE([first_name], '') || ' ' || COALESCE([last_name], '')

Expression Converts to CAST([col] AS DOUBLE) Decimal number; fails on bad values TRY_CAST([col] AS DOUBLE) Decimal number; returns null on bad values CAST([col] AS INTEGER) Whole number TRY_CAST([col] AS INTEGER) Whole number, null on failure CAST([col] AS DATE) Date TRY_CAST([col] AS DATE) Date, null on failure CAST([col] AS TIMESTAMP) Date and time CAST([col] AS BOOLEAN) True / false CAST([col] AS VARCHAR) Text [col]::DATE Shorthand cast (DuckDB)

Common type names:

You mean Use Decimal / float DOUBLE or FLOAT Whole number INTEGER or BIGINT Text / string VARCHAR Date DATE Date and time TIMESTAMP Yes / no BOOLEAN

Prefer TRY_CAST

Use TRY_CAST whenever the data might be messy. Plain CAST stops the node at the first bad value; TRY_CAST returns an empty cell instead, so the run continues.

TRY_CAST([amount_text] AS DOUBLE)
TRY_CAST([date_str] AS DATE)
TRY_CAST(REPLACE([amt_comma], ',', '') AS DOUBLE)   -- "1,200.50" → 1200.5
Operator Meaning = Equal <> or != Not equal <, >, <=, >= Less / greater than x BETWEEN a AND b Inclusive range x IN ('a', 'b', 'c') Member of list x NOT IN (…) Not in list x LIKE 'A%' Pattern match (case-sensitive) x ILIKE '%acme%' Pattern match (case-insensitive) x NOT LIKE '%test%' Inverse pattern AND, OR, NOT Logical operators x IS NULL Null check 

[amount] > 1000 AND [status] = 'Paid'

[region] IN ('US', 'CA', 'MX')

[score] BETWEEN 80 AND 100

[name] ILIKE '%smith%'

NOT [is_deleted]

Comparing text with numbers

[order_value] > 200 fails when the column is text. Cast first: TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) > 200.

Function What it does REGEXP_MATCHES(x, pattern) True when the full string matches REGEXP_REPLACE(x, pattern, replacement) Replace all matches REGEXP_REPLACE(x, pattern, repl, 'g') Replace globally REGEXP_EXTRACT(x, pattern) First match of the full pattern REGEXP_EXTRACT(x, pattern, group) Capture group n REGEXP_EXTRACT_ALL(x, pattern) All matches as a list

Patterns use standard regular-expression syntax.

REGEXP_REPLACE([sku], '[^0-9]', '', 'g')      -- keep digits only

REGEXP_EXTRACT([path], '([^/]+)$')             -- last path segment

REGEXP_MATCHES([email], '^[^@]+@[^@]+\.[^@]+$')   -- basic email check

REGEXP_REPLACE([phone], '[^0-9+]', '')         -- strip non-numeric

Backslashes in patterns

In a DuckDB expression, write \\d to match a digit (the first \ escapes the second for SQL). Inside the formula editor this looks like '\\d+'.

A single Formula node can hold up to 5 sections, running top to bottom. Each section can reference columns created by earlier sections in the same node.

Pattern: parse then extract

-- Section 1: target "audit_date"
TRY_CAST([audit_date_text] AS DATE)

-- Section 2: target "audit_year"  (uses audit_date)
YEAR([audit_date])

-- Section 3: target "audit_month"  (uses audit_date)
MONTH([audit_date])

Pattern: clean then categorise

-- Section 1: target "amount_num"
TRY_CAST(REPLACE([amount], ',', '') AS DOUBLE)

-- Section 2: target "size_band"  (uses amount_num)
CASE
    WHEN [amount_num] >= 10000 THEN 'Large'
    WHEN [amount_num] >= 1000  THEN 'Medium'
    WHEN [amount_num] IS NULL  THEN 'Unreadable'
    ELSE 'Small'
END

Pattern: build an identifier

-- Section 1: target "vendor_clean"
UPPER(TRIM([vendor]))

-- Section 2: target "ref_code"  (uses vendor_clean)
[vendor_clean] || '-' || LPAD(CAST([id] AS VARCHAR), 6, '0')

items.title: Common pitfalls
items.text:
CAST on a bad value stops the whole node

CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE)   -- stops with TD-TYP-001 on the first non-numeric row
Fix: use TRY_CAST so bad values become empty instead: 
TRY_CAST([amount] AS DOUBLE)

Adding text with +

[first_name] + ' ' + [last_name]   -- No function matches '+(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)'
Fix: use || or CONCAT: 
[first_name] || ' ' || [last_name]
CONCAT([first_name], ' ', [last_name])

Using = to check for null

[status] = NULL   -- always false; = never matches null
Fix: use IS NULL: 
[status] IS NULL

Preview uses 100 rows

The editor evaluates your formula on the first 100 rows of preview data. A bad value that sits on row 10,000 will not appear until you Run. Use TRY_CAST to guard against late surprises.

Back to the Formula node · Preparation node index

items.title: Formula
items.text:
Adds calculated columns, or replaces the values of an existing column, using SQL expressions. One node holds up to five formulas; each can use the columns created by the ones above it.

Quick links

  • Formula reference: every function family with examples (arithmetic, string, date, regex, and more).
  • SQL expressions guide: column reference syntax, the CSV text pitfall, and the read-only guard.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Adds calculated columns, or replaces the values of an existing column, using SQL expressions. One node holds up to five formulas; each can use the columns created by the ones above it.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Convert text to numbers or dates, compute a total or variance, build a category, combine columns, flag exceptions.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table to add columns to Out The same rows with the new or changed columns

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The Config Dock shows one card per formula. The dock toolbar has an Add formula (plus) icon button and each card has a Remove formula icon button. A new node starts with one empty card.

Control Default Effect Target column (drop-down) "Select target column" Where the result goes. Choose an existing column to replace it, or + add column to create a new one (an "Add Column" box asks for the name). Columns made by earlier cards are listed too. Data type (drop-down) Auto Applied to the result with CAST, for a new column or for one that is replaced. Choices: Auto, String, Integer, Float, Boolean, Date, Datetime, Time, Categorical. Auto keeps whatever the SQL produces. If the target is a column of the input the box is greyed and shows that column's type. Categorical results are Categorical columns. Time results are kept as text (HH:MM:SS) because the app has no Time column type. Formula (SQL editor; placeholder Enter formula e.g.: / CASE WHEN [Age] > 30 THEN 'Adult' ELSE 'Young' END) empty A SQL expression; see Writing SQL expressions. Drag the grip under the editor to make it taller. A message under the editor explains any error. Card header arrow expanded Collapse a card.

A card counts only when it has both a target column and a formula. Cards without both are skipped; if none counts, the table passes through unchanged. Formulas run top to bottom, so a later card may use a column created by an earlier one.

When a formula replaces a column made by an earlier card, the Data type of the card is applied to the result. When it replaces a column of the input the box is greyed; use CAST in the formula to change that column's type. A node holds at most five cards; a saved workflow with more stops with TD-SHAPE-004 ("holds at most 5 formulas") instead of dropping the extra cards.

The dock chips show how many columns the input has and how many formulas are set, for example "2 of 3 formulas".

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input (all text):

id vendor order_value date 1 Acme 120.50 2024-01-31 2 Beta 900 2024-02-15 3 Acme abc 2024-03-01 4 Cole 450 2024-03-31

One formula: new column value_num, formula TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE).

id vendor order_value date value_num 1 Acme 120.50 2024-01-31 120.5 2 Beta 900 2024-02-15 900.0 3 Acme abc 2024-03-01 (empty) 4 Cole 450 2024-03-31 450.0

Two formulas in one node:

-- formula 1: new column "size"
CASE WHEN TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) >= 400 THEN 'Large'
     WHEN TRY_CAST([order_value] AS DOUBLE) IS NULL THEN 'Unreadable'
     ELSE 'Small' END
-- formula 2: existing column "vendor"
UPPER([vendor]) || '-' || CAST([id] AS VARCHAR)
id vendor order_value date size 1 ACME-1 120.50 2024-01-31 Small 2 BETA-2 900 2024-02-15 Large 3 ACME-3 abc 2024-03-01 Unreadable 4 COLE-4 450 2024-03-31 Large

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows.
  • While you type, Formula checks names and syntax against the columns. An error that depends on the values (for example text that cannot be converted for a real row) appears when you leave the node, from the first 100 rows.
  • At most five formulas per node (the add button stops at five); a file with more stops with TD-SHAPE-004. Chain two Formula nodes for more, or use Multi-Field Formula to apply one rule to many columns.
  • Results are stored as the app's standard types (whole numbers, decimals, text, dates, yes/no); unusual SQL result types are converted.
  • Empty cells: most functions return empty when an input is empty. Use COALESCE([x], 0) to substitute a value.
  • Failed conversions: TRY_CAST gives an empty cell; CAST stops the node with an error.
  • Each formula is one expression and is protected by the read-only guard.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text:
The text after the code starts with the formula number, for example Section 2: ....

Code When Fix TD-SHAPE-004 The SQL engine rejected the formula: a type mismatch (No function matches ... VARCHAR), an unknown column (Referenced column "x" not found), a syntax error Use TRY_CAST; check column names and brackets TD-SHAPE-110, -112, -114, -115 Breaks the read-only guard Remove the offending part TD-SHAPE-005 No input data Fix the upstream node

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Work in steps: one card cleans the text, the next converts it, the next calculates. The preview shows the result of each.
  • Name new columns clearly (amount_num, is_late) so later nodes and reports are readable.
  • Yes/no formulas such as [amount_num] > 1000 make good flag columns for a Filter.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Applies one SQL expression to many columns at once. You write the expression once, with {col} standing for "the current column", and the node repeats it for every column you tick.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Clean or convert a block of similar columns in one step: trim all text columns, convert twelve monthly amounts from text to numbers, upper-case several code columns.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Out The same rows, with the ticked columns replaced or new columns added

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Control Default Effect Columns Columns (checklist) none The columns the formula runs on, up to 200. Hint: "The formula runs once for each ticked column (up to 200)." Formula Formula (text box; placeholder UPPER(TRIM({col})) or TRY_CAST({col} AS DOUBLE)) empty One SQL expression. {col} is replaced by each column. {name} is replaced by that column's name as text. No semicolons. Output Result Replace the columns Replace the columns overwrites each ticked column. Add new columns keeps the originals and adds one result column per ticked column. Output New column suffix (only for Add new columns) _new Added to each name: net with _num gives net_num. Must not be empty.

The syntax is the same as in Writing SQL expressions, except that you write {col} rather than [column]. Each {col} is inserted safely quoted, so column names with spaces or quotes work.

The dock note reads: "Use {col} for the column and {name} for its name. One expression only: no semicolons." After editing, a chip reads "2 columns replaced" or "2 columns added".

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input (all text):

id net tax vendor 1 100.5 10 Acme 2 200 x Beta 3 abc 30 Acme

Columns net and tax; Formula TRY_CAST(TRIM({col}) AS DOUBLE); Result Add new columns; suffix _num:

id net tax vendor net_num tax_num 1 100.5 10 Acme 100.5 10.0 2 200 x Beta 200.0 (empty) 3 abc 30 Acme (empty) 30.0

With Result = Replace the columns, net and tax themselves become decimal numbers: net = 100.5, 200.0, empty and tax = 10.0, empty, 30.0.

Using {name}: Columns net and vendor; Formula {name} || ': ' || UPPER({col}); Add new columns with suffix _lbl. The new net_lbl column holds net: 100.5, net: 200, net: ABC and vendor_lbl holds vendor: ACME, vendor: BETA, vendor: ACME.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows.
  • Up to 200 columns per node. In Add new columns mode the new names (<column><suffix>) must not already exist (TD-SHAPE-002).
  • The formula is one expression. A semicolon, or brackets that do not balance, is rejected with TD-SHAPE-110. A trailing -- comment is safe.
  • Because the columns are usually text, put TRIM(...) and TRY_CAST(...) inside the formula.
  • The read-only guard checks the whole composed query: read_csv(...), random(), uuid() and similar give TD-SHAPE-112.
  • The result type follows the expression.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: Code When Fix TD-SHAPE-001 No column ticked, or Add new columns with an empty suffix Fill it in TD-SHAPE-002 A new column name already exists Change the suffix TD-SHAPE-003 A ticked column is gone Tick it again TD-SHAPE-004 More than 200 columns, or an unknown result mode Tick fewer columns TD-SHAPE-110 More than one expression, or a semicolon Write one expression TD-SHAPE-112 A function or file access the guard blocks Remove it TD-SHAPE-113 The SQL could not be parsed or run (the message gives the engine's reason) Check syntax and types TD-SHAPE-114, -115 Too long (over 20,000 characters) or too slow (over 25 seconds) Simplify TD-SHAPE-120 The formula has no {col} Write {col} where the column goes, for example UPPER({col})

items.title: Tips
items.text:
Test the formula on one column first, then tick the rest.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Tidies the column names, not the values: trims spaces, turns spaces into underscores or removes them, and changes case. (The palette entry is "Normalize Columns"; the node uses the Select icon.)

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Files from different systems name the same column differently (Net Amount, net amount, NET_AMOUNT). Normalize gives them one pattern so formulas and joins do not trip over stray spaces.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Out The same data with new column names

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Rules apply in the order trim, whitespace, case.

Section Control Default Effect Name rules Trim spaces on Removes spaces at the start and end of the name. Name rules Spaces to underscores on Each run of spaces inside the name becomes _. Name rules Remove all whitespace off Deletes spaces entirely. Wins over underscores. Name rules Case None None, Lower Case, Upper Case, Title Case (first letter of each word upper, the rest lower). Columns Normalize (checklist) none ticked The columns to rename. Empty means every column.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input columns: Customer ID, Order Date (spaces around it), Net Amount. Case = Lower Case.

Output columns: customer_id, order_date, net_amount.

With "Remove all whitespace" on and Title Case, Customer ID becomes Customerid and Order Date becomes Orderdate.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• If two names end up identical (Net Amount and net amount with Lower Case), the node stops with TD-SHAPE-002 and names the duplicate. Untick one of the columns or rename it first.
  • A rule never produces an empty name; the original name is kept.
  • Only names change; data and types are untouched. Check any Select or Formula that refers to the old names.
  • Normalize reads no row data, so the 100-row preview makes no difference.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-002 (the rules give a duplicate column name: tick fewer columns or change the rules), TD-SHAPE-005.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
Place it directly after the input node, before anything refers to column names.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Adds a column of whole numbers that numbers the rows (1, 2, 3, ...), optionally restarting for each group and ordered by other columns.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Give each row a stable reference for workpapers, number the lines within each invoice or journal, or rank rows inside a group.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Out The same rows, in the same order, plus the ID column

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Control Default Effect (top) Name (placeholder RecordID) RecordID Name of the new column; it must be new. Hint: "Dense Int64 numbers. The column name must be new." (top) Start at 1 First number (-1,000,000,000 to 1,000,000,000). (top) Position First First puts the column on the left, Last on the right. Grouping & order (collapsible) Groups none Numbering restarts at the start value for each combination of these columns. Grouping & order Order by (list) none Decides which rows get the smaller numbers; each entry has a Column and a Descending tick.

A note in the dock reads: "Rows keep input order. This only changes the numbers." Order by never reorders the table.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

inv dept amt A x 5 B y 9 C x 7 D x 1

Defaults add RecordID = 1, 2, 3, 4 on the left.

Name Seq, Start at 100, Position Last, Groups = dept, Order by amt Descending:

inv dept amt Seq A x 5 101 B y 9 100 C x 7 100 D x 1 102

In dept x the largest amount (C, 7) gets 100, then A (5) gets 101, then D (1) gets 102.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows: preview numbers cover the sample only. Without Groups and Order by, the number is simply the row position.
  • Rows tied on the Order by columns keep their input order. Empty values in an Order by column are numbered last.
  • Name must not be empty (TD-SHAPE-001) and must not already exist (TD-SHAPE-002).
  • Group and order columns must exist (TD-SHAPE-003).

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-001, TD-SHAPE-002, TD-SHAPE-003, TD-SHAPE-005.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
Record ID after a Sort gives a ranking; with Groups it gives a "line number within invoice".

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Generates a column of sequence values (numbers, dates or text) and places it next to the input table. In code and some older documents this node is called Dynamic Row Builder.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Add a simple counter, a series of dates, or a test column. To number the rows of a real table, Record ID is usually the better choice.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input A table (the node needs a connected input) Out The input columns plus the new column

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Control Default Effect Name counter Name of the generated column. Must not be empty. Type Int Int, Float, Text or Date/time. Changing the type converts the values where possible. Start 1 First value. Increment 1 The step. For Date/time it is a number of seconds. For Text it is the text appended at each step. End 10 Last value, included. Not shown for Text.

Starting values when you switch type: Int 1 / 1 / 10; Float 1.0 / 1.0 / 10.0; Text A / 1 / Z; Date/time 2024-01-01 00:00, 3600 seconds, 2024-01-02 00:00.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input of three rows (a = x, y, z). Name n, Type Int, Start 10, Increment 10, End 30:

a n x 10 y 20 z 30

With Type Date/time, Start 2024-01-01 00:00, Increment 86400, End 2024-01-03 00:00 the same three rows get 2024-01-01 00:00:00, 2024-01-02 00:00:00 and 2024-01-03 00:00:00.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• The number of generated values must equal the number of input rows. The new column is attached side by side with the input. With a different count the node stops with TD-SHAPE-130 ("The generated rows do not match the input rows"), which states both counts. Set Start, Increment and End so the count matches, and remember the live preview only sees the first 100 input rows.
  • At most 10,000 values are generated; the chip "Reached 10,000 rows" warns when the cap is hit (for example Increment 0).
  • Text type has no End: it keeps appending the Increment text (A, A1, A11, ...) up to the 10,000 cap, so it only fits an input of exactly 10,000 rows. Use Int, Float or Date/time in practice.
  • Int and Float stop when the value goes past End. If Start is already past End no values are produced.
  • Date/time values have no time zone.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-001 (empty name), TD-SHAPE-004 (unknown type), TD-SHAPE-005 (no input data), TD-SHAPE-130 (generated count differs from the input row count).

items.title: Tips
items.text:
Count the input rows first (an Aggregate with Count) before you set End.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Picks rows by position or rank: the first or last N, a range of row numbers, or the largest or smallest N by a column. What is not picked goes to the second output.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Top 10 payments, the 5 oldest entries per account, rows 200 to 300 of an extract.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table S (Selected) The chosen rows R (Remaining) Everything else

items.title: Settings
items.text:
One section, Mode. A note says "Only the fields used by the chosen mode appear below."

Control Default Shown for Effect Mode First always First, Last, Range, Large, Small. N 10 First, Last, Large, Small How many rows (1 to 100,000,000). From row / To row 1 and 100 Range 1-based, inclusive, counted across the whole table (From must not exceed To). Rank by blank Large, Small The column to rank. Text columns are read as numbers the way Audit reads amounts (1,234.50, 1.234,50 and 12,5 all work); unreadable values are never selected. A text column with no readable numbers gives TD-SHAPE-091. Ties Exact N Large, Small Exact N returns exactly N rows. Include ties also includes rows tied with the Nth. Per group none all except Range Selects within each group of the chosen columns. For Range a note says it is global and per-group does not apply.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

k v a 9 b 5 c 5 d 5 e 1

Mode Small, N 2, Rank by v, Ties = Exact N: S is e (1) and b (5); R is a, c, d. (The first of the tied 5s in input order wins.)

Same with Ties = Include ties: S is e, b, c, d; R is a.

On an invoice table (A/x/5, B/y/9, C/x/7, D/x/1): Mode Large, N 2, Rank by amt gives S = B (9) and C (7). Mode Last, N 1, Per group dept gives S = B (the last of y) and D (the last of x).

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows: "First 10" or "row 150" refer to positions in the sample while you edit; Run applies them to the whole table.
  • For Large and Small, S is ordered by the ranked value (largest first for Large, smallest first for Small). For First, Last and Range, S keeps input order.
  • Empty values in the Rank by column are never selected; they go to R.
  • Asking for more rows than exist returns all rows in S.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: Code When Fix TD-SHAPE-001 Large or Small without a Rank by column Pick the column TD-SHAPE-003 The Rank by or group column no longer exists Pick it again TD-SHAPE-004 N below 1, or Range with From above To Fix the numbers TD-SHAPE-005 No input data Fix the upstream node

items.title: Tips
items.text:
To get "the first 10 by date", Sort first: First and Last follow the current row order.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Chooses which columns to keep, in what order, under what name and with what data type. It is the main place to turn text columns into numbers and dates.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Right after reading a file: drop columns you do not need, give columns readable names, and set the type of each column so later nodes can calculate and sort correctly.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Out Only the ticked columns, in the dock's order, renamed and converted

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The Config Dock shows a toolbar above a table with one row per input column.

Toolbar, left to right:

Control Effect Search box ("Search columns...") Filters the list by name (after about 300 ms). All Ticks every column. None Unticks every column. Move column up / Move column down Moves the highlighted column in the order. Column options (menu icon) Opens the bulk menu (below).

Table columns:

Column Effect (checkbox) Tick to keep the column in the output. Column The input column name (not editable). Data Type String, Int64, Float64, Boolean, Date, Datetime, List, Struct, Categorical, Binary, Decimal or Duration. Defaults to the column's current type. Rename An optional new name. Leave blank to keep the name.

Right-clicking a row offers Select / Deselect Column, Rename Column, Move to Top, Move Up, Move Down, Move to Bottom, Clear Renames and Reset Types.

The Column options menu has: Check Selected, Uncheck Selected, Move to Top, Move to Bottom, Sort (Original Order, Name A-Z, Name Z-A, By Type), Bulk Rename (Add Prefix or Suffix to Selected or to All, Clear Renames), Bulk Data Type (Auto-Detect Types and Reset Types, each for Selected or All) and a checkbox Auto-add new columns. When that box is on (the default), columns that later appear upstream are included automatically.

If no usable column is ticked, the node passes the whole table through instead of returning nothing.

How types are converted. When the chosen Data Type differs from the current one, the values are converted and anything that cannot be converted becomes empty, without an error:

  • Text to Int64, Float64 or Decimal: unreadable text becomes empty.
  • Text to Boolean: true, 1, yes, y, t, on become true and false, 0, no, n, f, off become false (any case); other non-zero numbers are true, zero is false, anything else is empty.
  • Text to Date or Datetime: many layouts are understood (2024-01-31, 31/01/2024, 31.01.2024, 01/31/2024, 31-Jan-2024, 31 January 2024, with or without a time). When a value fits several layouts, the day-before-month layouts are tried first. Auto-Detect Types reads up to 1,000 values of each column and remembers the layout it found, so day and month are read consistently.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input (all text, as from a CSV):

inv_no amount posted internal 1001 120.50 31/01/2024 a 1002 900 15/02/2024 b 1003 abc x c

Settings: inv_no ticked, Int64, renamed Invoice; posted ticked, Date, renamed Posted on, layout day/month/year; amount ticked, Float64; internal unticked.

Invoice Posted on amount 1001 2024-01-31 120.5 1002 2024-02-15 900.0 1003 (empty) (empty)

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows: conversion problems later in the file show only on Run.
  • A failed conversion becomes an empty cell silently. After converting, look for new empty cells (for example a Filter with [amount] IS NULL) to find values that did not convert.
  • A column that disappeared upstream stays in the list flagged as missing until you remove it; it is skipped in the output.
  • Keep new names unique.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-005 (no input data). Other problems show the engine's message.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Make Select the first node after an input node and fix the types once; every later node benefits.
  • Use Auto-Detect Types (All) as a starting point, then check Date columns for day and month order.
  • Untick columns that hold personal data you do not need before building reports.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Orders the rows by one or more columns.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Put the biggest amounts first, order by date for a review, or sort before Select Records or a report.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Out The same rows in the new order

items.title: Settings
items.text:
One section, Sort, holding a list of sort keys (up to 10). The first key is the main one; later keys break ties.

Control Default Effect Column (per key) empty The column to sort by. Order (per key) Ascending Ascending or Descending.

Keys without a column are ignored. With no valid key the table passes through unchanged. A chip "n sort key(s) missing" warns when a chosen column is no longer in the input.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

region rep amount N a 100 S b 50 N a 25 S c 75 N d (empty)

Keys: region Ascending, then amount Descending.

region rep amount N d (empty) N a 100 N a 25 S c 75 S b 50

Empty values come first, in both ascending and descending sorts.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows: the preview order is the order of the sample only.
  • Text columns sort as text: "100" comes before "25". Convert amounts with Select first.
  • Rows with equal keys may keep any relative order; add another key if the order must be repeatable.
  • Maximum 10 keys.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-005 only.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
Sort after an Aggregate so the summary reads largest first.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Divides the rows into two groups by percentage: an Estimation group and a Validation group (the usual build and test split).

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Develop a rule on one part of the data and test it on the rest, or take a reproducible portion of a population.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table E (Estimation) The first part, sized by Estimation % V (Validation) The rest

items.title: Settings
items.text:
One section, Split. Its info line reads "Estimation rows first; the rest go to Validation."

Control Default Effect Method Random Random shuffles the rows first. Sequential keeps the input order. Estimation % 70 1 to 99: the share that goes to E. Random seed 42 0 to 2,147,483,647. Shown only for Random. The same seed on the same data always gives the same split.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Ten rows numbered 1 to 10, Estimation % = 70.

  • Sequential: E gets rows 1 to 7, V gets rows 8 to 10.
  • Random with seed 42: E gets rows 2, 1, 7, 3, 6, 4, 5 (in shuffled order) and V gets 10, 9, 8.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• The split point is "row position below (number of rows minus 1) times the percentage", so sizes are close to the percentage, not always exact. With 5 rows and 50 percent, 2 rows go to E and 3 to V. With a single row, E is empty and the row goes to V.
  • In Random mode rows come out in shuffled order, not input order.
  • Preview uses 100 rows: the preview splits the sample, Run splits the whole table, so the rows that land in E and V differ.
  • This is not a statistical sampler; for audit samples use the Sample test in Audit nodes.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-004 ("Estimation percent must be between 1 and 99"), TD-SHAPE-005.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
Record the seed with your workpapers so someone else can reproduce the split.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Splits one text column into several columns, or into several rows, at a delimiter or a pattern.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Split Surname, First name, a code-description field, account strings such as 100.200.300, or a cell holding several values separated by semicolons (one value per row).

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Out The table with the extra columns, or with more rows

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Section Control Default Effect Split Column empty The text column to split. Hint: "Text columns only." Split Split by Delimiter Delimiter is plain text. Regex is a regular expression that must match at least one character. Split Pattern (placeholder , or \t) , The separator. For a delimiter, \t, \n, \r and \\ are accepted. Output Output Columns Columns or Rows. Output Max splits 2 Columns: 1 to 49, and you get that number plus one columns, so 2 gives three columns and the last one receives whatever is left. Rows: 0 to 49, where 0 means no limit. Output Column names (placeholder a, b, c; Columns only) empty Comma-separated names. Missing names become <column>_1, <column>_2, .... Output Piece number (placeholder n; Rows only) empty Optional column holding the 1-based number of the piece within its cell. Options Trim spaces on Trims spaces around each piece. Options Keep original on Keeps the source column. In Rows mode the original text is kept in <column>_original. Options Skip empty (Rows only) off Drops pieces that are empty. A cell with no pieces left (empty or missing) still gives one empty row, so no record disappears.

In Rows mode the piece goes into the original column's name and all other columns repeat for each piece. A chip reads "n rows become m (first 100 rows)".

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

id full 1 Smith, John, Jr 2 Doe,Jane 3 Solo

Column full, Pattern ,, Output Columns, Max splits 2, Column names last, first, suffix:

id full last first suffix 1 Smith, John, Jr Smith John Jr 2 Doe,Jane Doe Jane (empty) 3 Solo Solo (empty) (empty)

Same data with Max splits 1, no names and Keep original off: the columns are full_1 and full_2; row 1 gives Smith and John, Jr (the remainder stays together).

Output Rows, Max splits 0, Piece number n, Keep original off:

id full n 1 Smith 1 1 John 2 1 Jr 3 2 Doe 1 2 Jane 2 3 Solo 1

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows; in Rows mode the row count after Run is much larger than in the preview.
  • Only text columns (TD-SHAPE-044). Convert numbers to text first.
  • Fewer pieces than columns leaves the extra columns empty; a cell without the delimiter ends up entirely in the first column.
  • If a new column name already exists, a number is added (name_2).
  • A regex that can match nothing, such as \s*, is rejected: use \s+ (TD-SHAPE-101).
  • A regex separator is replaced by a special marker character (U+241F) internally, so a cell that already contains that character would split there too. This is very rare.
  • Maximum 50 columns. An empty Pattern is an error.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: Code When Fix TD-SHAPE-001 No column picked, or the Pattern is empty Fill it in TD-SHAPE-003 The column is gone Pick it again TD-SHAPE-004 Max splits outside the range Change the number TD-SHAPE-040 Invalid regular expression Escape special characters TD-SHAPE-044 The column is not text Convert it with Select TD-SHAPE-101 The pattern can match nothing Use \s+ rather than \s*

items.title: Tips
items.text:
To split into rows and then total per piece, follow with an Aggregate.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Finds duplicates. One output keeps the first row of each distinct key; the other lists every row that belongs to a duplicated key.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Duplicate invoices, repeated payments, duplicate vendor records. The Duplicates output is your exception list.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input The table Unique The first row of each distinct combination of the chosen columns, in input order Duplicates Every row (including the first) whose combination appears more than once

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Control Default Effect Columns (checklist, section "Duplicate key") none ticked Rows that match on all ticked columns are duplicates.

With no column ticked all rows go to Unique and Duplicates is empty. The dock summary reads "n columns selected".

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input:

region rep amount N a 100 S b 50 N a 25 S c 75 N d (empty)

Columns = region and rep.

Unique:

region rep amount N a 100 S b 50 S c 75 N d (empty)

Duplicates:

region rep amount N a 100 N a 25

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Preview uses 100 rows: a duplicate whose second copy lies beyond row 100 does not appear in the preview.
  • Matching is exact: Acme, acme and Acme are different. Clean the key columns first (Cleansing).
  • Empty cells match each other: two rows with an empty key in the same position are duplicates.
  • Unique keeps the first occurrence in the input; sort first if you want the latest or largest.
  • Chosen columns that are no longer in the input are ignored.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: TD-SHAPE-005 only.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• To find duplicate invoices tick vendor, invoice number and amount.
  • For tolerance-based or near-duplicate tests see the Duplicates test in Audit nodes; use Unique for quick exact checks.

Back to the Preparation node index.

items.title: Report nodes
items.text:
Report nodes help you look at data and explain your work. They do not change your data: Graph and Data Profile pass the table through untouched, and Comment is a note that is not connected to anything.

If you want to... Use Draw a line, bar or scatter chart of a table Graph Check the quality of a table: nulls, distinct values, text that should be numbers, odd values Data Profile Leave a note for yourself or the reviewer on the canvas Comment

items.title: Nodes in this family
items.text:
• Graph

    Charts the incoming data in its own window after a successful Run; passes the data through unchanged.

  • Data Profile

    Profiles every column: empty cells, distinct values, ranges, common values and data-quality flags.

  • Comment

    A note on the canvas. It has no sockets and never runs.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: A Comment is a note on the canvas. It never runs, has no inputs or outputs, and has no effect on the data. Its text is saved with the workflow.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• Explain why a filter or a tolerance was chosen ("tolerance 0.50 agreed with client, see email of 3 March").
  • Mark a step as "to be reviewed", or leave a question for the reviewer.
  • Describe a group of nodes.
  • Explain the process in an Excel workpaper: every Comment on the canvas is copied word for word to the Workflow sheet of a workpaper.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: None. A Comment has no sockets, so it cannot be connected to other nodes. Its summary in the dock reads "0 inputs · 0 outputs · never runs".

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Control What it does Default Note (a large text box, placeholder "Note for the reviewer") The text of the comment, as many lines as you like. Tooltip: "The first line is shown above the node." Empty

The first non-blank line of the note, cut to its first 60 characters, is shown as a label above the node on the canvas, so the canvas stays readable. The rest of the text is only visible when you select the node.

Editing a Comment does not make the workflow re-evaluate and does not mark anything as out of date.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
You type:

Tolerance of 0.50 agreed with the client
Source: bank rec policy, section 4

The node shows Tolerance of 0.50 agreed with the client above it. Select the node to read both lines.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Label length. Only the first 60 characters of the first line are shown on the canvas. The note itself is not limited.
  • Empty note. No label is shown.
  • Running a workflow does nothing for a Comment: its generated code is only the line # Comment (not executed).
  • Privacy. The note is stored in the workflow file as plain text. Do not put confidential details in a workflow you will share outside the team.

items.title: Errors you may see
items.text: None. A Comment cannot fail.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Start the note with a short title on the first line; that line is what people see on the canvas.
  • Place one Comment above each group of nodes that does one job (for example "Step 2: match bank to ledger").

Back to the Report node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Data Profile describes every column of a table: how many values are empty, how many are distinct, the smallest and largest value, the most common values, whether a text column looks like numbers or dates, and a list of warning flags such as "mixed numbers and text" or "leading zeros". It passes the data through unchanged and also gives you the findings as a table.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• Straight after File Input, to learn what you have been given before you rely on it.
  • After cleaning, to confirm the cleaning worked.
  • To document the state of the data in the working paper (the profile can be exported).

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input (left) The table to profile. Output D Data. The input, unchanged. Output P Profile. One row per column of the input, with the figures described below.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The node's Config Dock shows the profile itself (a toolbar, a table of columns, and a detail panel for the selected column) with a collapsed Options section underneath.

Options (collapsed by default)

Control What it does Default Allowed values Sample Which rows a workflow Run profiles: All rows, First N rows, or Random N rows. Hint: "Which rows a workflow run profiles". All rows Rows (N) How many rows to profile when Sample is not All rows. 100,000 1,000 to 100,000,000 Seed Shown for Random N rows. The same seed picks the same random rows every run, so a reviewer can repeat your result. 42 0 to 2,147,483,647 Top values How many of the most common values to list per column. 5 1 to 50 Estimate over Above this many rows, distinct counts are estimated (within about 5%) to save time. Estimated counts are shown with a ~. 2,000,000 10,000 to 2,000,000,000 Chart bars Number of bars in the distribution chart of a number column. 20 5 to 100

A value outside its range, or an unknown Sample, is quietly brought back into range when the workflow is opened.

The profile view

Control What it does Filter columns (search box) Shows only the columns whose names contain the text. Open the full report (every column) in your browser (icon) Writes an HTML report of the profile and opens it in your browser. The temporary file is deleted when you close the app. Export profile (icon, menu) Copy to clipboard (tab-separated text), CSV file..., HTML report..., Excel workbook.... Recompute profile (icon) Profiles again. It discards the last Run's profile and re-profiles the rows the canvas holds (the first 100). Status chip Says which rows the figures describe: Data: 5 rows, Sample: first 100,000 rows, or Sample: random 100,000 rows (seed 42). Hover for whether it is a live preview or the result of a Run.

items.title: Reading the profile
items.text:
The table in the dock has six columns. Click a header to sort by it.

Column Meaning Column The column name. Type The type the column has now (for example String, Int64, Date). A CSV read by File Input is all String. Null % Share of values that are empty (null), with a small bar. Distinct How many different non-empty values (~ in front when estimated). Suggested The type the values look like, when it differs from the current type: for example Float64, or Date (99%) when 99% of the values read as dates. Flags Warnings and notes (below). Hover for the full list.

Select a row to see its detail panel: a bar chart (the distribution of a number column, or the frequency of the most common values), then figures such as Null, Blank text, Stray whitespace, Distinct, Min / max, Mean / median / std, Negative values, Zeros, Length, and Look like dates. For a text column that holds numbers, the figures are worked out from the text read as numbers and are labelled "(parsed from text)".

Suggested type is only offered when at least 98% of the non-blank values fit. It checks, in order: whole numbers, decimal numbers (amounts with a trailing minus, decimal commas and thousands separators count as number-like), true/false/yes/no/y/n, dates, then text. A column of whole numbers with leading zeros (007) is suggested to stay text, so the zeros are not lost. Recognised date forms are 2025-01-31, 31/01/2025, 01/31/2025, 2025/01/31, 31-01-2025, 31.01.2025, 20250131, 31-Jan-2025 and 31 Jan 2025, plus date-times such as 2025-01-31 14:30:00. A value such as 03/04/2025 can be read two ways, so check your dates.

Flags

Flag shown Meaning Tone all null Every value is empty. warning all blank Every non-empty value is only spaces. warning constant At least two rows, none empty, one distinct value. note almost all unique At least 20 values and 95% or more are different (typical for IDs). note mostly null 50% or more of the values are empty. warning mixed numbers and text A text column where between 2% and 98% of the values read as numbers. warning mixed dates and text A text column where half or more, but under 98%, read as dates. warning leading zeros Values such as 007 in a column that is mostly whole numbers. warning trailing minus Values such as 100- (a negative number written the old way). warning decimal comma More values use a decimal comma (12,50) than a decimal point. warning stray whitespace Values with spaces at the start or end. warning numbers stored as text A text column that is really numbers. note dates stored as text A text column that is really dates. note negative values A number column (or text that holds numbers) with negative values. note possible outlier At least 20 values, and the largest or smallest is 10 or more standard deviations from the mean. warning NaN values / infinite values Not-a-number or infinite values in a decimal column. warning

"Note" flags are normal for many files (every number in a CSV is "numbers stored as text"). "Warning" flags deserve a look and are drawn more strongly.

items.title: The profile table (output P)
items.text:
Output P has one row per input column and these columns, in this order. Empty cells are null.

Group Columns Identity column, position, dtype Emptiness row_count, null_count, null_pct, empty_count, empty_pct, blank_count, whitespace_count Distinct distinct_count, distinct_is_approx, distinct_pct Range min_value, max_value, min_length, max_length Numbers mean_value, median_value, std_value, sum_value, min_numeric, max_numeric, numeric_basis (native for number columns, parsed_text for text that holds numbers), negative_count, zero_count, nan_count, inf_count What text looks like numeric_like_count, integer_like_count, date_like_count, bool_like_count, leading_zero_count, trailing_minus_count, decimal_comma_count Common values top_values (JSON text of value and count pairs), top_value, top_count, histogram (JSON list of bar heights) Verdict suggested_type, suggested_confidence, flags (comma-separated internal names such as numeric_as_text,leading_zeros), sampled (true when only some rows were profiled)

Pass P to File Output, to a Filter (for example, keep rows whose flags contain mixed_numeric_text) or on to the working paper.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input (read from a CSV, so every column is text except Qty):

Invoice Amount Date Code Qty Status INV-001 100.50 2025-01-03 007 1 Open INV-002 2000 2025-01-04 012 2 Open INV-003 75.40 2025-01-05 003 -1 Open INV-004 310 2025-01-06 099 4 Open INV-005 (empty) 2025-01-07 010 4 Open

Output D is this table, unchanged. Output P (the main columns):

column dtype null_pct distinct_count min_value max_value suggested_type flags top_value Invoice String 0.0 5 INV-001 INV-005 String INV-001 Amount String 20.0 4 75.4 2000 Float64 numeric_as_text 100.50 Date String 0.0 5 2025-01-03 2025-01-07 Date date_as_text 2025-01-03 Code String 0.0 5 003 099 String leading_zeros 003 Qty Int64 0.0 4 -1 4 Int64 negative_values 4 Status String 0.0 1 Open Open String constant Open

How to read it: Amount is numbers stored as text, with the range 75.4 to 2000 (worked out from the text) and one empty value (20%); its mean is 621.475. Date is dates stored as text. Code has leading zeros, so convert it as text, not as a number. Qty has a negative value you may want to explain. Status is the same in every row.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Live preview vs Run. While you edit, the profile covers only the rows the canvas holds, the first 100, and the status chip says so ("Live preview of the rows the canvas holds (the first 100). Run the workflow to profile all rows."). After you press Run, the dock shows the full-data profile, labelled as the result of the run with its time, until you change a setting or press Recompute. The Sample settings only take effect in a Run. See Live preview and Run.
  • Wide tables. The live preview is skipped for tables with more than 150 columns (the dock says "N columns: the live preview is skipped so the editor stays responsive. Run the workflow to profile every column."). A Run profiles every column.
  • Large tables. There is no row limit. Distinct counts are estimated above the Estimate over threshold. Use First N rows or Random N rows to profile a sample of a very large table.
  • Random sample. The node counts the rows first, then picks N row positions. The same seed on the same data gives the same rows.
  • Long text. Minimum, maximum and common values longer than 100 characters are cut to 100 (ending with an ellipsis).
  • Nested columns (lists, records) and binary columns get only the empty count; no distinct count or common values.
  • Zero columns shows "No columns".
  • Stable numbers. Mean, median, standard deviation and sum are rounded to 12 significant digits so the same data gives the same profile on every run.
  • Empty versus blank. For text columns, "empty" means no text at all, "blank" means only spaces, and null means missing. They are counted separately.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text: Message Meaning and fix Profiling... The profile is being calculated. Live preview skipped The table has more than 150 columns. Run the workflow instead. Profile failed: ... The profile could not be calculated; the reason follows. Check the upstream node. Nothing to copy yet / Nothing to export yet / Nothing to show yet There is no profile to copy or export yet. Copied N rows / Exported N rows to CSV / Exported N rows to Excel / Exported HTML report The action finished. Export failed: ... The file could not be written (for example, it is open in another program), or, for Excel, the Excel writer is not installed ("Excel export is unavailable"). Close the file, choose another name, or export CSV or HTML. Could not write the report / Could not open the report The full report could not be created or opened in your browser. TD-SHAPE-005 The input has no data. Connect and fix the upstream node.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Put a Data Profile right after each File Input and look at Flags first. "Mixed numbers and text" and "leading zeros" are the two that most often change an audit result.
  • Compare profiles before and after a Cleansing or Select node to show that the cleaning did what you said.
  • Export the HTML report for the working paper. It lists every column.
  • For a repeatable result, use All rows, or Random N rows with a fixed seed, and note the seed.

Back to the Report node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Graph draws a chart of the table it receives, in its own window. It passes the table on unchanged, so you can put it in the middle of a workflow without disturbing anything.

items.title: When to use it
items.text:
• See how amounts change over time (a line chart of totals by month).
  • Compare groups (a bar chart of the amount per vendor).
  • Look for outliers and clusters (a scatter chart of amount against quantity).

It is for looking at data, not for producing a report file. The chart window lets you save a picture.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Socket Carries Input (left) The table to chart. Output Out (right) The same table, unchanged.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
The Config Dock has one section. The Show graph icon button sits on the top row of the dock.

Control What it does Default Show graph (icon button) Opens the chart in its own window. It is switched on only after a successful Run, with X and Y chosen. Its tooltip says why it is off: "Show graph (run the workflow first)" or "Show graph (no data to draw)". If the window is already open, it is brought to the front. Off until a Run Type Line, Bar or Scatter. Line Renderer The library that draws the chart: matplotlib or pyqtgraph. matplotlib uses its standard navigation toolbar; pyqtgraph replaces it with reset view and save PNG buttons. This only changes the look and the toolbar, never the data. matplotlib X column The column for the horizontal axis. The list shows (select column) until you pick one. Empty Y column The column for the vertical axis (the values). Empty Color by Splits the data into one coloured series per value of this column (for example one line per region). (none) turns it off. None Aggregate How to combine rows that share the same X (and colour): None, Sum, Count, Mean, Median, Min, Max. For a bar chart the default is Sum; for line and scatter it is None (one point per row). Depends on Type Title Optional chart title, also shown in the window title. Empty

Details:

  • A column you chose that later disappears from the input stays selected and is shown as name (missing). The chart then reports the problem instead of drawing.
  • The chart window follows your changes: edit a setting while it is open and the chart redraws after a short pause.
  • With Type Bar, Aggregate shows Sum, because that is what a bar chart does unless you say otherwise. Choose None to draw one bar per row.
  • After you reopen a saved workflow, the Show graph button is off again until you Run the workflow.
  • The window title reads "Graph", "Graph - your title", and adds the renderer name when it is not matplotlib.
  • Under the chart, a status line describes what is drawn, for example 3 points · sum of Sales per Month, 5 points · colored by Region, or 2,000 points shown (truncated).

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
A table of sales:

Month Region Sales Jan N 100 Jan S 50 Feb N 120 Feb S 70 Mar N 90

Bar chart, X = Month, Y = Sales, Aggregate = Sum (the default). The bars drawn are:

Month Bar height Feb 190 Jan 150 Mar 90

Status line: 3 points · sum of Sales per Month. Note the order: text X values are sorted alphabetically (Feb, Jan, Mar), not by calendar. Use a real date, or a number such as 202501, to get time order.

Aggregate = Mean gives Feb 95, Jan 75, Mar 90.

Line chart, X = Month, Y = Sales, Color by = Region. One line per region: Region: N with Feb 120, Jan 100, Mar 90, and Region: S with Feb 70 and Jan 50. Status line: 5 points · colored by Region.

Count. X = Region, Y = Month, Aggregate = Count draws a bar of 3 for N and 2 for S. Count works with any Y column; the other aggregates need a number.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Live preview vs Run. The chart is built from the table the node last received. While you edit upstream, that is the first 100 rows; after a Run it is the full result. The Show graph button only opens after a Run, so you normally see the full data. See Live preview and Run.
  • Points are capped at 2,000. With no aggregation, only 2,000 rows are drawn (for a line chart, the first 2,000 after sorting by X) and the status line says "(truncated)". With aggregation, the whole table is summarised first, and the number of distinct X groups is capped at 2,000. Summarise first (the Aggregate node in Preparation nodes) if you have more groups than that.
  • Order. Line charts sort by X (ties keep the input order). Aggregated charts also sort by X. A scatter or bar chart with Aggregate = None keeps the input order.
  • Nulls. A null X sorts last.
  • Aggregations need numbers (except Count). If Y is text you get the message below; convert it with a Select node.
  • Empty table. You get "No rows to plot."
  • Graph itself never writes a file. Only the save button in the chart window does, and only when you press it.

items.title: Messages you may see
items.text:
Graph does not raise TD- codes; the chart window and the status line describe the problem in plain words.

Message Meaning and fix No incoming data. Nothing is connected, or the upstream node has an error. Graph needs a table input. The input is not a table. Select an X column. / Select a Y column. Choose the columns in the dock. X column 'name' is not in the incoming data. (same for Y) The column was renamed or removed upstream. Pick it again. Y column 'name' must be numeric for sum. The chosen aggregation needs numbers. Convert the column, or choose Count. X and Y must differ to aggregate. Choose two different columns. Color by must differ from X and Y. Choose another column for colour. (A colour column that no longer exists is ignored.) No rows to plot. The table is empty after the settings are applied. No data to plot. Nothing could be drawn. Could not build the chart: ... The data could not be read; the message gives the reason.

items.title: Tips
items.text:
• Put a Graph after an Aggregate node so that you chart totals, not raw rows.
  • To check amounts for outliers, use Scatter with X = a number or date and Y = amount, with Aggregate = None.
  • A chart is a working-paper aid. For a number to quote, use a Data Profile or a summary table.

Back to the Report node index.

items.title: Transform nodes
items.text:
The Transform tab holds seven nodes that change the shape of a table: count it, add running totals, turn columns into rows (or rows into columns), compare each row with its neighbours, or rewrite the whole table with SQL. The other families are in the node index.

All seven icons are purple, the colour of the Transform family.

Arrange is not a node. You may see "Arrange" mentioned next to the Transform family in older notes. It is the canvas Arrange menu (align and distribute the nodes you selected), not something you put in a workflow.

items.title: Nodes in this family
items.text:
• Count

    Returns the number of rows as a one-row table.

  • Running Total

    Adds a cumulative sum column, optionally per group.

  • Transpose

    Turns chosen columns into Name and Value rows.

  • Pivot

    Turns the values of one column into columns and totals a value column in each.

  • Unpivot

    Stacks several columns into a name column and a value column.

  • Window

    Adds previous or next row, row number, rank, running and rolling figures.

  • SQL Query

    Runs one read-only SELECT over up to three tables (t1, t2, t3).

items.title: How these nodes behave
items.text:
A node runs when you leave its settings. Edits in the Config Dock are saved at once, but the Transform nodes recalculate only when you click another node, click the canvas, save or run. Until then the node shows a yellow "!" badge (tooltip "Changes pending - the node runs when you click away"). See Live preview versus Run.

The preview uses 100 rows. While you edit, each Transform node works on the first 100 rows of its input and shows at most 100 output rows. A Run uses every row. So a Count in the preview can only say "100", a Pivot may be missing a header that appears later in the file, and a running total only covers the sample. Check the full result after a Run: the Data Preview dock labels a table evaluated · not run (preview) or from Run.

Column types. A CSV or text file arrives with every column as text. Pivot, Window, Running Total and SQL Query can read text that holds numbers. Use a Select node to change a column's type.

Errors. A mistake in the settings turns the node red. The Logs dock shows a short message, a hint and a code. The codes you can meet in this family:
