Code Message What to do TD-SHAPE-001 A required setting is missing Fill it in (for example, the header column of a Pivot) TD-SHAPE-002 An output column name is empty, duplicated or already exists Choose a unique name TD-SHAPE-003 A selected column is not in the input any more Select the column again; it was renamed or removed upstream TD-SHAPE-004 A setting value is out of range or unknown Pick a value inside the range TD-SHAPE-005 A required input has no data Connect the input and fix the upstream node ("Input 1 has no data") TD-SHAPE-060 Index, header and value columns must be different Pick three different columns (Pivot); a column cannot be both kept and unpivoted (Unpivot) TD-SHAPE-061 Too many new columns The Pivot header has more than 500 distinct values; filter first TD-SHAPE-091 The column must be a number Pick a numeric column, or text that holds numbers (Window) TD-SHAPE-110 to -115 SQL guard messages See SQL Query

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Counts the rows of a table and returns the number as a one-row table.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: To reconcile record counts: "does the file have the 4,812 rows the system report says?" Put it after File Input, or after a Filter to count the matches. For a count per group (rows per vendor), use Aggregate in the Preparation family instead; Count has no grouping.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. One output, labelled Out, with a single column Count (a whole number).

items.title: Settings
items.text: None. The Config Dock only says "No configuration. The output socket carries the row count."

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Input of 5 rows (Account, Date, Amount):

Account Date Amount A 2025-01-01 100.0 A 2025-01-02 -30.0 B 2025-01-01 50.0 B 2025-01-03 25.0 B 2025-01-04 -75.0

Output:

Count 5

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• In the live preview the node counts only the sample and shows a warning chip, "First 100 rows only: full count at Run". Never quote the preview number. After a Run the count covers all rows.
  • An empty input gives Count 0, not an error.
  • An unconnected input gives TD-SHAPE-005.

items.title: Tip
items.text:
Connect Count to a File Output to keep the figure in your working papers.

Back to the Transform node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Turns the distinct values of one column into new columns, and summarises a value column in each. This is the Excel PivotTable layout: row labels down the side, headers across the top.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Amount by vendor and month; count of journals by user and posting period; a quick matrix of two categories.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input, one output (no letter): the Row labels columns, then one column per distinct header value.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Layout

Label Default Effect Row labels none Columns that become the rows (several allowed). With none chosen, the result is a single row. Headers none The column whose values become the new column names. Required. Values none The column that is summarised in each cell. Required.

Aggregation

Label Default Effect Function Sum How several rows in one cell are combined: Sum, Mean, Min, Max, Median, First, Last or Count. Empty cells Blank A cell with no data shows blank (Blank) or 0 (Zero).

Naming & limits (collapsed; open it to change)

Label Default Effect Blank header (blank) The column name used for rows whose header cell is empty.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Row labels Vendor, Headers Month, Values Amount, Function Sum. Amount arrives as text, as it does from a CSV:

Vendor Month Amount Acme Jan 100 Acme Feb 200 Acme Jan 50 Beta Jan 75 Beta Mar (empty) Vendor Feb Jan Mar Acme 200.0 150.0 Beta 75.0

With Empty cells = Zero, every blank cell becomes 0.0. With Function = Count, the result is Acme: Feb 1, Jan 2; Beta: Jan 1, Mar 0.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Columns are sorted by name, not by the order they appear (Feb, Jan, Mar above). Number the headers (01 Jan, 02 Feb) if you need calendar order, or reorder with Select afterwards.
  • Sum, Mean, Min, Max and Median read text as numbers the way Audit reads amounts (1,234.50, 1.234,50, 12,5 and (12.00) all work; text that is not a number is ignored). First, Last and Count work on any column and Count counts non-empty values.
  • When the value column is text and none of the first 100 rows can be read as a number, a warning chip says so.
  • A Sum of cells that are all empty is empty, not 0.
  • Count shows 0 for a header that exists for that row (a row with only empty values), and blank when no row has that combination. Choose Zero to show 0 everywhere.
  • Limit: 500 columns. More than 500 distinct header values stops the node with TD-SHAPE-061. Filter or group first.
  • Row labels, Headers and Values must be three different columns (TD-SHAPE-060). Headers and Values are required (TD-SHAPE-001).
  • Rows are sorted by the Row labels, empty labels last.
  • Pivot must see the data to know the headers. In the preview it sees only 100 rows, so some headers may be missing until you Run.

items.title: Tip
items.text:
To total by two keys across two headers (vendor by month by entity), add a Formula that joins them into one header column first.

Back to the Transform node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Adds a cumulative sum of one or more number columns, optionally restarting for each group.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: To build a running balance from a transaction list, or to see when a cumulative total crosses a threshold. For other running figures (minimum, maximum, average, rolling windows) use Window.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. One output, labelled Out: every input column in the same order, then one new column per chosen sum column.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
(section Running totals):

Label Default Effect Sum none chosen The columns to total: number columns and text columns (read as numbers, like Window; a value that is not a number becomes empty). Each one adds a column named RunTot_<column>. Group by none chosen The columns that define a group (account, branch). The total restarts at each new value. With none chosen, one total runs down the whole table.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Sum Amount, Group by Account, on the table above:

Account Date Amount RunTot_Amount A 2025-01-01 100.0 100.0 A 2025-01-02 -30.0 70.0 B 2025-01-01 50.0 50.0 B 2025-01-03 25.0 75.0 B 2025-01-04 -75.0 0.0

With no Group by, the last column reads 100, 70, 120, 145, 70.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Row order matters. The total accumulates in the order the rows arrive. Sort first (a Sort node) if you want it in date order. Rows are never reordered.
  • Text columns are read as numbers. A CSV arrives as text, so its columns are offered too. Amounts are read the way Audit reads them (1,000 is 1000, 1.234,50 and 12,5 use a decimal comma, (5) is -5), spaces are trimmed, and a value that is not a number stays empty in the new column (it is not an error). The result column is a decimal number. Columns that are neither numbers nor text (dates, yes/no) are not offered.
  • With no Sum column chosen, the node passes the table through unchanged (no error).
  • An empty cell stays empty in the new column and the total carries on past it (1, empty, 3 gives 1, empty, 4).

items.title: Tip
items.text:
The name is fixed (RunTot_<column>); rename it afterwards with Select.

Back to the Transform node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Runs one SQL SELECT over up to three tables and returns its result. It is the escape hatch for reshapes that the other nodes do not cover: joins with several conditions, subqueries, window functions, CASE logic, set operations.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: When you already think in SQL, or the same job would take five nodes. Prefer the dedicated nodes (Filter, Join, Aggregate) for simple steps: they are easier to review.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: Three inputs, top to bottom: t1 (required), t2 and t3 (optional). One output (no letter). Inside the query the connected inputs are the tables t1, t2 and t3, by position. The summary line in the dock reads "t1 required · t2, t3 optional".

items.title: Settings
items.text:
One section, Query:

Label Default Effect SQL SELECT * on the next line FROM t1 The query. The editor has syntax colours and completes the table and column names. An error line under the editor shows the first problem, found by checking the query against empty copies of your tables, without reading your data.

The note under the editor reads: "One read-only SELECT. Connected inputs are the tables t1, t2 and t3 (t2 and t3 are optional). Files and random functions are blocked."

What you can write. One statement that is a SELECT, WITH (common table expressions), FROM ... (DuckDB shorthand), VALUES or TABLE, or one wrapped in brackets. Inside it, anything DuckDB's SQL offers: joins, GROUP BY, CASE, window functions (OVER), subqueries, UNION, ORDER BY, LIMIT, USING SAMPLE, string, date and maths functions. A closing ; is fine and comments (--, /* */) are allowed. Names are not case-sensitive; put a column name that contains spaces in double quotes, for example "Posting Date". Only the SQL is checked, not your result: add ORDER BY if row order matters, because SQL does not promise an order without it.

What is rejected. Every query passes a guard before it runs, and again each time it runs. It rejects:

Code Message you will see Cause TD-SHAPE-001 SQL is empty Nothing in the editor TD-SHAPE-110 Only one statement is allowed A ; followed by a second statement TD-SHAPE-111 Only SELECT queries are allowed INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE, CREATE, DROP, PRAGMA, DESCRIBE, EXPLAIN, COPY, ATTACH, SET, INSTALL and the like TD-SHAPE-112 This function is not allowed (files, system or random) File readers (read_csv, read_parquet, any read_..., glob, any ..._scan, sniff_csv), system functions (duckdb_..., pragma_..., current_setting, getenv, query), and random ones (random, uuid, gen_random_uuid, setseed) TD-SHAPE-112 Reading files is not allowed FROM 'data.csv' or a table name that looks like a path TD-SHAPE-112 Dollar-quoted and escape strings are not allowed $$text$$ and E'text' strings; also control characters TD-SHAPE-113 SQL could not be parsed: ... or the engine's own message A typo, an unknown table or column (for example Table with name t2 does not exist! when t2 is not connected), a wrong function argument TD-SHAPE-114 SQL is longer than 20,000 characters Query too long TD-SHAPE-115 Query took longer than 25 s The query ran too long and was stopped; filter the data first or simplify the query

The query runs in a sealed, in-memory copy of the engine with no access to files or the network, on single-threaded settings and with a 2 GB memory limit. It can read only t1, t2 and t3 and cannot change anything on disk or your original data. An unconnected t1 gives TD-SHAPE-005 ("Input 1 has no data"). now() and similar clock functions are allowed, so a query that uses them can give different results each run.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
t1 is a payments list, t2 is a department list:

Vendor Amount Dept Acme 100 1 Acme 250.5 2 Beta 75 1 Dept DeptName 1 Sales 2 Ops 
SELECT d.DeptName,
       COUNT(*) AS n,
       SUM(TRY_CAST(t1.Amount AS DOUBLE)) AS total
FROM t1
JOIN t2 AS d ON t1.Dept = d.Dept
GROUP BY d.DeptName
ORDER BY d.DeptName
DeptName n total Ops 1 250.5 Sales 2 175.0

The text-column trap (TRY_CAST). A CSV arrives with every column as text, so Amount above is text.

  • SUM(Amount) on a text column fails with TD-SHAPE-113 ("No function matches the given name and argument types 'sum(VARCHAR)'. You might need to add explicit type casts"). Cast it first.
  • TRY_CAST(Amount AS DOUBLE) turns text into a number, and silently gives empty for anything it cannot read instead of an error. It reads 1250.50 and 42 but not 1,234.50, (500), $75, abc or an empty cell. In a test column of 1250.50, 1,234.50, (500), $75, abc, an empty cell and 42, SUM(TRY_CAST(Amount AS DOUBLE)) returns 1292.5, and only 2 of the 7 rows were readable: five were dropped without a message. Always compare COUNT(*) with COUNT(TRY_CAST(Amount AS DOUBLE)) to see how many were lost, or clean the column first with a Cleansing or Find and Replace node.
  • Cast to DOUBLE or DECIMAL(18,2), not INTEGER: TRY_CAST('250.5' AS INTEGER) is 251, a rounded figure.
  • Plain CAST(x AS DOUBLE) stops the whole query with TD-SHAPE-113 on the first unreadable value. Use it when you want to be told.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• In the live preview the query sees the first 100 rows of each table, so totals and counts are for the sample. Run the workflow for the real result. The sealed engine, the guard and the 25 s time limit apply to both.
  • The output column types are chosen by the query; unusual types are converted to the ones the rest of the app supports (text, whole numbers, decimals, true/false, dates).
  • If a query returns no rows, the node returns an empty table with the right columns.

items.title: Tip
items.text:
Start from SELECT * FROM t1, run it, then build up. The editor's error line catches typos before you click away. Keep the query short and put the business rule in a comment (-- exclude reversals): it is saved in the workflow and in the run record.

Back to the Transform node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Turns chosen columns into rows: every data column becomes a set of Name / Value rows, and the key columns repeat on each. (It does not flip the whole table; if you want one row per key and a column per value, use Pivot.)

items.title: When to use it
items.text: A trial balance or budget with one column per month (Jan, Feb, Mar) is hard to filter, chart or join. Transpose it into one row per branch and month.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input. One output, labelled Out: the key columns, then Name (the old column name) and Value.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
(section Transpose):

Label Default Effect Key columns none Columns that identify the row (branch, account). They are repeated on every output row. Data columns none The columns to turn into rows. With none chosen the table passes through unchanged. If columns are missing Warn and skip What to do when a chosen data column no longer exists. Warn and skip and Ignore both leave the missing column out of the result; Warn and skip also shows a "data column(s) missing" chip (and a "key column(s) missing" chip), Ignore shows no chip. Error stops the node with TD-SHAPE-003.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Key Branch, data Jan, Feb, Mar:

Branch Jan Feb Mar North 10 15 South 20 25 30

becomes

Branch Name Value North Jan 10 South Jan 20 North Feb 15 South Feb 25 North Mar (empty) South Mar 30

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Output is one block per data column, in the order you ticked them, and in input row order inside each block.
  • Empty cells are kept as empty Value rows. Filter them afterwards if you do not want them.
  • If the data columns have different types (numbers and text), Value becomes text.
  • If every data column is missing, the table passes through unchanged. Missing key columns only raise a chip (none under Ignore).

items.title: Tip
items.text:
Unpivot does the same job with more control (it names the two new columns and can drop empty values). Use Transpose for a quick reshape, Unpivot when you need the names.

Back to the Transform node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Stacks several columns into two: the name of the column and its value. It is the opposite of Pivot.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Data laid out as one column per month, per account or per test result, when you need one row per measurement to filter, aggregate, chart or join.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input, one output (no letter): the kept columns, then the name column, then the value column.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Shape

Label Default Effect Keep none Columns that identify the row and are repeated on every output row. Unpivot none The columns to stack. At least one is required (TD-SHAPE-001). A column cannot be in both lists (TD-SHAPE-060).

Output columns

Label Default Effect Name column Attribute Name of the new column holding the old column names. Value column Value Name of the new column holding the values. Drop empty values off Off keeps rows whose value is empty; on removes them.

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Keep Vendor, Unpivot Jan, Feb, Mar, Name column Month, Value column Amt, Drop empty values on:

Vendor Jan Feb Mar Acme 100 200 Beta 75 30 Vendor Month Amt Acme Jan 100 Acme Feb 200 Beta Jan 75 Beta Mar 30

With Drop empty values off, Acme/Mar and Beta/Feb are also there, with an empty Amt.

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• The two new names must be different, not empty, and not the same as a kept column (TD-SHAPE-002).
  • Rows stay grouped by input row (all of Acme's months, then Beta's), columns in the order you ticked them.
  • If the stacked columns have different types, they are converted to one: all numbers become decimals (100 becomes 100.0), anything else becomes text ("Mixed types are cast to text").
  • The output has (rows x stacked columns) rows. Stacking 12 columns of a 100,000-row file makes 1.2 million rows.

items.title: Tip
items.text:
After an Unpivot, an Aggregate by the name column gives you totals per old column.

Back to the Transform node index.

items.title: Purpose
items.text: Adds one new column per calculation that compares a row with the rows around it: the previous or next value, a row number, a rank, a running sum, minimum, maximum or mean, or a rolling sum over the last few rows. The rows stay in their input order.

items.title: When to use it
items.text: Days between one posting and the previous one (previous value, then the days between with a Date Helper); number the lines in each journal; rank invoices by amount within each vendor; detect a balance that jumps from the one before.

items.title: Inputs and outputs
items.text: One input, one output (no letter): every input column, then the new columns.

items.title: Settings
items.text:
Window

Label Default Effect Restart per none Columns that define a group. Every calculation starts again for each group. None means the whole table is one group. Order by none One or more rows of Column and Descending. This decides which row is "previous", "next", first or last. It does not reorder the output. With none, the input order is used.

Calculations (a list; add as many as you need; each card shows only the fields its calculation uses)

Label Default Effect Calculation Previous row (lag) One of the ten calculations below. Output name Auto Name of the new column. Leave empty to get the automatic name below. It must be different from every existing column (TD-SHAPE-002). Column none The column to calculate on. Not shown for Row number. Required (TD-SHAPE-001). Offset 1 Previous/Next row only: how many rows back or ahead (at least 1). Window rows 3 Rolling sum only: how many rows are summed (at least 1). Allow partial window off Rolling sum only: on gives a value for the first rows from the rows available; off leaves them empty until the window is full. Rank high to low off Rank and Dense rank only: on gives rank 1 to the largest. Nulls Skip Running sum, min, max, mean and rolling sum: Skip leaves an empty cell empty; Treat as 0 counts it as 0. Calculation New column What it holds Previous row (lag) <column>_lag<offset> The value from offset rows earlier in the group; empty for the first rows Next row (lead) <column>_lead<offset> The value from offset rows later Row number Row_Number 1, 2, 3 ... in order within the group Rank <column>_rank Rank; equal values share a rank and the next rank is skipped (1, 1, 3) Dense rank <column>_dense_rank As Rank without skipping (1, 1, 2) Running sum / min / max / mean <column>_cum_sum, _cum_min, _cum_max, _cum_mean The cumulative figure from the first row of the group to this row Rolling sum <column>_roll<window> The sum of the last window rows

items.title: Worked example
items.text:
Restart per Account, Order by Date (A to Z). Calculations: Row number; Previous row on Amount; Running sum on Amount; Rank on Amount with Rank high to low. Input (Amount arrives as text):

Account Date Amount A 2025-01-03 100 A 2025-01-01 40 A 2025-01-02 60 B 2025-01-01 25 B 2025-01-02 10 Account Date Amount Row_Number Amount_lag1 Amount_cum_sum Amount_rank A 2025-01-03 100 3 60 200.0 1 A 2025-01-01 40 1 40.0 3 A 2025-01-02 60 2 40 100.0 2 B 2025-01-01 25 1 25.0 1 B 2025-01-02 10 2 25 35.0 2

The rows are still in input order; the Date ordering decided that 2025-01-01 is the first row of account A. A Rolling sum over 2 rows with Allow partial window on adds Amount_roll2: 160, 40, 100 for account A and 25, 35 for account B. With it off, the first row of each account in date order is empty (for account A the column reads 160, empty, 100).

items.title: Edge cases and limits
items.text:
• Rank, Dense rank and the running and rolling calculations read text as numbers the way Audit reads amounts (1,234.50, 1.234,50 and 12,5 all work; other text becomes empty). Previous and Next work on any column and keep its type. Choosing a column that is neither text nor a number gives TD-SHAPE-091.
  • Every Order by row needs a column (TD-SHAPE-001); an offset or window below 1 gives TD-SHAPE-004.
  • Running mean divides by the number of non-empty values so far.
  • Text dates sort correctly only when written year-month-day (2025-01-03). 03/01/2025 sorts as text.
  • With no calculation in the list, the table passes through unchanged.

items.title: Tip
items.text:
Equal order keys keep input order, so the result is repeatable.

Back to the Transform node index.

items.title: Trigger Designer v0.1.0-alpha.1
items.text:
Alpha build

A first public build for testing. Expect rough edges. Please report what you find using the bug report template.

items.title: Download
items.text:
• TriggerDesigner-0.1.0a1-windows-portable.zip: the program for Windows 10 or 11, 64-bit.
  • SHA256SUMS.txt: checksums for the files above.

There is no installer and no Linux build in this alpha. Unzip the archive and run TriggerEditor.exe. The steps are on the install page.

Check the download with Get-FileHash and compare the result with SHA256SUMS.txt.

items.title: What is in this alpha
items.text:
• A node canvas for data checks: read, clean, join, transform, audit and write.
  • Audit nodes for duplicates, gaps, Benford's law, sampling and risk filters.
  • A run record for each Run, with a verify button and an HTML report.
  • Workpaper Output for a formatted Excel workpaper.
  • A command-line program, trigger-designer-cli, for unattended runs. It is not included in the portable zip; see the command line guide.
  • How-to posts: blog.

items.title: Known issues
items.text:
• Crash with code 0xC0000409. Under heavy workloads (large files, many nodes at once) the program can close without an error message. Windows records it as an application fault. Save often, and report the steps.
  • Windows shows a warning on first start. The alpha is not code-signed. Click More info, then Run anyway. See the install page.
  • No update check. The program does not contact the internet. Watch this releases page for new versions.
  • Settings and logs are per user. They live in %APPDATA%\Trigger Designer, not beside the portable exe.

items.title: Feedback
items.text: Report bugs through GitHub Issues. Security problems go through the private route in SECURITY.md. Response times are best effort: the maintainer is one person.
